qs.q: A bus driver has stopped upon encountering this sign. When is the driver permitted to continue?
o: After the cause of the danger has been removed.
qs.x: After stopping at the Danger sign, the driver may continue only after receiving permission.

qs.q: Is it permitted to cross this road marking?
o: Yes, when stopping on the shoulder or re-entering the carriageway from the shoulder, at places where stopping or parking is permitted.
qs.x: The edge line may be crossed when stopping on or leaving the shoulder where stopping or parking is allowed.

qs.q: A bus driver is leaving the enclosed courtyard of residential buildings where there is no 'Residential Zone' sign. Must the driver yield the right of way to vehicles travelling on the road?
o: No, because in the absence of a 'Residential Zone' sign, the road leading out of the area is considered to have equal priority.
qs.x: Leaving a courtyard with no Residential Zone sign, the driver must yield to vehicles on the road.

qs.q: Which of these road signs apply to public transport vehicles?
qs.x: No Parking, odd/even-day parking and No Stopping signs (1, 2, 3) apply to public transport; sign 4 concerns cars only.

qs.q: This sign does not apply to:
o: Public transport vehicles and taxis only.
qs.x: The mandatory straight-ahead sign does not apply only to public transport vehicles.

qs.q: Which of these signs does not apply to public transport vehicles?
qs.x: None of these three prohibitory signs applies to route public transport.

qs.q: Is it permitted to cross the solid line separating traffic flows and enter a lane for oncoming traffic?
o: Yes, on roads outside built-up areas, to turn left or make a U-turn.
Yes, but only on illuminated sections of road during daylight hours.
qs.x: Crossing the solid line between opposing traffic flows and entering the oncoming lane is prohibited.

qs.q: What does this road sign warn of?
o: Approaching a trolleybus and tram stop.
Approaching a dedicated lane for public buses.
qs.x: The sign shows a tram and warns of a crossing with tram tracks.

qs.q: In residential zones and courtyard areas, the following are prohibited:
o: Parking buses with their engines running.
qs.x: In residential zones and courtyards through bus traffic, parking with the engine running and driving instruction are all prohibited.

qs.q: Is this road marking used to indicate the boundaries of vehicle parking spaces?
qs.x: This marking is also used to mark the boundaries of parking spaces.

qs.q: What does this road marking indicate?
o: Lane boundaries at hazardous locations on the road.
The dividing lines between all lanes carrying traffic in the same direction.
qs.x: This marking shows lane boundaries at hazardous locations on the road.

qs.q: Which of these signs do not apply to public transport vehicles?
qs.x: None of these three signs exempts public transport; they apply to it as well.

qs.q: Which of these signs do not apply to public buses?
qs.x: None of these signs exempts public buses.

qs.q: Which of these signs apply to public transport vehicles?
qs.x: The No Parking sign (3) applies to public transport, whereas the turn and U-turn bans do not.

qs.q: What does this road marking indicate?
o: The boundary between lanes carrying traffic in opposite directions.
The edge of the carriageway and the central dividing strip.
qs.x: This marking shows the edge of the carriageway and the central dividing strip.

qs.q: What does this horizontal road marking separate?
o: The public transport lane from the other lanes of the carriageway.
Traffic flows in opposite directions on roads with four or more lanes.
qs.x: The double solid line (1.3) separates opposing traffic flows on roads with four or more lanes.

qs.q: What does this solid yellow road marking indicate?
o: The boundaries of special free parking spaces designated for electric vehicles and hybrid vehicles.
A location where both stopping and parking of vehicles are prohibited.
qs.x: The solid yellow line (1.4) marks the edge where both stopping and parking are prohibited.

qs.q: What does this road marking separate?
o: Traffic flows travelling in opposite directions on roads with two or three lanes (centre line); on roads with two or more lanes in the same direction, it indicates lane boundaries.
The carriageway of a one-way road from the shoulder.
qs.x: The broken line (1.5) is a centre line on two- or three-lane roads and marks lane boundaries where there are several lanes in one direction.

qs.q: What does this broken line, with dashes equal in length to the gaps between them, indicate?
o: The boundary between the main carriageway and an acceleration or deceleration lane.
qs.x: A line of short, equal dashes (1.7) shows the lanes within an intersection.

qs.q: What does the combination of a continuous line and a broken line indicate?
o: Places for U-turns, entrances to and exits from adjacent areas, and similar locations where crossing is permitted in only one direction.
A point where traffic flows travelling in different directions merge.
qs.x: The solid-plus-broken line (1.11) marks U-turn spots and entrances or exits of adjacent areas where crossing is allowed from one side only.

qs.q: Is it permitted to cross a combined continuous and broken line from the continuous-line side?
o: Yes, when completing an overtaking manoeuvre or passing an obstruction.
qs.x: From the solid-line side it may be crossed only when completing an overtaking or passing an obstruction.

qs.q: Within the area of effect of this sign, traffic is prohibited for buses whose:
o: Axle load exceeds the value indicated on the sign.
qs.x: The sign limits axle load (6 t), so it bans buses whose axle load exceeds the stated value, not total mass.

qs.q: Which of these signs do not apply to public transport buses?
qs.x: No Entry (1) and No Vehicles (2) do not apply to route public transport buses, while the height, length and distance signs do.

qs.q: Which of these signs do not apply to vehicles driven by persons with Group I or II disabilities or severe or profound functional limitations, or vehicles carrying such persons or children with disabilities?
qs.x: Signs 1 (No Vehicles) and 5 (No Motor Vehicles) do not apply to vehicles of disabled drivers or those carrying them.

qs.q: Under these signs, which vehicles are permitted to proceed straight ahead only?
qs.x: The mandatory arrow sign requires going straight only, and here it binds buses.

qs.q: Under these signs, which vehicle is prohibited from turning right?
qs.x: The straight-ahead sign bans a right turn for tourist buses, while route public buses are exempt.

qs.q: Is it permitted to cross a broken reversible lane marking when the reversible traffic signal is switched on?
o: Yes, from either side, if the line separates lanes of traffic travelling in the same direction.
qs.x: With the reversible signal on, the broken line may be crossed from either side if it separates lanes going the same way.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a passenger is defined as:
o: A person who is inside or on a vehicle, other than the driver or driving instructor.
A person who is inside or on a vehicle, or who is boarding or alighting from a vehicle, other than the driver or driving instructor.
qs.x: By law a passenger also includes a person boarding or exiting the vehicle, excluding the driver and the driving instructor.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the carriageway is defined as:
o: The part of a road intended for the movement of vehicles.
The part of a road intended for the movement of non-rail vehicles.
qs.x: A roadway is the road element intended for non-rail vehicles.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a driving licence for category D and subcategory D1 vehicles may be issued to persons who have reached the age of:
qs.x: A licence for category D and subcategory D1 can be issued from age 21.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', who is considered a pedestrian?
o: A person on the road outside a vehicle, excluding a person authorized to carry out roadworks who is performing such work in accordance with the law.
A person on the road outside a vehicle, including a person authorized to carry out roadworks who is performing such work in accordance with the law.
qs.x: A pedestrian is a person on the road outside a vehicle, except one authorized to work on the road and doing so.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', where must initial practical driving instruction take place?
o: On roads outside built-up areas, taking account of traffic volume.
On an enclosed training ground or driving practice track.
On any road (except motorways), taking account of traffic volume.
qs.x: Initial practical driving instruction takes place on a closed training area or driving range.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', is an exit from an adjacent area onto a road considered an intersection?
qs.x: An exit from an adjacent area onto a road is not considered an intersection.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', holders of driving licences for categories B, C and D may also drive vehicles with trailers if the trailer's maximum authorised mass does not exceed:
qs.x: With B, C or D licenses you may tow a trailer whose maximum authorized mass does not exceed 750 kg.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', which of the following is considered a compulsory stop?
o: An interruption of movement caused by the unexpected activation of a prohibitory traffic light signal.
An interruption of movement caused by a traffic jam.

Bringing a vehicle to a standstill due to danger arising from a vehicle malfunction, the physical and/or mental condition of the driver (or passenger), the load being carried, or another obstruction on the road.
qs.x: A forced stop covers all the listed cases: a sudden prohibitory signal, a traffic jam, a malfunction, or another obstruction.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what is considered insufficient visibility?
o: The distance at which the road is visible during darkness.
The distance at which the road is visible in built-up areas where the carriageway has no artificial lighting.
Road visibility and/or a visibility distance of up to 300 metres in fog, rain, snowfall and/or other weather conditions adverse to road traffic safety.
qs.x: Insufficient visibility means poor weather such as fog, rain or snow and/or visibility of up to 300 m.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what is considered stopping?
o: Intentionally bringing a vehicle to a standstill for up to five minutes, or for the time necessary for passengers to board or alight and/or for loading or unloading.
Bringing a vehicle to a standstill for more than five minutes when this is not connected with passengers boarding or alighting, or with loading or unloading.
qs.x: Stopping is a deliberate standstill of up to five minutes, or as long as boarding, alighting, loading or unloading takes.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what is considered a public service vehicle?
o: A vehicle operating on a fixed route with designated stops and carrying passengers and/or luggage (tram, trolleybus or bus).
A vehicle operating on a fixed route with designated stops and carrying passengers and/or luggage (tram, trolleybus or bus), as well as a passenger taxi.
qs.x: A public service vehicle is a tram, trolleybus or bus on a fixed route with stops; a taxi is not included.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what is considered a trailer (semi-trailer)?
o: Any motor vehicle being towed by means of a rigid towbar.
A vehicle without an engine, designed to be drawn by a motor vehicle and to travel as part of a vehicle combination (including a special-purpose trailer).
qs.x: A trailer is an engineless vehicle designed to travel as part of a combination with a motor vehicle.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', which side of the road is used for traffic in Armenia?
qs.x: Armenia has right-hand traffic.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what is considered parking?
o: Intentionally bringing a vehicle to a standstill for more than five minutes when this is not connected with passengers boarding or alighting, or with loading or unloading.

Intentionally bringing a vehicle to a standstill for more than five minutes, except when necessary to avoid a collision with another road user or an obstacle, for passengers to board or alight and/or for loading or unloading, or in other cases provided for by law.
qs.x: Parking is a deliberate standstill of over five minutes, excluding collision avoidance, boarding or loading and other cases set by law.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', at what age may persons conscripted into the Armed Forces or other troops of the Republic of Armenia be issued a driving licence for category D or subcategory D1 vehicles?
qs.x: Conscripts may receive a category D or D1 licence from age 19.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', within what period after purchasing a vehicle must it be presented for state registration at a registration and examination division of the Ministry of Internal Affairs?
qs.x: A newly acquired vehicle must be presented for state registration within 15 days.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', who is responsible for maintaining a vehicle used in road traffic in a roadworthy condition?
o: The organization that sold the vehicle.
The organization that carried out the vehicle's most recent annual technical inspection.
All of the persons and organizations listed above.
qs.x: The vehicle's owner or user is responsible for keeping it roadworthy.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what must a driver check before setting off?
o: That the braking and steering systems are in working order.
That the remaining tyre tread depth complies with the prescribed standards.
qs.x: Before setting off the driver must check both the brakes and steering and the tyre tread depth.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', to whom must a driver make their vehicle available to provide assistance?
o: To police officers for transporting people in need of emergency medical care to a medical facility.
To medical personnel travelling in the same direction to provide medical assistance (with the driver's consent).
qs.x: A driver must provide the vehicle both to police to transport someone needing urgent care and to medical staff going the same way, with consent.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what must a driver do if involved in a road traffic accident?
o: Switch on the hazard warning lights.
Do not move any objects connected with the accident.
Perform all of the above actions.
qs.x: After an accident the driver must stop at once, switch on the hazard lights and not move objects related to the accident, so all three.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', which documents must the driver of a motor vehicle carry?
o: A driving licence for the relevant vehicle category and the vehicle registration documents, or their digital versions when driving within the Republic of Armenia.
A power of attorney when driving a vehicle belonging to another person.
All of the documents listed above.
qs.x: The driver must carry the licence for the relevant category and the registration documents, or their digital versions.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what is considered a traffic lane?
o: A marked longitudinal strip of the carriageway wide enough for vehicles to travel in a single file.
A marked or unmarked longitudinal strip of the carriageway wide enough for vehicles to travel in a single file.
qs.x: A traffic lane is a marked or unmarked longitudinal strip of the carriageway wide enough for a single line of vehicles.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what is meant by the maximum permissible mass of a vehicle?
o: The mass of a fully equipped vehicle with its fuel and other fluids.
The mass of a fully equipped vehicle, with its fuel and other fluids, loaded with the driver, passengers and goods.
qs.x: Maximum permissible mass is that of the fully equipped vehicle loaded with driver, passengers and cargo.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', who is considered a traffic controller?
o: A person authorized to regulate road traffic who performs traffic control in accordance with the procedure prescribed by law.
Any road user (driver, passenger or pedestrian) who directs traffic when necessary.
qs.x: A traffic controller is a person authorised by law to regulate traffic, not any road user.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', is a person teaching someone to drive treated as a driver?
o: Yes, the instructor is treated as a driver.
No, the instructor is not treated as a driver.
qs.x: A driving instructor is treated as a driver.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what constitutes a dangerous traffic situation?
o: A situation arising from an act and/or omission of a road user that creates a real risk of a road traffic accident.
A situation arising from an act and/or omission of a road user and/or traffic controller that creates a real risk of a road traffic accident.
qs.x: A dangerous situation may result from the act or omission of a road user and/or a traffic controller.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what is considered the hours of darkness?
o: In autumn and winter, the period from 8:00 p.m. to 8:00 a.m.; in spring and summer, the period from 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m.
The period between the end of evening twilight and the beginning of morning twilight.
The period when there is no sunlight.
qs.x: The hours of darkness are the period between the end of evening twilight and the start of morning twilight.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what is considered a bus?
o: A motor vehicle with more than eight passenger seats, designed and equipped for the safe and comfortable carriage of passengers and luggage.
A motor vehicle with eight or more passenger seats, designed and equipped for the safe and comfortable carriage of passengers and luggage.
qs.x: A bus is a motor vehicle with more than eight passenger seats.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', which of the following persons are treated as pedestrians?
o: Persons with disabilities moving at walking speed in motorized wheelchairs.
Persons walking alongside and pushing a bicycle, moped or motorcycle.
qs.x: Both disabled people in motorised wheelchairs moving at walking pace and people pushing a bicycle, moped or motorcycle count as pedestrians.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', when does the right to drive a motor vehicle take effect?
o: Upon successfully passing the practical driving test at the registration and examination division of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
qs.x: The right to drive arises upon receiving the driver's license, not upon passing the exam.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', for how long is a national driving licence issued?
qs.x: A national driving licence is issued for 10 years.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', for how long is an international driving permit issued?
qs.x: An international driving permit is issued for 3 years.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', who may become a learner driver (except a learner driver of a category AM vehicle)?
o: A person who has reached the age of 15.
A person who has reached the age of 16.
A person who has reached the age of 17.
qs.x: A person may become a driver candidate (except for AM) from age 17.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what is considered stopping?
o: Bringing a vehicle to a standstill at a passenger's request.
Deliberately bringing a vehicle to a standstill for more than 5 minutes, where this is not connected with boarding or alighting of passengers or loading or unloading the vehicle.
Deliberately bringing a vehicle to a standstill for up to 5 minutes, or for the time necessary for passengers to board or alight and/or for the vehicle to be loaded or unloaded.
qs.x: Stopping is a deliberate halt of up to 5 minutes or as long as boarding or loading takes; beyond 5 minutes it is parking.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what is considered a public transport vehicle?
o: A vehicle operating on a set route with designated stops and carrying passengers and/or luggage (tram, trolleybus or bus), as well as a passenger car used as a taxi.
A vehicle operating on a set route with designated stops and carrying passengers and/or luggage (tram, trolleybus or bus).
A vehicle operating on a tourist route and carrying passengers and/or luggage.
qs.x: Public transport is a tram, trolleybus or bus on a fixed route with stops; taxis and tourist services do not count.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what is considered the maximum permissible mass of a vehicle?
o: The maximum mass of a fully equipped and fuelled vehicle.
The mass of a fully equipped and fuelled vehicle, including the driver, passengers and load, specified by the manufacturer as the maximum permissible mass.
The mass of a vehicle, including the driver, passengers and load, specified by the manufacturer as the maximum permissible mass.
qs.x: Maximum authorized mass is the manufacturer-set mass of a fully equipped, fueled vehicle loaded with driver, passengers and cargo.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', holders of driving licences for categories B, C and D and subcategories C1 and D1 may also drive vehicles of those categories with a trailer, provided the trailer's maximum permissible mass is:
qs.x: With those categories you may tow a trailer with a maximum authorized mass of 750 kg.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', what is considered a stopping place for public transport vehicles?
o: A place along a designated public transport route intended for passengers to board and alight and identified by the appropriate road signs.
A place along a designated public transport route intended for passengers to board and alight.
qs.x: A public transport stop is a boarding and alighting place equipped with the appropriate road signs.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', a driving licence for category D and subcategory D1 vehicles may be issued to persons who:
o: Hold a driving licence for category B or C or subcategory C1 vehicles and have reached the age of 21.
Hold a driving licence for category B or subcategory B1 vehicles and have reached the age of 18.
Hold a driving licence for categories A and B or subcategories A1 and B1 vehicles and have reached the age of 18.
Hold a driving licence for category B or C or subcategory C1 vehicles and have reached the age of 20.
qs.x: Category D or D1 requires a B, C or C1 licence and an age of 21.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', an international driving permit for categories D and DE and subcategories D1 and D1E may be issued to persons who have reached the age of:
qs.x: An international permit for D, DE, D1 and D1E is issued from age 21.

qs.q: When entering an asphalt-concrete surfaced road from an unpaved road, the asphalt-concrete surfaced road:
o: Must be regarded as the priority road.
Must be regarded as a road of equal priority.
qs.x: When entering a paved road from an unpaved road, the paved road is the priority road and you must yield.

qs.q: How many traffic lanes are there on this carriageway?
qs.x: The single solid line in the middle divides the roadway into two lanes, one for each direction.

qs.q: Is it permitted to drive along the centre of the carriageway when it has the width shown?
o: Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
qs.x: A 7 m carriageway has two lanes, so you must keep to the right side, not drive down the centre.

qs.q: Which of the following stationary objects is not considered an obstruction?
o: A broken-down or stationary passenger car.
A passenger car stopped because of traffic congestion.
qs.x: A car stopped in a traffic jam is part of the traffic flow, not an obstruction; road damage, a foreign object and a disabled car are.

qs.q: Are the pavement and the road shoulders considered parts of the road?
qs.x: A road includes the roadway, sidewalks, shoulders and medians, so both sidewalks and shoulders are part of the road.

qs.q: How many carriageways does this road have?
qs.x: The grassy median in the picture splits the road into two separate roadways.

qs.q: How many intersections are shown in the picture?
qs.x: The roads meet at a single place, so this is one intersection even though the crossing road has a median.

qs.q: How many carriageway intersections are there at this junction?
qs.x: The main road here has two separate carriageways, so the junction crosses two carriageways.

qs.q: How many traffic lanes does this road have?
qs.x: The road has two roadways, each with two lanes, for four traffic lanes in total.

qs.q: In which picture does the road have a central reservation?
o: Only in the picture on the right.
Only in the picture on the left.
qs.x: A central reservation can be structural (grass strip) or marked by lines (left picture), so both pictures have one.

qs.q: Yielding the right of way to other vehicles means that:
o: The driver must not continue or resume driving or carry out any manoeuvre if doing so could cause other drivers to change their direction or speed.
The driver must not continue or resume driving or carry out any manoeuvre if doing so could cause other drivers to change their direction or speed unexpectedly.
The driver must stop the vehicle unconditionally.
qs.x: Yielding means not continuing or starting a maneuver if it would force others to change direction or speed unexpectedly; stopping is not always required.

qs.q: Which picture shows an intersection?
o: Only the picture on the left.
Only the picture on the right.
qs.x: An intersection is where roads cross or join; the left picture shows roads joining, while the right is a plain straight section.

qs.q: How many carriageway intersections are there at this junction?
qs.x: The crossing road has a median, so our roadway crosses two roadways.

qs.q: Changing lanes means:
o: Leaving the traffic lane occupied by the vehicle while maintaining its original direction of travel.
Leaving the line of traffic occupied by the vehicle within a marked traffic lane while maintaining its original direction of travel.
qs.x: A lane change covers leaving the occupied lane and also leaving a row within a marked lane, keeping the original direction.

qs.q: A turn is defined as:
o: A manoeuvre performed to enter another road.
A manoeuvre performed to enter another road or an area adjacent to the road.
qs.x: A turn is a maneuver made to enter another road or an adjacent area from the road.

qs.q: A U-turn is defined as:
o: Driving a vehicle in the opposite direction.
A manoeuvre performed to reverse the direction of travel of a vehicle.
qs.x: A U-turn is a maneuver done to reverse the direction of travel, not just driving in the opposite direction.

qs.q: Passing is defined as:
o: Moving ahead of one or more moving vehicles without leaving the occupied traffic lane.
Moving ahead of one or more moving vehicles by leaving the occupied traffic lane.
qs.x: Passing without leaving the lane is advancing ahead of vehicles without leaving your lane; leaving the lane makes it overtaking.

qs.q: Moving off is defined as:
o: The moment a vehicle starts moving from a stopping or parking place, whether or not it involves changing to an adjacent traffic lane.
The moment a vehicle starts moving from a stopping or parking place, involving changing to an adjacent traffic lane.
qs.x: Starting to move is pulling away from a stop or parking spot, with or without moving into an adjacent lane.

qs.q: Manoeuvring is defined as:
o: Moving off (involving entry into an adjacent traffic lane), changing lanes, changing direction, stopping (involving a lane change), and reversing.
Moving off, changing lanes, changing direction, stopping, and reversing.
qs.x: Maneuvering includes starting to move (with entering an adjacent lane), changing lanes, changing direction, stopping with a lane change, and reversing.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Road Traffic Safety, a truck is defined as:
o: A motor vehicle designed and equipped for the carriage of goods.
A motor vehicle weighing more than 3.5 tonnes, designed and equipped for the carriage of goods.
qs.x: A truck is any motor vehicle designed to carry goods, regardless of weight.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Road Traffic Safety, a central reservation is defined as:
o: A structurally separated part of the road dividing adjacent carriageways, not intended for the movement or stopping of vehicles or pedestrians.
A part of the road separated structurally and/or by appropriate road markings, dividing adjacent carriageways and not intended for the movement or stopping of vehicles or pedestrians.
qs.x: A central reservation is separated structurally and/or by markings and is not meant for traffic or stopping.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Road Traffic Safety, a vehicle is defined as:
o: A device designed to carry persons, goods or equipment mounted on it along a road.
qs.x: A vehicle is any device designed to carry people, cargo or mounted equipment on a road, not just cars and motorcycles.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Road Traffic Safety, the following persons are treated as drivers:
o: A person driving pack and/or riding animals or livestock along a road.
A person driving pack and/or riding animals or livestock.
qs.x: A person driving pack or riding animals or livestock along a road is treated as a driver.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Road Traffic Safety, a pavement (sidewalk) is defined as:
o: A part of the road adjoining the carriageway and intended for pedestrian movement in accordance with the procedure established by law.
A part of the road separated from the carriageway by any means and intended for pedestrian movement in accordance with the procedure established by law.
qs.x: A sidewalk is a road element for pedestrians that may adjoin the roadway or be separated from it.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Road Traffic Safety, a motor vehicle is defined as:
o: A power-driven vehicle intended for carrying passengers or goods by road, or for towing a vehicle used to carry goods, excluding vehicles such as agricultural tractors for which carrying passengers or goods by road, or towing a vehicle used to carry goods, is only an ancillary function.

A power-driven vehicle intended for carrying passengers or goods by road, or for towing a vehicle used to carry goods, including vehicles such as agricultural tractors for which carrying passengers or goods by road, or towing a vehicle used to carry goods, is only an ancillary function.
qs.x: Agricultural tractors, for which carrying or towing is only a secondary function, are excluded from the definition of an automobile.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', is a driver holding driving licences for categories B and C and subcategory D1 permitted to drive a bus with 17 seats?
qs.x: A 17-seat bus needs category D; D1 only covers up to 16 seats.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia 'On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety', who is permitted to travel in a vehicle without wearing a seat belt?
o: A driver with a disability travelling outside a built-up area.
The driver of a vehicle with distinctive colour and graphic markings, travelling within a built-up area.
An emergency service officer travelling outside a built-up area.
qs.x: The driver of a vehicle with special colour-graphic markings may go unbelted inside a built-up area.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia “On Ensuring Road Traffic Safety”, what is a bus driver prohibited from doing while driving?
o: Wearing sunglasses in conditions of poor visibility.
Smoking or throwing objects or items out of the vehicle.
Listening to the radio or music at a low volume.
qs.x: A bus driver may not smoke or throw objects out of the vehicle.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, which category or subcategory of driving licence is required to transport nine people in a truck?
o: Category D or DE, or subcategory D1 or D1E.
Only category C or subcategory C1, since the vehicle is a truck.
qs.x: Carrying passengers at bus level requires category D, DE, D1 or D1E even in a truck.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, an electric vehicle is:
o: A motor vehicle propelled by one or more electric motors powered by an independent source of electricity (excluding trolleybuses and trams).
A motor vehicle propelled by one or more electric motors powered by an independent source of electricity (including trolleybuses and trams).
A vehicle equipped with both an electric motor and an internal combustion engine, which may operate simultaneously or in succession.
qs.x: An electric vehicle runs on electric motors from its own power source and excludes trolleybuses and trams.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, road traffic safety means:
o: The prevention of accidents through monitoring carried out by the relevant government bodies and technical equipment.
Strict compliance with road traffic rules by all drivers and pedestrians.
The state of protection of road users against road traffic accidents.
qs.x: Road traffic safety is the state of protection of road users from accidents.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a bus driver is prohibited from:
o: Opening the bus doors while the bus is moving.
Opening the bus doors while stopped if doing so would obstruct other road users.
qs.x: A bus driver may not open doors while moving, nor when stopped if it obstructs other road users.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, passengers waiting for public transport vehicles are permitted to wait:
o: At locations where visibility in both directions exceeds 100 metres.
On raised boarding platforms or, where none are provided, on pavements and road shoulders.
At all of the above locations.
qs.x: Passengers wait on raised boarding platforms or, if none, on pavements and shoulders.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, bus passengers are prohibited from:
o: Distracting the driver from controlling the vehicle.
Boarding or alighting from the pavement or shoulder side before the bus has stopped.
qs.x: Bus passengers may not distract the driver from driving.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, persons responsible for the operation of buses must:
o: Organise drivers' work and ensure compliance with working-time and rest-period requirements.
Investigate accidents, establish their causes and identify the person at fault.
qs.x: Those running buses must organise drivers' work and respect working and rest time rules.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, road traffic is defined as:
o: The system of social relations arising during the movement of people and/or the transport of goods on roads by means of vehicles.
The system of social relations arising during the movement of people and/or the transport of goods on roads, with or without vehicles.
A system of measures implemented by government bodies to ensure the safe movement of vehicles on roads.
qs.x: Road traffic is the system of social relations in moving people and goods on roads, with or without vehicles.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a pedestrian crossing is:
o: A section of road at an intersection, marked by road signs and/or road markings and designated for pedestrian movement in accordance with the law.
A designated section of the carriageway, marked by road signs and/or road markings and intended for pedestrian movement in accordance with the law.
qs.x: A pedestrian crossing is a section of the carriageway marked by signs and/or markings for pedestrians.

qs.q: What is meant by 'change of direction of travel'?
o: A manoeuvre made for the purpose of entering another road.
A manoeuvre made for the purpose of entering another road or adjacent area.
A change from the previously selected direction of travel (excluding reversing), made by turning or making a U-turn.
A change from the previously selected direction of travel (including reversing), made by turning or making a U-turn.
qs.x: Changing direction means altering the chosen direction by a turn or U-turn, excluding reversing.

qs.q: An 'organised convoy of vehicles' is:
o: A group of at least three motor vehicles travelling directly one behind another in the same lane with their lights continuously switched on, escorted at the front by a vehicle with blue and red flashing beacons switched on.

A group of at least two motor vehicles travelling directly one behind another in the same lane with their lights continuously switched on, escorted at both the front and rear by vehicles with blue and red flashing beacons switched on.
qs.x: An organised convoy is at least three motor vehicles in one lane with lights on, led by a vehicle with blue and red flashing beacons.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, technical means of traffic control include:
o: Road signs, traffic lights, safety barriers and road markings.
qs.x: Technical traffic-control means are road signs, traffic lights, barriers and markings.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, when is a driver prohibited from leaving the driver's position or leaving the vehicle unattended?
o: When the vehicle is parked on a slope and its wheels have not been turned towards the kerb.
If the driver has not taken all necessary measures to prevent the vehicle from moving on its own or being used in the driver's absence.
qs.x: A driver may not leave the vehicle unless every measure has been taken to prevent it moving on its own or being used in his absence.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, 'international traffic' means:
o: The movement within the Republic of Armenia of a vehicle registered in another country and present in Armenia continuously, or with breaks of no more than two months, for up to one year.
The movement of a vehicle bearing Armenian registration plates that transports goods or passengers to a foreign country.
qs.x: International traffic is a foreign-registered vehicle moving in Armenia for up to a year.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, is a driver with a category D licence permitted to drive a bus with more than eight passenger seats while towing a trailer whose maximum authorised mass does not exceed 750 kg?
qs.x: A category D driver may tow a trailer up to 750 kg with a bus.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a national driving licence of the Republic of Armenia authorising the holder to drive category D vehicles also authorises the holder to drive:
qs.x: A category D licence also covers subcategory D1 vehicles.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, who conducts the practical driving test for entitlement to drive a trolleybus?
o: The registration and examination divisions of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

Trolleybus operating organisations, in accordance with the procedure established by an order of the head of the government-authorised public administration body responsible for transport and communications.
qs.x: The practical trolleybus test is conducted by the organisations operating trolleybuses.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, is a holder of a subcategory D1 driving licence permitted to drive a bus with more than eight but no more than sixteen passenger seats, excluding the driver's seat?
qs.x: Subcategory D1 allows buses with more than 8 but no more than 16 seats besides the driver's.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, is a holder of a subcategory D1 driving licence permitted to drive a 15-seat bus towing a trailer with a maximum authorised mass of 800 kg?
o: Yes, provided the trailer is empty.
qs.x: With D1 the trailer's maximum mass may not exceed 750 kg, so an 800 kg trailer is not allowed, even empty.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The rear fog lamps are connected to the brake lights.
The engine coolant temperature gauge is not working.
qs.x: Rear fog lights wired to the brake lights prohibit operation; a faulty coolant temperature gauge is not on the prohibition list.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: Even one wheel fastening bolt or nut is missing.
Tyres with different tread patterns are fitted on the same axle.
qs.x: A single missing wheel-fastening bolt and tires with different tread patterns on one axle both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The seat head restraints provided for in the vehicle's design are missing.
New and retreaded tyres are fitted on the same axle.
qs.x: Missing head restraints and new plus retreaded tires on one axle both prohibit operation under the list.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The engine crankcase ventilation system is not airtight.
The engine fuel supply system is not leak-tight.
qs.x: A leak in the crankcase ventilation or in the fuel system each prohibits operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The engine crankcase ventilation system is not airtight.
Frost-resistant and non-frost-resistant tyres are fitted on the same axle.
qs.x: A leaking crankcase ventilation system and mixing winter and non-winter tires on one axle both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The windscreen washers provided for in the vehicle's design are not working.
The external noise emitted by the engine exceeds the limits established by the applicable standard.
qs.x: Non-working windshield washers and excessive engine noise both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The rear fog lamps are not connected to the brake lights.
The windscreen washers provided for in the vehicle's design are not working.
In all of the above cases.
qs.x: Of these, only non-working windshield washers prohibit operation; rear fog lights not tied to the brake lights is correct.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: Objects or equipment that could injure road users are fitted to the vehicle.
The audible warning device (horn) does not work.
qs.x: Installed objects that could injure road users and a non-working horn both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The seat belts provided for in the vehicle's design are not functioning.
Objects or equipment obstructing the driver's field of vision from the driver's seat are fitted to the vehicle.
qs.x: Non-working seat belts and objects blocking the driver's view both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: Changes (modifications) have been made to the vehicle's design without permission from the vehicle registration authority.
Front turn indicators emit yellow light.
qs.x: Unauthorized structural modifications prohibit operation, while yellow front turn signals are permitted.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: A motor vehicle used for practical driving instruction does not display the required identification sign.
The fuel gauge does not work.
qs.x: A training vehicle without its identification sign may not be operated; a broken fuel gauge is not on the prohibition list.

qs.q: The operation of a motorcycle is prohibited if:
o: The safety bars provided for in its design are missing.
The minimum remaining tyre tread depth is 1.6 mm.
qs.x: Missing safety bars prohibit operation, while 1.6 mm tread is acceptable for a motorcycle.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: Front turn indicators emit yellow light.
At least one wheel fastening bolt or nut is missing.
qs.x: Even one missing wheel-fastening bolt prohibits operation, while yellow front turn signals are normal.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: Front turn indicators emit amber light.
The towing coupling of the trailer is defective.
qs.x: A defective towing device prohibits operation, while amber front turn signals are allowed.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: White retro-reflective devices are fitted to the front of the vehicle.
The towing coupling of the trailer is defective.
qs.x: A defective towing device prohibits operation, while white front reflectors are normal.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The seat belts provided for in the vehicle's design are missing.
White reversing lights are fitted to the rear of the vehicle.
qs.x: Missing seat belts prohibit operation, while white reversing lamps at the rear are correct.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The driver's seat adjustment mechanism provided for in the vehicle's design does not work.
The interior lighting in the passenger compartment of a bus does not work.
qs.x: Both faults, the seat adjustment mechanism and the bus interior lighting, prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: Red retro-reflective devices are fitted to the rear of the vehicle.
The speedometer provided for in the vehicle's design does not work.
qs.x: A faulty speedometer bars operation, while red rear reflectors are required.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The engine is difficult to start.
A first-aid kit is missing from the bus.
qs.x: A missing first-aid kit on a bus prohibits operation; a hard-starting engine does not.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The warning triangle is missing from the bus.
White lights illuminating the registration plate are fitted to the rear of the vehicle.
qs.x: A missing warning triangle prohibits operation, whereas white plate lights are normal.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The hydraulic braking system is not leak-tight.
Rear turn indicators emit white light.
qs.x: A leaking hydraulic brake system and white rear turn signals (they must be amber or red) both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: Tyres of different constructions are fitted to the same axle.
The engine fuel supply system is not leak-tight.
qs.x: Tires of different construction on one axle and a leaking fuel system both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The audible warning device (horn) does not work.
The cooling system does not maintain a stable operating temperature for the engine.
qs.x: A non-working horn prohibits operation; the cooling system condition is not the listed prohibition here.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: Threaded connections in the steering system are not properly tightened or secured as specified.
Fire extinguishers are missing from the bus.
qs.x: Loose steering connections and missing fire extinguishers both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: There is movement in steering components or assemblies that is not provided for in the vehicle's design.
Front turn indicators emit white light.
qs.x: Unintended play in steering parts prohibits operation; this is the correct option.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The remaining tyre tread depth on the bus is 1.8 mm.
The hydraulic braking system is not leak-tight.
qs.x: A bus tread of 1.8 mm is below the 2 mm minimum, and a leaking hydraulic brake also bars operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The pressure gauge of the pneumatic braking system does not work.
The remaining tyre tread depth on the bus is 1.6 mm.
qs.x: A dead air-brake pressure gauge and a 1.6 mm bus tread (minimum 2 mm) both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The exterior lighting devices do not operate in the prescribed modes.
The remaining tyre tread depth on the bus is 0.8 mm.
qs.x: Malfunctioning exterior lights and a 0.8 mm tread both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The tyres have localized damage exposing the tyre cord.
qs.x: Local tyre damage exposing the cord prohibits operation; an engine running intermittently does not by itself.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The remaining tyre tread depth is 2.2 mm.
qs.x: A missing first-aid kit prohibits a bus; a 2.2 mm tread is above the 2 mm minimum.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The interior lighting of a passenger car does not work.
The interior lighting of a bus does not work.
qs.x: Faulty interior lighting prohibits a bus but not a passenger car.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The total steering free play of a bus built on a passenger-car chassis exceeds 10 degrees.
The mudguards and splash guards provided for in the vehicle’s design are missing.
qs.x: Steering play over 10 degrees on a car-based bus and missing mudguards both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The total steering free play of a bus built on a passenger-car chassis is 15 degrees.
The total steering free play of a bus is 15 degrees.
qs.x: A car-based bus is limited to 10 degrees of play, so 15 degrees bars it; for an ordinary bus 15 degrees is acceptable.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: White retro-reflective devices are fitted to the rear of the bus.
Red retro-reflective devices are fitted to the rear of the bus.
qs.x: White rear reflectors are prohibited because they must be red; red ones are fine.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The bus is equipped with at least two wheel chocks.
White retro-reflective devices are fitted to the rear of the bus.
qs.x: White rear reflectors bar operation, while two wheel chocks are the required minimum.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The emergency door-opening mechanisms do not work.
The front turn indicators emit red light.
qs.x: Faulty emergency door openers and red front turn indicators both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The stop-request signal does not work.
The rear turn indicators emit red light.
qs.x: A broken stop-request signal prohibits operation; red rear turn indicators are allowed.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The remaining tyre tread depth is 1.6 mm.
The engine coolant temperature gauge does not work.
qs.x: A 1.6 mm bus tread is below the 2 mm minimum; a dead coolant temperature gauge does not bar operation.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The remaining tyre tread depth is 2.5 mm.
The interior lighting in the passenger compartment does not work.
qs.x: Faulty cabin lighting prohibits a bus; a 2.5 mm tread is fine.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The emergency exits and their operating mechanisms do not work.
The stop-request signal does not work.
qs.x: Faulty emergency exits and a faulty stop-request signal both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The door-control mechanism does not work.
qs.x: A faulty door mechanism and a missing first-aid kit both bar a bus from operation.

qs.q: The operation of a bus with a maximum permissible mass exceeding 5 tonnes is prohibited if:
o: The reversing lights fitted to the rear emit red light.
qs.x: For a bus over 5 t, missing wheel chocks and red reversing lights (they must be white) both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The bus has only one fire extinguisher.
qs.x: A bus needs two fire extinguishers and a warning triangle, so both shortcomings bar operation.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The bus has only one wheel chock.
The bus has only one fire extinguisher.
qs.x: One wheel chock and one fire extinguisher are not enough for a bus, so both bar operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The body-door lock provided by the vehicle design does not work.
The cab-door lock provided by the vehicle design does not work.
qs.x: A non-working cargo-bed door latch or cab door latch each prohibits operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The rear turn indicators emit red light.
The rear underrun protection device provided by the vehicle design is missing.
qs.x: A missing rear protective device prohibits operation, while red rear turn signals are allowed.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The power steering system provided by the vehicle design is faulty or missing.
The car audio system is not functioning.
qs.x: A defective or missing power steering unit prohibits operation, while a broken car audio system does not.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The parking brake system cannot hold the vehicle stationary on a gradient specified by the applicable standard.
qs.x: A parking brake that cannot hold the vehicle on the specified slope and leaking transmission seals both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The spare-wheel carrier does not work.
The rear axle seals are leaking.
qs.x: A faulty spare-wheel holder and leaking rear-axle seals both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: There are visible tears in the webbing of the seat belts provided by the vehicle design.
The vehicle is not equipped with fog lamps.
qs.x: Visible tears in seat belt webbing prohibit operation, while lacking fog lamps does not.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The bonnet (hood) latch provided by the vehicle design does not work.
The rear side windows are curtained and the vehicle has two exterior rear-view mirrors.
qs.x: A non-working hood latch prohibits operation, while curtained rear side windows are fine if both side mirrors are present.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The rear side windows are curtained and the vehicle does not have two exterior rear-view mirrors.
The window heating and demisting devices provided by the vehicle design do not work.
qs.x: Curtained rear windows without side mirrors and non-working window heating and defogging both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The fuel tank cap provided by the vehicle design does not work.
The front side windows are curtained.
qs.x: A faulty fuel-tank cap and curtained front side windows each prohibit operation, so both apply.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The audible warning device (horn) does not work.
The windows provided by the vehicle design are missing.
qs.x: A non-working horn and missing design-provided windows each prohibit operation, so both apply.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: There are cracks in a wheel rim or wheel disc.
There is visible deformation of the shape or size of the wheel-rim mounting holes.
qs.x: Cracks in the rim or wheel disc and visibly deformed mounting holes each prohibit operation, so both apply.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The exterior lights and retro-reflectors are dirty.
The front and rear protective devices are dirty.
qs.x: Dirty exterior lights and reflectors reduce visibility and prohibit operation, whereas dirty protective devices do not.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The lamps or lenses of the lighting devices are missing.
Lenses or lamps unsuitable for the type of lighting device are being used.
qs.x: Missing lamps or lenses, and lamps or lenses not matching the type of light, each prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The exterior lights and retro-reflectors are dirty.
Exterior lighting devices from a vehicle of another make are fitted to a vehicle model that is no longer in production.
qs.x: Dirty lights and reflectors prohibit operation, but fitting another make's lights on a discontinued vehicle is allowed.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: Yellow retro-reflectors are fitted at the rear of the vehicle.
Yellow retro-reflectors are fitted at the front of the vehicle.
qs.x: Yellow reflectors are not allowed at the front (must be white) or at the rear (must be red).

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: A vehicle driven by a physician does not display the “Doctor” identification sign.
The fuel tank cap provided by the vehicle design does not work.
qs.x: A faulty fuel-tank cap prohibits operation; a missing Doctor sign does not.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: Tyres with different tread patterns are fitted on the same axle.
A “Children on Board” identification sign with a yellow retro-reflective background and red retro- reflective border is displayed at the front of the vehicle.
qs.x: Different tread patterns on one axle prohibit operation, but the Transportation of Children sign belongs at front and rear.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: Bulbs or lenses are missing from the external lights.
The engine coolant temperature gauge does not work.
qs.x: Missing bulbs or lenses on exterior lights prohibit operation; a broken temperature gauge does not.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The remaining tyre tread depth is 2.5 mm.
The external lights are fitted with lenses or bulbs that are not suitable for those lights.
qs.x: Lenses or bulbs unsuited to the lamp bar operation; a 2.5 mm tread is acceptable.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: White-light turn indicators are fitted at the rear.
Red-light turn indicators are fitted at the rear.
qs.x: Rear turn indicators must be amber or red, so white ones prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The tyres do not match the vehicle model in size or permitted load rating.
Red-light turn indicators are fitted at the front.
qs.x: Tyres of the wrong size or load rating and red front indicators both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: At least two wheel chocks are provided.
qs.x: A defective exhaust system prohibits operation; having two wheel chocks is correct.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The crankcase ventilation system is not airtight.
Red retroreflectors are fitted at the rear.
qs.x: A leaking crankcase ventilation system bars operation; red rear reflectors are required.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The emergency exits and their operating mechanisms do not function.
The remaining tyre tread depth is 2.2 mm.
qs.x: Non-working emergency exits prohibit operation; a 2.2 mm tread is permitted.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The door operating mechanism does not work.
Only one fire extinguisher is provided.
qs.x: A faulty door mechanism and only one fire extinguisher both bar the bus.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: Only one fire extinguisher is provided.
qs.x: A bus must carry two fire extinguishers, so having only one prohibits operation.

qs.q: The operation of a bus with a maximum permissible mass exceeding 5 tonnes is prohibited if:
o: Only one wheel chock is provided.
Only one fire extinguisher is provided.
qs.x: A bus over 5 t needs two chocks and two extinguishers, so one of either prohibits operation.

qs.q: The operation of a bus with a maximum permissible mass exceeding 5 tonnes is prohibited if:
o: Red reversing lights are fitted at the rear.
qs.x: For a bus over 5 t, missing wheel chocks and red reversing lights (they must be white) both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The total free play in the steering system of a bus with a maximum permissible mass exceeding 5 tonnes is 15 degrees.
The total free play in the steering system of a bus built on a passenger car chassis is 15 degrees.
qs.x: Car-based buses allow only 10 degrees of steering play, whereas a bus over 5 t may have 15.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The interior lighting in the passenger compartment does not work.
qs.x: Faulty cabin lighting prohibits operation; two wheel chocks are normal.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The warning triangle is missing from the bus.
The rear-wheel fastening bolts are securely tightened.
qs.x: A missing warning triangle prohibits operation; tightly fastened wheel bolts are correct.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The remaining tyre tread depth is 2.2 mm.
The hydraulic brake system is not airtight.
qs.x: A leaking hydraulic brake system bars operation; a 2.2 mm tread is acceptable.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: Modifications have been made to the bus's design without the permission of the vehicle registration authority.
The remaining tyre tread depth is 1.6 mm.
qs.x: Unauthorised design changes and a 1.6 mm tread (minimum 2 mm) both prohibit operation.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The dates of the last and next scheduled inspections are not marked on the exterior of the gas cylinders of a bus fitted with a gas-fuel system.
qs.x: Missing test dates on gas cylinders bar operation; an intermittently running engine alone does not.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The tyres show separation of the carcass plies.
The remaining tyre tread depth is 2.2 mm.
qs.x: Tyre carcass ply separation prohibits operation; a 2.2 mm tread is permitted.

qs.q: The operation of a vehicle is prohibited if:
o: The threaded connections of the steering system are not tightened or secured in the prescribed manner.
The threaded connections of the steering system are secured in the prescribed manner.
qs.x: Loose or unsecured steering threaded joints prohibit operation; properly secured ones are correct.

qs.q: According to the Road Traffic Rules, the operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The steering wheel is difficult to turn.
The driver cannot change direction even when travelling at the lowest speed.
The total free play in the steering system is 15 degrees.
qs.x: Operation is barred when the driver cannot change direction even at minimum speed; a stiff wheel or 15 degrees of play alone does not bar it.

qs.q: According to the Road Traffic Rules, the operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The brake pedal is difficult to depress.
The bus deviates sideways even slightly during braking.
The driver cannot stop the vehicle even when travelling at the lowest speed.
qs.x: Operation is barred if the vehicle cannot be stopped even at minimum speed, not for a stiff pedal or slight pull.

qs.q: The operation of a bus is prohibited if:
o: The remaining tyre tread depth is 2.2 mm.
The tyres show separation of the tread and sidewall layers.
qs.x: Separation of tread and sidewall layers prohibits operation; a 2.2 mm tread is acceptable.

qs.q: This sign applies:
o: From 15 November of the current year to 31 March of the following year.
When there is snow or black ice.
qs.x: The snow-chains sign applies when snow or ice is present, not on fixed dates.

qs.q: This sign applies to:
o: Only trucks and buses with a maximum authorised mass exceeding 3.5 tonnes.
qs.x: The sign applies only to trucks and buses over 3.5 t maximum mass.

qs.q: This road sign indicates:
qs.x: The blue sign shows a tyre wrapped in chains, meaning movement with snow chains.

qs.q: The area of effect of this sign extends:
o: To the end of the built-up area.
To the end of the section affected by snow or black ice.
To the 'End of snow chains requirement' sign.
qs.x: The sign remains in force until the 'End of snow chains requirement' sign.

qs.q: This road sign indicates:
o: A section of road with a pavement or footpath.
A section of road with a pedestrian crossing.
A section of road without a pavement or footpath.
qs.x: The red triangle shows a pedestrian walking over zebra stripes, so it warns of a pedestrian crossing.

qs.q: Which of these signs prohibits vehicles from travelling with a following distance shorter than that indicated on the sign?
qs.x: Sign 3, a red circle with two cars and 70 m, prohibits driving closer to the vehicle ahead than the stated distance.

qs.q: At what distance before a hazardous road section are these signs installed in built-up areas?
qs.x: Warning signs like these red triangles are placed 50–100 m before the hazard in built-up areas.

qs.q: This road sign:
o: Prohibits all motor vehicles except two-wheeled motorcycles without sidecars.
Prohibits all vehicles except wheeled tractors.
qs.x: The prohibition sign with a tractor bans tractors and self-propelled machinery.

qs.q: Which sign requires drivers to yield the right of way to oncoming vehicles entering or approaching a narrow section of road?
qs.x: Sign 3 shows a red oncoming arrow against our black arrow, requiring us to yield to oncoming traffic at the narrow section.

qs.q: Which sign warns of an approaching intersection of roads of equal priority?
qs.x: Sign 5, the X in a triangle, warns of an intersection of equal roads, whereas the others show a side road meeting the main road.

qs.q: Which sign is placed immediately before the intersection of carriageways?
qs.x: Priority-regulating signs are placed right before the crossing of roadways, and sign 2 is the one that fits.

qs.q: Which of the following signs gives a driver priority over oncoming vehicles?
qs.x: Sign 4 is a blue square with a large white up arrow and a small red down arrow: our direction has priority over oncoming traffic.

qs.q: What does the supplementary plate below the sign indicate?
o: The distance from the sign to the beginning of the first bend.
The distance from the first bend to the beginning of the second bend.
The length of the road section with dangerous bends.
qs.x: The 100 m plaque with arrows at both ends under the winding-road triangle shows the length of the hazardous section.

qs.q: Which of the following signs prohibits parking on even-numbered days of the month?
qs.x: Sign 5, the crossed blue disc with two vertical bars, prohibits parking on even dates, while sign 4 with one bar is for odd dates.

qs.q: This road sign:
o: Permits driving only at the indicated speed or higher.
Prohibits driving at a speed higher than that indicated on the sign.
Indicates the recommended speed for this section of road.
qs.x: A blue disc with a number is a minimum-speed sign: driving is allowed only at that speed or faster.

qs.q: Which of the following signs requires drivers to yield the right of way to oncoming vehicles?
qs.x: Sign 2, the red circle with a black and a red arrow, requires yielding to oncoming traffic at a narrow section.

qs.q: What is this sign called?
o: Advance indication of how to pass an obstruction.
Advance indication of a change to another carriageway.
Advance indication of a diversion into a lane for oncoming traffic.
qs.x: The yellow temporary sign with an arrow leading across to the other carriageway is the advance indication of changing to another roadway.

qs.q: Which of the following signs requires drivers to yield the right of way to vehicles travelling on the intersecting road?
qs.x: Sign 3, the inverted red-bordered triangle (Yield), requires giving way to traffic on the intersecting road.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to overtake within the area of effect of this road sign?
o: Permitted in all cases, provided the overtaking rules are observed.
Permitted if the speed of the vehicle being overtaken does not exceed 30 km/h.
qs.x: The sign (no overtaking for trucks) applies only to trucks, so a bus may overtake while following the normal rules.

qs.q: Which of the following signs requires vehicles to travel at the indicated speed (km/h) or higher?
qs.x: Sign 3, the blue disc with 50, is a minimum-speed sign, while sign 1 in a red ring is a maximum limit.

qs.q: Which of the following signs indicates a section of one-way road?
qs.x: Sign 3, a blue square with one large white arrow, marks a one-way road.

qs.q: What does the supplementary plate used with the main sign indicate?
o: The length of the narrow section of road.
The distance from the sign to the point where the restriction begins.
The distance to the point where the narrow section of road can be bypassed.
qs.x: The 300 m plaque under the width-limit sign shows the distance from the sign to where the restriction begins.

qs.q: This road sign warns that ahead there is:
o: A section of road leading to a water crossing without a bridge or ferry.
A section of road with a movable bridge over a waterway.
A section where the road leads to a riverbank or waterfront.
qs.x: The triangle shows a car at the edge of a quay above waves, warning that the road runs out onto a riverbank or shore.

qs.q: Which of the following indicates the area of effect of road signs prohibiting stopping and parking?
qs.x: The white plaque with an arrow and a distance in metres (plaque 4) shows the length of the zone where the stop and parking bans apply.

qs.q: Which of the following indicates the length of the hazardous road section to which a warning sign applies?
qs.x: Plaque 4, white with arrows at both ends and 100 m, gives the length of the hazardous stretch covered by the warning signs.

qs.q: Which of the following signs indicates a hotel or motel?
qs.x: Sign 3, a bed on blue, means Hotel or Motel, whereas sign 1 with a red cross is a hospital.

qs.q: Vehicles bearing this identification sign are driven by drivers who:
o: Are deaf or deaf and mute.
Have less than three years of driving experience.
qs.x: The yellow disc with three black dots is the identification sign for deaf or deaf-mute drivers.

qs.q: Which of the following signs indicates the end of a zone with a maximum speed limit of 50 km/h?
qs.x: Sign 2, the black-ringed disc with a grey 50 struck by diagonal lines, marks the end of the maximum-speed zone.

qs.q: What do this sign and supplementary plate warn of?
o: Stopping on the road shoulder is prohibited because of roadworks.
Entering the road shoulder is dangerous because of roadworks.
Parking on the road shoulder is prohibited because of roadworks.
qs.x: The triangle shows a worker digging and the plaque shows a car on the shoulder: driving onto the shoulder is dangerous due to roadwork.

qs.q: Which of the following signs indicates the end of all previously imposed restrictions?
qs.x: Sign 4, the plain white disc with black diagonal stripes, cancels all previously imposed restrictions.

qs.q: In which case has the driver correctly complied with the requirements of this sign?
o: The driver yielded the right of way to motor vehicles travelling on the intersecting road.
The driver yielded the right of way to vehicles travelling on the intersecting road.
qs.x: The inverted-triangle Yield sign requires giving way to all vehicles on the intersecting road, not only motor vehicles.

qs.q: Which sign requires drivers to yield the right of way to vehicles travelling on the intersecting road?
qs.x: Sign 4, the inverted red-bordered triangle, is Yield and requires giving way to traffic on the intersecting road.

qs.q: Is stopping to pick up passengers permitted in the lane indicated by this sign?
o: Permitted if the lane is adjacent to the right edge of the carriageway and is not separated from the rest of the carriageway by a solid road marking.
qs.x: The blue sign with an arrow and a bus marks a transit lane; stopping to pick up passengers is allowed if it is on the right edge and not separated by a solid line.

qs.q: When this road sign is in place:
o: Overtaking by all types of vehicles is prohibited, except for overtaking slow-moving vehicles, horse- drawn carts, two-wheeled motorcycles without sidecars, mopeds and bicycles.
Overtaking by trucks with a maximum permissible mass not exceeding 3.5 tonnes is permitted.
Overtaking is permitted if the speed of the overtaking vehicle does not exceed 30 km/h.
qs.x: The sign with a red car beside a black car prohibits overtaking, except of slow vehicles, animal carts, solo motorcycles, mopeds and bicycles.

qs.q: Which of the following signs indicates a crossing with a cycle track?
qs.x: Sign 2, the triangle with a bicycle, warns of a bicycle-path crossing, whereas the blue disc 1 marks the bicycle path itself.

qs.q: Which of the following signs indicates the end of the no-overtaking zone?
qs.x: Sign 1, two cars crossed by diagonal stripes, marks the end of the no-passing zone.

qs.q: Which of the following signs indicates the directions of travel at a T-junction?
qs.x: Permitted directions at an intersection are shown by a blue arrow sign, while the chevron board, dead-end and side-road signs mean something else.

qs.q: This road sign indicates:
o: The direction of travel to a destination located within a built-up area.
The end of an acceleration lane or an additional lane on an uphill section.
qs.x: The blue square with a white T-shape and a red bar on top is the dead-end sign.

qs.q: Which of the following signs does not apply to public transport vehicles operating on regular routes?
qs.x: The No Motor Vehicles sign (4) does not apply to route public transport.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to travel within the area of effect of this sign?
o: Vehicles with a maximum speed exceeding 40 km/h.
qs.x: The blue sign with a white car marks a road for automobiles, where cars and motorcycles are allowed.

qs.q: Which of the following road signs is not a prohibitory sign?
qs.x: Sign 2, the inverted triangle (Yield), is a priority sign, while the others in red rings or with a red cross are prohibitory.

qs.q: What does this identification sign mean?
o: A section of road with an uneven carriageway lies ahead.
A section of road with three traffic lanes in this direction lies ahead.
The motor vehicle is fitted with studded tyres.
qs.x: The letter Ш in the red triangle shows the vehicle is fitted with studded tyres.

qs.q: Which of the following signs is called “End of one-way road”?
qs.x: Sign 4, a blue square with a white arrow slashed by a red diagonal, means end of one-way road.

qs.q: Which of the following signs requires drivers to yield the right of way to vehicles travelling on the intersecting road?
qs.x: Sign 2, the inverted triangle, requires giving way to vehicles on the intersecting road.

qs.q: The following signs indicate:
o: A parking area 30 metres ahead for passenger cars displaying the “Disabled Person” identification sign.
A parking area extending for 30 metres for vehicles other than motorized wheelchairs.
A parking area extending for 30 metres for motorized wheelchairs and passenger cars displaying the “Disabled Person” identification sign.
qs.x: The blue P with a wheelchair plaque and a 30 m plaque with arrows marks a 30 m parking zone for motorized wheelchairs and cars displaying the Disabled sign.

qs.q: Which of the following signs is a vehicle identification sign?
qs.x: Sign 3, the yellow square with a red border and running children, is a vehicle identification sign; the other two are road signs.

qs.q: Which vehicles are prohibited from travelling by this road sign?
o: Passenger cars and other automobiles only.
qs.x: The car in a red ring prohibits all motor vehicles, not just cars.

qs.q: Which of the following signs indicates that an obstruction may be passed on either the right or the left?
qs.x: Sign 5, a blue disc with two diverging white arrows, allows passing the obstruction on either side.

qs.q: Which of the following signs must be displayed at the front and rear of vehicles transporting organized groups of children?
qs.x: Sign 1, the yellow square with a red border and running children, goes on the front and rear of vehicles carrying organized groups of children.

qs.q: What do the following road signs indicate?
o: The priority road continues to the left at the intersection.
The priority road continues straight ahead and to the left at the intersection.
qs.x: The plaque below the yellow diamond Priority Road sign shows that at the intersection the priority road turns to the left.

qs.q: What do the following road signs indicate?
o: Within the area of effect of the supplementary plate, drivers must travel at a speed higher than that shown on the sign.
Within the area of effect of the supplementary plate, drivers are advised to travel at the speed shown on the sign.
qs.x: The blue square sign with 50 and the 800 m plaque with arrows recommend that speed on that stretch.

qs.q: Which of the following signs apply only when the road surface is wet?
qs.x: Only sign C carries the rain-cloud plaque, so only it applies just while the road surface is wet.

qs.q: What should the driver do in this situation?
o: Move into the lane for oncoming traffic.
qs.x: The overhead sign and yellow temporary diagram show your lane is closed, so you move into the oncoming lane.

qs.q: What do the following road signs indicate?
o: The road narrows on the right 150–300 metres beyond the sign, and the narrowed section is 100 metres long.
The road narrows on the right 100 metres beyond the sign.
qs.x: The right-narrowing triangle with the 100 m plaque means a narrowed section 100 m long begins some 150–300 m ahead.

qs.q: In which direction is the driver permitted to proceed?
o: Straight ahead or in the opposite direction.
qs.x: The red-ringed sign with the double-headed arrow plaque closes the road to both left and right, leaving only straight ahead and a U-turn.

qs.q: What do the following road signs indicate?
