o: Stopping is prohibited on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.
qs.x: The no-stopping sign with the red asterisk plaque applies on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, i.e. non-working days.

qs.q: Which road sign prohibits making a U-turn?
qs.x: Sign 3, the crossed-out U-shaped arrow, prohibits a U-turn, while signs 1 and 2 prohibit right and left turns.

qs.q: What do these road signs indicate?
o: It is dangerous to drive onto the shoulder because of roadworks.
Roadworks are being carried out on the road.
qs.x: The roadwork triangle with the plaque of a car beside the shoulder warns that driving onto the shoulder is dangerous.

qs.q: What must a driver do when this road sign is placed before an intersection?
o: Proceed through the intersection while ensuring safety.
Yield the right of way to vehicles travelling on the intersecting road.
Stop before the sign and yield the right of way to vehicles travelling on the intersecting road.
qs.x: The red octagonal STOP sign requires a full stop before the line or sign and yielding to traffic on the intersecting road.

qs.q: Which of the following road signs do not apply to public transport vehicles operating on regular routes?
qs.x: Only the fourth sign, the car in a red ring, does not apply to public transit vehicles, whereas the parking and stopping bans apply to them too.

qs.q: This road sign indicates that:
o: At the intersection, traffic must proceed either left or right.
Reversible traffic is in operation on the intersecting road.
One-way traffic is in operation on the intersecting road.
qs.x: The blue square with a double-headed arrow at the intersection indicates reversible traffic on the intersecting road.

qs.q: In this situation, is the driver required to yield the right of way to the truck?
o: Yes, the driver is required to yield.
No, the driver is not required to yield.
qs.x: The blue sign with the red slash over a car and pedestrians is End of Residential Zone, so on leaving it you must yield to other road users, including the truck.

qs.q: What do the following road signs indicate?
o: When the road is icy, vehicles must travel at a speed of 40 km/h.
When the road surface is wet, vehicles must not exceed 40 km/h.
qs.x: The red-ringed 40 with the rain-cloud plaque sets a 40 km/h maximum when the road surface is wet.

qs.q: What do the following road signs indicate?
o: Stopping is prohibited on working days.
qs.x: The no-stopping sign with the crossed-hammers plaque applies on working days (weekdays).

qs.q: What do the following road signs indicate?
o: The maximum permitted speed on this section of road is 50 km/h.
The recommended speed on this section of road is 50 km/h.
Only travel at the speed indicated on the sign or at a higher speed is permitted.
qs.x: The blue square with 50 is a recommended-speed sign, and the windsock triangle beside it warns of crosswinds.

qs.q: Which road sign requires drivers to proceed either left or right only?
qs.x: Sign 3, the blue disc with arrows splitting left and right, allows only a left or right turn.

qs.q: What do the following road signs indicate?
o: When the road surface is wet, the recommended speed is 40 km/h.
When the road surface is wet, the maximum permitted speed is 40 km/h.
qs.x: The blue square 40 with the rain-cloud plaque recommends that speed on a wet road.

qs.q: The following road signs apply:
o: On the left side of the road.
On the right side of the road.
On the side of the road on which they are installed.
qs.x: The odd-date and even-date parking-ban signs apply on the side of the road where they are installed.

qs.q: In this situation, which path is permitted for passing the obstruction?
qs.x: The blue disc with two diverging arrows shows the barrier can be passed on the right (A) or on the left (B).

qs.q: What must the driver do in this situation?
o: Stop at least 5 metres before the first railway track.
qs.x: At the crossing a red STOP sign stands in front of the crossbuck, so the driver must stop before the second sign, the STOP sign.

qs.q: What should the driver do if they intend to turn right at the intersection?
o: The driver may change into the right-hand traffic lane and then turn right.
The driver may approach the intersection and then turn right.
qs.x: The blue lane signs above the intersection allow a right turn from the right lane and from the straight-or-right lane, so both approaches are valid.

qs.q: In this situation, is the driver permitted to make a U-turn 200 metres beyond the sign?
o: No, a U-turn is not permitted.
qs.x: The blue U-turn sign with the 200 m plaque indicates a designated place for a U-turn 200 m ahead, so turning there is permitted.

qs.q: In this situation, is the driver required to stop at the location indicated by the traffic controller?
o: No, because the road sign prohibits stopping.
Yes, the driver is required to stop.
qs.x: The traffic controller's signals override road signs, so you must stop where he indicates despite the no-stopping sign in the picture.

qs.q: What must the driver do in this situation?
o: Proceed across the railway level crossing while ensuring safety.
Proceed across the railway level crossing without stopping.
Stop before the sign and, after ensuring safety, proceed across the multiple-track railway level crossing.
qs.x: The double crossbuck marks a multiple-track crossing and the red STOP sign requires stopping first, then crossing only when safe.

qs.q: What does the road marking on the carriageway indicate?
o: The boundaries of lanes designated for vehicles travelling in the same direction.
The boundaries of a reversible traffic lane.
qs.x: The overhead lights with a red X and a green arrow above the lane mark a reversible traffic lane.

qs.q: What should the driver do in this situation?
o: Yield the right of way to vehicles travelling on the intersecting road, if necessary.
Stop and yield the right of way to vehicles travelling on the intersecting road.
qs.x: The red STOP sign and the stop line require a full stop and yielding to the vehicle on the intersecting road, not just yielding if necessary.

qs.q: Which of the following road signs prohibits entering an intersection when traffic congestion ahead in the direction of travel has developed, except when turning right or left?
qs.x: Sign 3, the grey square with a yellow border and diagonals (Intersection Area), prohibits entering the intersection if a jam has formed ahead.

qs.q: At a complex intersection, what is the maximum distance from the intersection boundary at which the “Intersection Area” road sign may be installed if it cannot be placed at the boundary?
qs.x: The Intersection Area sign, the square with a yellow cross, may be placed at most 30 m away if it cannot be put at the intersection boundary.

qs.q: What does the following road sign warn of?
o: Entering the intersection area is prohibited if congestion ahead in the direction of travel would force the driver to stop.
Entering the intersection area is prohibited if congestion has developed ahead in the direction of travel.
qs.x: The square with the yellow cross forbids entering the intersection if a jam ahead would force you to stop inside it.

qs.q: What does the following road marking indicate?
o: An area of an intersection that must not be entered if congestion ahead in the direction of travel would force the driver to stop.
qs.x: The yellow criss-cross grid marking denotes an intersection area you may not enter if congestion would make you stop in it.

qs.q: Which of the following road markings indicates an area of an intersection that must not be entered if congestion ahead in the direction of travel would force the driver to stop?
qs.x: The yellow grid (option 3), unlike the zebra bars or the chevron wedge, marks the area you may not enter when traffic is jammed.

qs.q: Is making a U-turn from the indicated lane permitted?
qs.x: The sign above permits only straight or right from this lane and there is a double solid line to the left, so a U-turn is prohibited.

qs.q: Along which path is a U-turn permitted?
o: It is prohibited along both paths.
qs.x: The straight-only sign applies from where it stands, so a U-turn is allowed only along path A, made before the sign.

qs.q: Along which path is a U-turn permitted?
qs.x: The signs in view (end of one-way road and the two-way traffic warning) allow a U-turn along neither path A nor B.

qs.q: Which driver may proceed straight ahead at this intersection?
o: The driver of a public transport vehicle.
qs.x: The blue mandatory right-turn sign does not apply to public transit vehicles, so only the transit driver may go straight.

qs.q: Along which path is a U-turn permitted?
qs.x: The straight-only sign applies from its location, so the U-turn at the intersection along A is allowed but not along B.

qs.q: Are you required to stop before the stop line?
qs.x: The traffic light is green and a signal takes precedence over the STOP sign, so there is no need to stop at the stop line.

qs.q: Travel is permitted:
o: Only in direction A or B.
qs.x: The blue sign with straight and right arrows permits only straight (B) or right (A); left (C) is not allowed.

qs.q: This road sign indicates:
o: The distance from the end of the tunnel.
The distance from a place where children may be present.
The location of an emergency exit and the distance to it.
qs.x: The green arrow sign in the tunnel with a door, a running figure and 150 m shows the emergency exit and its distance.

qs.q: In this situation:
o: We must yield the right of way to the truck driver.
We may pass through the narrow section first.
qs.x: The blue sign with a large white up arrow and a small red down arrow gives us priority over the oncoming truck, so we may pass the narrow section first.

qs.q: What does this road sign prohibit?
o: Travelling at a speed exceeding 20 km/h.
qs.x: The sign with a pedestrian in a blue disc and the zone wording marks a pedestrian zone, where all vehicle traffic is prohibited.

qs.q: Where must you stop to comply with this sign?
o: Before the intersection of the carriageways (C).
qs.x: With a STOP sign and no stop line, you stop before the intersecting roadway (C), not at the sign or earlier.

qs.q: Which signs impose a speed limit?
qs.x: Only sign 2, the Residential Zone sign with a car, people and houses, limits speed; yield, recommended 50 and loose-gravel signs do not.

qs.q: Which sign applies only to the lane above which it is placed?
qs.x: Sign A, the 50 limit with the down-arrow plaque, applies only to the lane above which it is installed.

qs.q: Is parking in the indicated place permitted?
qs.x: The no-parking sign is still ahead and the car is before it at the roadside, so parking there is allowed.

qs.q: In which direction is travel permitted?
o: Straight ahead and in the opposite direction.
qs.x: The sign on the right shows a crossed-out left-turn arrow, so a left turn is banned while straight ahead and a U-turn remain allowed.

qs.q: Which sign does not apply to you if you reside within the area in which the sign is in force?
qs.x: Signs A (plain red ring) and C (car in red ring) do not apply to residents' vehicles, while B (the red disc with a white bar, No Entry) applies to everyone.

qs.q: What does this supplementary information plate indicate?
o: The distance from the sign to an intersection where a “Yield” sign is placed immediately before the intersection.
The distance from the sign to an intersection where a “Stop” sign is placed immediately before the intersection.
The location of a border checkpoint.
qs.x: The STOP 250 m plaque shows the distance to the intersection where a STOP sign is installed right before it.

qs.q: Is stopping at the indicated place permitted?
qs.x: The no-stopping sign is still ahead of us, so stopping at our current position is allowed.

qs.q: Which signs remain in force, in the direction of travel, up to the next intersection?
qs.x: A and C carry the zone plaque and apply within the zone, while ordinary signs B (50) and D (no parking) apply up to the nearest intersection.

qs.q: What speed requirement is established on this road by these signs?
o: A minimum speed of 50 km/h in the left-hand lane for traffic travelling in the same direction.
qs.x: The blue disc 50 with a down-arrow plaque sets a minimum speed of 50 km/h only for the lane the arrow points to.

qs.q: Which of the signs prohibit turning left?
qs.x: Signs A (left arrow reserved for the bus) and C (U-turn) keep ordinary vehicles from turning left, while B bans only a U-turn.

qs.q: Is the driver permitted to turn left?
qs.x: The sign only shows a dead end on the left side road and imposes no ban, so a left turn is permitted.

qs.q: These signs indicate that:
o: There is a risk of pedestrians entering the carriageway along the next 150 m of road.
There is an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing 150 m ahead.
qs.x: The triangle with a pedestrian on zebra stripes and the 150 m plaque warns of an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing 150 m ahead.

qs.q: Along which paths is travel permitted?
qs.x: The blue Roundabout sign requires circulating counter-clockwise, so only path B is allowed, whereas A is cut off by the no-right-turn sign and C goes against the flow.

qs.q: Which signs prohibit travelling at a speed below 40 km/h?
qs.x: The Motorway (A) and Road for Automobiles (B) signs forbid driving slower than 40 km/h, while C is only a recommended speed.

qs.q: Which signs require you to yield the right of way to oncoming traffic on a narrow section of road?
qs.x: A shows a steep descent where the downhill driver must give way at a narrow section, and C, the red-ringed arrows sign, directly requires yielding to oncoming traffic.

qs.q: Is turning right onto the unpaved road permitted?
qs.x: There is no sign banning a right turn; the triangle and chevron boards only warn about the bend, so turning right onto the unpaved road is allowed.

qs.q: Is stopping at the indicated place to pick up a passenger permitted?
qs.x: The no-parking sign (blue disc with one slash) with the 50 m plaque bans only parking, so stopping to pick up a passenger is allowed.

qs.q: Which sign indicates a footpath?
qs.x: The blue disc with a walking figure (B) is the pedestrian path; A bans pedestrians and C marks a pedestrian crossing.

qs.q: This road sign:
o: Warns that you are approaching a narrow section of road.
Requires you to yield the right of way to oncoming drivers on a narrow section of road.
qs.x: The red circle with black and red arrows requires yielding to oncoming traffic at a narrow section, such as the oncoming truck here.

qs.q: What should you do if you need to reverse your direction of travel?
o: Make a U-turn at this intersection.
Proceed straight through the intersection and then make a U-turn.
qs.x: The blue sign mandates straight ahead only, so to reverse direction you drive straight through and make the U-turn elsewhere.

qs.q: Is parking at the indicated place permitted?
qs.x: A no-stopping sign (red cross on blue) stands at the right, and a stopping ban also covers parking, so parking there is prohibited.

qs.q: This road sign indicates that:
o: Stopping on the shoulder is prohibited.
Driving onto the shoulder is dangerous because of roadworks.
Stopping is permitted only on the carriageway.
qs.x: The roadworks triangle with the plaque of a car at the roadside means entering the shoulder is dangerous because of roadwork.

qs.q: In which directions is travel permitted from the indicated lane?
o: Straight ahead, left and in the opposite direction.
qs.x: The lane signs show that from the leftmost lane straight, left and a U-turn are all permitted.

qs.q: In which of the indicated directions may you continue at this intersection?
qs.x: The straight-only sign stands at the far side and applies from its location, so A and B are allowed, while the right turn (C) passes the sign.

qs.q: This road sign:
o: Permits travelling only at 40 km/h or more.
Prohibits travelling at a speed exceeding 40 km/h.
qs.x: The red-ringed 40 prohibits driving faster than 40 km/h.

qs.q: Which supplementary plates indicate the area of effect of the sign with which they are displayed?
qs.x: Plaques B (arrows and 100 m) and C (arrow and 10 m) show the zone of effect, while A (300 m) gives only a distance ahead.

qs.q: Which courtyard may the driver enter?
qs.x: The straight-ahead sign governs the intersection itself and does not ban entering a yard; the right yard, beyond the intersection, may be entered.

qs.q: Which of these signs takes effect immediately from the point where it is installed?
qs.x: A's plate with arrows gives a zone starting at the sign and B has no plate, so both act immediately; C's 200 m plate is a distance ahead to the hazard.

qs.q: Along which paths is travel permitted?
qs.x: The U-turn sign allows turning around, and going straight or along C and D is fine; only path B does not follow the permitted manoeuvre.

qs.q: What does this road sign warn of?
o: An approaching slippery section of road.
An approaching wet and muddy section of road.
An approaching section of road where loose gravel may be thrown up by vehicle wheels.
qs.x: The triangle shows a car with stones flying from its wheels, which is the loose-gravel warning sign.

qs.q: Under which of these signs do the traffic rules applicable in built-up areas not apply?
qs.x: The blue sign (C) marks a settlement where built-up-area rules do not apply, while the white signs (A, B) introduce those rules.

qs.q: Which of these signs prohibits making a U-turn?
qs.x: These are only direction-of-traffic information signs (one-way, bus lane); none of them prohibits a U-turn.

qs.q: Is entering the indicated courtyard permitted?
qs.x: The straight-ahead sign applies to the intersection and does not prevent entering adjacent territory such as a yard.

qs.q: Which of these signs prohibits entry without a permit?
qs.x: Only the Customs (B) and Danger (C) signs, with red rim and bar, forbid proceeding without permission.

qs.q: What is the minimum distance from this sign at which an intersection of roads of equal priority may be encountered?
qs.x: In a populated area, warning signs are placed at least 50 m before the hazard.

qs.q: From which point do the traffic rules applicable in built-up areas take effect?
o: After the “Beginning of a Built-up Area” sign with a white background.
Only after signs displaying the name of a built-up area on a white or blue background.
Only after entering an area with buildings.
qs.x: Built-up-area rules take effect from the white-background Beginning of Populated Area sign.

qs.q: This road sign:
o: Warns of an intersection with tram tracks.
Warns of an approaching tram stop.
Requires you to yield the right of way to a tram driver.
qs.x: The triangle shows a tram, so this is the warning sign for a crossing with tram tracks.

qs.q: These signs require you to maintain the following distance from the vehicle ahead:
o: Up to 70 m over a 900 m section of road.
At least 70 m over a 900 m section of road.
A distance of 70 m after travelling 900 m.
qs.x: The distance sign with the 900 m plate and arrows requires at least 70 m behind the vehicle ahead along that 900 m stretch.

qs.q: In which directions may you proceed from the indicated lane?
o: Left, straight ahead and by making a U-turn.
qs.x: The sign above the middle lane allows a left turn and straight ahead; a U-turn is not provided for.

qs.q: These signs warn that:
o: A railway level crossing with three tracks is ahead.
A railway level crossing without barriers is 150–300 m ahead.
A railway level crossing is 50–100 m ahead.
qs.x: The plate with three red stripes means a railroad crossing without a barrier lies 150–300 m ahead.

qs.q: In this situation, sounding the horn is permitted:
o: Only to warn of an intention to overtake.
Only to prevent a road traffic accident.
qs.x: Under the no-horn sign, the horn may be used only to prevent a traffic accident.

qs.q: Which of these signs is used to mark a speed hump?
qs.x: A speed hump is marked by the blue square sign A; B and C are triangular warning signs.

qs.q: Along which paths may you proceed?
qs.x: A right turn must end in the nearest right-hand lane, which path A does, while B ends in the far lane.

qs.q: Which of these signs gives a driver priority over traffic on the intersecting road at an uncontrolled intersection?
qs.x: Sign A (priority road) and C (side road junction) give priority over traffic on the intersecting road.

qs.q: Is overtaking permitted in this situation?
o: Yes, if the motorcycle is travelling at less than 30 km/h.
qs.x: The no-overtaking sign does not apply to two-wheeled motorcycles, so passing is allowed.

qs.q: Along which path is making a U-turn permitted?
qs.x: A U-turn is made from the left and ends in the nearest lane of the opposite direction, which is path B.

qs.q: Is parking permitted at the indicated place on odd-numbered days of the month?
qs.x: The odd-date no-parking sign applies until 7:00 PM, after which the sides switch, so parking is allowed after 7:00 PM.

qs.q: Which signs indicate an area where drivers must yield the right of way to pedestrians crossing the carriageway?
qs.x: Signs B (pedestrian crossing) and C (residential zone) mark places where drivers must yield to pedestrians; A only warns.

qs.q: Which sign warns that you are approaching the beginning of a road with two-way traffic?
qs.x: Only the triangular warning sign A warns of the start of two-way traffic; B and C are information signs.

qs.q: Are you permitted to drive to your workplace located within the area of effect of these signs?
qs.x: The signs restrict through traffic; a person who works or lives within the zone may enter on any day, whatever the plate says.

qs.q: In which of the indicated directions is travel permitted?
qs.x: The sign shows the cross street is one-way to the left, so straight (A), left (B) and a U-turn (C) are all allowed; only a right turn is impossible.

qs.q: This sign:
o: Indicates the permitted directions of travel at the intersection.
qs.x: The sign with red-and-white chevrons shows the directions of travel at a T-intersection and prohibits nothing.

qs.q: Which sign indicates the length of the lane for making a U-turn?
qs.x: Sign B gives the length of the U-turn lane (15 m), while A's plate gives the distance to the U-turn place.

qs.q: In a built-up area, how far ahead does the slippery section of road begin?
qs.x: In a populated area, warning signs stand at least 50 m before the hazard.

qs.q: In which of the indicated directions may you continue at the next intersection?
qs.x: The straight-ahead sign governs the previous intersection; at the next one, every direction is allowed.

qs.q: Within the area of effect of which sign may you travel at 60 km/h?
qs.x: A caps speed at 50, B sets a minimum of 50, and C only recommends 50, so 60 km/h is fine under B and C.

qs.q: Which of the indicated directions are permitted?
qs.x: The no-right-turn sign rules out D, and path B does not follow the proper movement, leaving the left turn (A) and straight ahead (C).

qs.q: Which signs indicate a railway level crossing with two or more tracks?
qs.x: A crossing with two or more tracks is shown only by the double-cross sign C; A and B are single-track warnings.

qs.q: Is making a U-turn along the indicated path permitted?
qs.x: A U-turn in front of the roundabout would mean driving against its circulation, so it is prohibited.

qs.q: Is parking beyond the viaduct permitted?
qs.x: The no-parking sign stands right after the overpass, so parking beyond it is prohibited.

qs.q: These road signs indicate:
o: Construction work at a railway level crossing.
An approach to a railway level crossing with a barrier.
A railway level crossing without a barrier.
qs.x: The sign showing a barrier gate warns of an approaching railroad crossing with a barrier.

qs.q: Which signs permit making a U-turn?
qs.x: Neither the turn-left sign, the no-left-turn sign nor the one-way sign bans a U-turn, so it is allowed with all of them.

qs.q: From the indicated lane, travel is permitted:
o: To the left and for making a U-turn.
qs.x: The sign over the leftmost lane allows a left turn, and a U-turn from that lane is also allowed since nothing prohibits it.

qs.q: This sign warns that you are approaching a tunnel:
qs.x: This warning tunnel sign indicates a tunnel without artificial lighting.

qs.q: At which of the indicated places is stopping permitted?
o: Stopping is prohibited at all the indicated places.
qs.x: The no-stopping sign acts from its location onward, so stopping is allowed only before it, at B.

qs.q: Which of these signs permits you to turn left?
qs.x: A left turn is possible with B (dead-end information sign) and C (counter-flow bus lane); A marks one-way traffic to the right.

qs.q: This sign gives advance warning of:
o: The need to yield the right of way to a cyclist.
An intersection with a cycle track.
The approach to a cycling area.
qs.x: The triangle with a bicycle warns of an intersection with a bicycle path.

qs.q: Under which sign is it prohibited to resume driving after stopping without permission?
qs.x: Only sign 5 (Danger, with the bar) forbids resuming after stopping without permission.

qs.q: May these signs be installed immediately before a steep descent or ascent?
o: No, because warning signs must give advance notice of a hazard.
Yes, if descents and ascents follow one another.
Yes, but only in built-up areas.
qs.x: Descent and ascent signs may be placed right before them when descents and ascents follow one another.

qs.q: Which of the following road signs must the driver of a taxi with its taximeter switched on comply with?
qs.x: A taxi with its meter on is exempt from no-parking signs (2, 4, 5) but must obey No Stopping (1) and the speed limit (3).

qs.q: Which of the following road signs do not apply to vehicles owned by, or serving, people who live or work within the area of effect of the signs?
qs.x: No Vehicles (2) and No Motor Vehicles (3) do not apply to vehicles of people living or working in the zone.

qs.q: Which of the following road signs must the driver of a public transport vehicle operating on a regular route comply with?
qs.x: A route public transport driver must obey the speed limit (3) and No Stopping (5) signs.

qs.q: Which of the following road signs applies to vehicles driven by, or transporting, persons with Group I or Group II disabilities?
qs.x: The No Stopping sign (2) still applies to disabled drivers' vehicles, while they are exempt from the parking and no-vehicle bans.

qs.q: Which of the following road signs does not apply to public transport vehicles operating on regular routes?
qs.x: The No Entry sign (2) does not apply to route public transport.

qs.q: Which of the following road signs does not apply to public transport vehicles operating on regular routes?
qs.x: The No Vehicles sign (1) does not apply to route public transport.

qs.q: What do mandatory signs indicate?
o: Permitted directions of travel and the minimum speed, and prescribed directions of travel for pedestrians and drivers of certain vehicles.
The order of priority when passing through intersections and narrow sections of road.
qs.x: Mandatory signs show permitted directions, minimum speed and prescribed routes for pedestrians and certain vehicles.

qs.q: What do special regulation signs introduce or remove?
qs.x: Special regulation signs introduce or cancel particular traffic regimes.

qs.q: What information do information signs provide?
o: They specify or restrict the applicability of the signs with which they are used.
The location of built-up areas and other destinations, as well as established or recommended traffic arrangements.
qs.x: Information signs tell where towns and facilities are and which traffic regimes are set or recommended.

qs.q: What information do service signs provide?
o: The distance and direction to built-up areas and other inhabited places.
The location of the relevant facilities.
qs.x: Service signs show the location of the relevant facilities.

qs.q: What do supplementary information signs specify or restrict?
o: Specific traffic arrangements, and they indicate the distance to service facilities.
The applicability of the signs with which they are used.
qs.x: Supplementary plates clarify or restrict the effect of the signs they accompany.

qs.q: Is a bus with a trailer permitted to travel within the area of effect of the 'No Vehicles Towing Trailers' sign?
o: Only if the bus is a public transport vehicle operating on a regular route.
qs.x: The no-trailers sign covers trucks and tractors, so a bus with a trailer may proceed.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to tow a motor vehicle within the area of effect of the 'No Vehicles Towing Trailers' sign?
qs.x: The sign also forbids towing another motor vehicle, so the bus driver may not tow one.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to enter the area of effect of the 'Length Limit' sign if the bus is longer than the length indicated on the sign?
o: Yes, because the sign applies only to trucks and combinations of vehicles.
qs.x: The length-limit sign applies to all vehicles, so a bus longer than shown may not enter.

qs.q: In which case is the area of effect of a 'Maximum Speed Limit' sign not interrupted?
o: When the driver leaves a built-up area but there is no sign indicating the end of the speed restriction.
At exits from adjacent properties and at intersections with or junctions of field, forest and other minor roads, where no corresponding signs are installed before them.
At exits from adjacent properties and at intersections with or junctions of field, forest and other minor roads, where corresponding signs are installed before them.
qs.x: A speed-limit sign stays in force at exits from adjacent areas and minor road junctions when no signs precede them.

qs.q: What does this sign indicate?
o: The beginning of an area (section of road) where parking is permitted and regulated by signs and road markings.
The beginning of an area (section of road) designated for parking passenger cars.
qs.x: The 'Zone' sign with blue P marks the start of a permitted parking area regulated by signs and markings.

qs.q: Which statement about the “Zone with Parking Restrictions” sign is incorrect?
o: It applies across the entire width of the road.
It ceases to apply after passing through an intersection.
It applies only to the side of the road on which it is installed.
qs.x: It is false that the zone ends after an intersection; a zone sign remains in force through junctions.

qs.q: Which sign cancels the restriction imposed by the “Zone with Maximum Speed Limit” sign?
o: The “End of All Restrictions Zone” sign.
The “End of Maximum Speed Limit Zone” sign.
qs.x: A speed-limit zone is cancelled by its own End of Zone sign.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the “Emergency Escape Lane” sign?
o: To inform drivers of a lane on a steep descent where vehicle maintenance may be carried out.
To inform drivers of a lane on a steep descent intended for emergency stopping.
qs.x: The emergency escape lane sign shows a lane on a steep descent meant for emergency stopping.

qs.q: Which of the signs shown indicates that the main sign used with it applies exclusively to public transport vehicles?
qs.x: The plate with a bus and a plus sign (2) makes the main sign apply to public transport vehicles; plate 1 does not.

qs.q: To which vehicles does the main sign apply when this supplementary plate is placed beneath it?
o: Only electric vehicles with a maximum authorised mass not exceeding 3.5 tonnes.
Electric vehicles and plug-in hybrid vehicles that can be charged from an external power source.
qs.x: The plate with a plug and car refers to electric vehicles and hybrids that can be charged from an external source, not to a mass limit.

qs.q: Is a bus powered by an internal combustion engine permitted to enter the section of road where these signs are installed?
o: No, because the “No Entry” sign prohibits entry by all types of vehicles.
Yes, because in this case the prohibition applies only to electric and hybrid vehicles.
qs.x: The plate limits the No Entry sign to electric and hybrid vehicles only, so a combustion-engine bus may enter.

qs.q: With which signs may the supplementary plate shown above be used?
o: Only with signs prohibiting stopping or parking.
qs.x: The tow-truck plate is used only with signs that prohibit stopping or parking.

qs.q: Are intersections or junctions with other roads at the same level permitted on a motorway?
o: Yes, if they are controlled by traffic signals or appropriate road signs.
Only junctions intended to provide access from minor roads are permitted.
qs.x: A motorway has no same-level intersections or junctions at all, even ones controlled by signals or signs.

qs.q: On a motorway, opposing carriageways must be separated from one another by:
o: Only double continuous road markings and a planted strip.
A central reservation or a road safety barrier.
qs.x: Opposing carriageways on a motorway must be separated by a central reservation or road barrier, not just by markings.

qs.q: A bus travelling on a motorway develops a mechanical fault that prevents it from exceeding 40 km/h. May it continue at that speed to the nearest parking area or repair facility?
o: Yes, if it travels in the rightmost lane with its hazard warning lights switched on.
qs.x: Only vehicles able to reach at least 40 km/h may use a motorway, so the bus may not carry on even with hazard lights.

qs.q: What must a bus driver do in the event of a forced stop on the carriageway of a motorway?
o: Leave the bus where it is, activate the left turn indicator and wait for a towing vehicle.
Switch on the hazard warning lights, place a warning triangle and take steps to remove the bus from the carriageway.
qs.x: After a forced stop you must switch on the hazard lights, set out a warning triangle and take steps to clear the carriageway.

qs.q: Are buses with a maximum permissible mass exceeding 3.5 tonnes permitted to use lanes to the left of the second lane on a motorway?
qs.x: The ban on lanes left of the second applies to trucks over 3.5 t, not to buses, so buses are permitted.

qs.q: If a bus develops a mechanical fault while travelling on a motorway, may its driver use an emergency opening in the central reservation?
o: Yes, because a mechanical fault constitutes a forced stop and the driver may use any unobstructed part of the road to clear the carriageway as quickly as possible.
qs.x: Openings in the central reservation are not for general traffic, and a breakdown does not give a right to use them.

qs.q: Is a bus permitted to enter an emergency opening in the central reservation of a public road in order to manoeuvre?
o: Yes, but only for scheduled-service buses.
qs.x: Entering openings in the central reservation to manoeuvre is prohibited for all buses, scheduled-service ones included.

qs.q: When leaving a residential zone, to which vehicles on the intersecting road must a bus driver yield the right of way if there are no priority signs before the intersection?
o: Only vehicles approaching from the right.
Only vehicles approaching from the left.
qs.x: Leaving a residential zone gives no priority, so the driver yields to all vehicles on the road being joined.

qs.q: On which roads is learner-driver training permitted?
o: On any road, provided the vehicle displays the 'Learner Vehicle' identification sign.
On roads designated by the local self-government authorities (the Yerevan Municipality in Yerevan).
qs.x: Learner training is allowed only on roads designated by local authorities (the Yerevan Municipality in Yerevan), not on any road.

qs.q: What does a black outline arrow (or arrows) on the main green traffic signal inform drivers about?
o: The presence of an additional signal section.
The absence of an additional signal section.
qs.x: A black outline arrow on the main green signal tells drivers that the signal has an additional section.

qs.q: What does a black outline arrow (or arrows) on the main green traffic signal indicate to drivers?
o: The permitted directions of travel not controlled by the additional signal section.
The permitted directions of travel controlled by the additional signal section.
qs.x: The outline arrow shows the permitted directions that are not controlled by the additional section's signal.

qs.q: When may the green signal of a pedestrian traffic light be accompanied by an audible signal different from the special audible signals used by vehicles?
o: Only at intersections with a dedicated lane for buses and other public transport vehicles, to help passengers find their way in poor visibility.
At locations where blind pedestrians frequently cross the road, to inform them that they may cross the carriageway.
qs.x: A sound accompanies the pedestrian green where blind pedestrians often cross, to tell them they may cross.

qs.q: Which vehicles may be controlled by a traffic signal consisting of four single-colour, moon-white circular lights arranged in a T-shape?
o: All buses operating regular urban passenger services.
Trams and other public transport vehicles travelling in a dedicated lane.
qs.x: A T-shaped signal of four moon-white round lights controls trams and other public transport using a dedicated lane.

qs.q: Is learner-driver training permitted in residential zones?
o: Yes, but only during daylight hours.
Yes, but only if the learner vehicle does not exceed 20 km/h.
qs.x: Learner training is prohibited in residential zones regardless of time of day or speed.

qs.q: Is learner-driver training permitted on roads marked with the 'Road for Motor Vehicles' sign?
o: Yes, but only when traffic is light.
Yes, but only during daylight hours.
qs.x: Learner training is prohibited on roads with the Road for Motor Vehicles sign under any conditions.

qs.q: Which of these signs apply to public transport vehicles?
qs.x: Only sign 4 (No motor vehicles) does not apply to public transport; signs 1, 2, 3 and 5 do.

qs.q: Which of these signs prohibit public transport vehicles from turning right?
qs.x: Only sign 4 (left arrow only) rules out a right turn; signs 1 and 3 both allow it.

qs.q: Which sign does not apply to public transport vehicles?
qs.x: The No Right Turn sign (5) does not apply to public transport vehicles; the other signs do.

qs.q: Is crossing the broken reversible lane marking permitted when the reversible traffic signals are absent or switched off?
o: Yes, if the marking is to the driver's right.
qs.x: With reversible-lane signals absent or off, the 1.9 marking may be crossed if it lies to the driver's right.

qs.q: A bus driver intends to proceed straight ahead. What must the driver do when the traffic signal is flashing yellow?
o: Yield the right of way to vehicles approaching from both the right and the left.
Yield the right of way to the tram only.
Yield the right of way to the passenger car only.
qs.x: At a flashing yellow the junction is unregulated, and the bus going straight must yield only to the passenger car on the main road.

qs.q: The signals of this traffic light apply to:
o: Trams and other public transport vehicles travelling in a designated lane.
qs.x: The T-shaped moon-white signals apply to trams and other public transport in a dedicated lane.

qs.q: Is a bus permitted to travel in the right lane?
o: Yes, if it is a route-service bus.
qs.x: The right lane in the picture is a bus lane (A marking and sign), so only a scheduled-service bus may use it.

qs.q: Is the driver of a bus with an actual mass of 3.5 tonnes permitted to continue straight ahead from this lane?
o: No. From the second lane and any lane to its left, a bus may only turn left or make a U-turn.
qs.x: The truck plate limits the sign to trucks; a bus is not a truck, so it may continue straight ahead.

qs.q: Is a bus with an actual mass of 3.5 tonnes permitted to turn right in this situation?
o: No. Before turning, the driver must move into the appropriate outermost lane in advance.
Yes, because a right turn may be made from any lane without restriction.
qs.x: The bus is already in the outermost right lane under a right-turn sign, so turning right is permitted.

qs.q: In which direction is the bus driver permitted to proceed in this situation?
o: To the right only, yielding the right of way to vehicles approaching from other directions.
To the left or by making a U-turn.
qs.x: The red main signal prohibits movement, and the additional section does not let the bus go in any direction from this lane.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: Trolleybus and bus, then passenger car.
qs.x: By the main-road plate, the trolleybus is on the main road and goes first, then the car, while the bus yields to both.

qs.q: Which car will be the first to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: No vehicle approaches from the green car's right, so by the right-hand rule it goes first.

qs.q: Which car will be the last to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: The blue car has the red car on its right, which in turn has the truck on its right, so blue yields to both and goes last.

qs.q: When will the blue car pass through the intersection?
qs.x: The light is green and the red car turning left must yield to the oncoming blue car going straight, so blue goes first.

qs.q: Which answer gives the correct order in which the vehicles will pass through the intersection?
o: The bus, the passenger car, the bicycle.
The passenger car, the bus, the bicycle.
The bicycle, the bus, the passenger car.
qs.x: Nothing is on the bicyclist's right, the bus has the bicyclist on its right, and the car has the bus on its right: bicycle, bus, car.

qs.q: Which vehicle will be the second to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: The blue car turning left yields to both the oncoming red car and the tram; the tram goes second, after the red car.

qs.q: In which direction is driving prohibited?
o: To the right at the first entrance.
To the right at the second entrance.
To the right at both the first and second entrances.
qs.x: The no-right-turn sign stands at the second passage, so a right turn is prohibited there, not at the first.

qs.q: Which car will be the second to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: By the priority-road and yield signs, the red car yields only to the one with priority over it and has priority over the last one, so it goes second.

qs.q: Which car will be the second to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: At an unmarked intersection the right-hand rule applies: blue yields to the car on its right and has priority over the one on its left, so it goes second.

qs.q: Which car will be the second to pass through the intersection?
o: The white car, at the same time as the yellow car.
qs.x: Red is on the main road and has priority over cars at the yield sign, but yields to the main-road car with priority over it, so it goes second.

qs.q: Which car will be the last to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: Vehicles approach from green's right, so by the right-hand rule it yields and goes last.

qs.q: Which road user must yield the right of way?
qs.x: The bicyclist approaches from the car's right, so the car driver must yield.

qs.q: Which car will be the first to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: The red car is on the main road and has priority; the cars on the minor roads must yield.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The motorcycle, the car, the tram.
The tram, the car, the motorcycle.
The tram, the motorcycle, the car.
qs.x: The tram goes straight and leaves the main road shown by the plates, so it yields and goes last; the motorcycle goes before the car.

qs.q: Which car will be the second to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: At an unmarked intersection blue yields to the truck on its right and has priority over the red car on its left, so it goes second.

qs.q: Which car will be the last to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: Red has a vehicle approaching from its right and ends up last in the right-hand-rule order.

qs.q: Which car will be the last to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: The plate shows the main road bends along the green and blue cars' route, while red is on the secondary road and yields to both.

qs.q: Which car will be the first to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: Nothing approaches from the green truck's right, so by the right-hand rule it goes first.

qs.q: Which vehicle driver must yield the right of way?
qs.x: The motorcycle approaches from the bus's right, so the bus driver must yield.

qs.q: Which car will be the first to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: Blue is on the main road (sign with plate), so it has priority over the others and goes first.

qs.q: Which car will be the second to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: At an unmarked intersection blue yields to the car on its right and has priority over the one on its left, so it goes second.

qs.q: Which car will be the third to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: Yellow faces a yield sign, so it goes after the main-road cars but before the one that must yield to it, making it third.

qs.q: The red car:
o: Has priority because it approaches the roundabout from the right of the blue car.
Must yield the right of way to the blue car travelling around the roundabout.
qs.x: Entering a roundabout, you must yield to the blue car already on it, even if you approach from its right.

qs.q: In which order will the cars pass through the intersection?
o: The yellow car, the green car, the blue car.
The blue and green cars at the same time, followed by the yellow car.
qs.x: The blue and green paths do not cross, so they go together, and yellow yields and goes last.

qs.q: Which car will be the third to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: Blue goes third, while yellow faces the STOP sign and goes last.

qs.q: Which car will be the first to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: Red has no vehicle on its right, so by the right-hand rule it goes first.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The red car, the green car, the blue car, the black car.
The green car, the red car, the black car, the blue car.
The green car, the red car, the blue car, the black car.
qs.x: Red and green are on the main road (red first); of the minor-road cars blue goes before black, which must stop at STOP and yield to the vehicle on its right.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The tram, the yellow car, the green car.
The tram and the green car, followed by the yellow car.
The green car, the yellow car, the tram.
qs.x: The tram and the green car do not conflict, so they go together, and yellow yields to them and goes last.

qs.q: Which driver has the right of way?
qs.x: The car approaches from the motorcycle's right, so by the right-hand rule the car driver has priority.

qs.q: Which car will be the second to pass through the intersection?
qs.x: At an unmarked intersection green yields to the car on its right and has priority over the one on its left, so it goes second.

qs.q: Which vehicle driver must yield the right of way?
qs.x: The tram has priority on its rails at an unmarked intersection, so the car drivers must yield.

qs.q: When will the red car pass through the intersection?
qs.x: The light is green and the green car turning left must yield to the oncoming red car going straight, so red goes first.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The passenger car, the bus, the bicycle.
The bus, the bicycle, the passenger car.
The bus, the passenger car, the bicycle.
The bicycle, the bus, the passenger car.
qs.x: The bicyclist is on the main road and goes first, the bus second, and the car, at the yield sign, goes last.

qs.q: Which road user has the right of way?
qs.x: Both are on the main road, but the van turning left must yield to the oncoming bicyclist.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The tram, followed by the car and bus at the same time.
The tram, the bus, the car.
The bus, the tram, the car.
qs.x: The tram is on the main road and goes first; the car and bus both face give-way signs but their paths do not cross, so they go together.

qs.q: Which vehicle driver must yield the right of way?
o: The driver of the blue car.
The driver of the red car.
qs.x: The red car approaches from the blue vehicle's right, so by the right-hand rule the blue driver must yield.

qs.q: Which vehicle driver must yield the right of way?
qs.x: The car is on the main road (sign with plate), while the motorcyclist faces a yield sign.

qs.q: Which driver is entering the roundabout correctly?
qs.x: Both drivers turn right into the roundabout from their own lanes in the direction of circulation, which is correct.

qs.q: Which vehicle has the right of way?
o: The red car, because it enters the roundabout from the right of the blue car.
The blue car, because it is already travelling around the roundabout.
qs.x: On a roundabout the blue car already circulating has priority, and the red car entering must yield.

qs.q: Indicate the order in which the vehicles will pass through the intersection.
o: The blue car, followed by the red and green cars at the same time.
The red car, the blue car, the green car.
The red and green cars at the same time, followed by the blue car.
qs.x: Red and green are on the main road and do not obstruct each other, while blue faces a STOP sign and goes last.

qs.q: The driver of the green car:

qs.q: Which car will be the last to pass through the intersection?

qs.q: Which car will be the second to pass through the intersection?

o: The blue car, the green car, the red car.

qs.q: Which car will be the second to pass through the intersection?

qs.q: When will the red car pass through the intersection?
o: Second, at the same time as the blue car.
Third, after the green and yellow cars.
qs.x: The red and blue cars' paths do not cross, so they go together as the second group.

qs.q: When will the yellow car pass through the intersection?
qs.x: Yellow faces a STOP sign, so it must stop and yield to everyone, going last.

qs.q: Which answer gives the correct order in which the vehicles will pass?
o: The motorcycle, the bus, the truck.
The bus, the motorcycle, the truck.
The bus, the truck, the motorcycle.
qs.x: Nothing is on the motorcycle's right, the bus has the motorcycle on its right, and the truck has the bus on its right: motorcycle, bus, truck.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The passenger car, the bus, the tram.
The tram, the bus, the passenger car.
The tram, the passenger car, the bus.
qs.x: The tram has priority on rails and the left-turning bus yields to the oncoming car: tram, car, bus.

qs.q: Which vehicle driver must yield the right of way?
qs.x: The car approaches from the bus's right, so the bus driver must yield.

qs.q: Which vehicle must yield the right of way?
qs.x: Red is entering the roundabout and must yield to the blue car already on it.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The yellow bus, the truck, the green bus.
The truck, the yellow bus, the green bus.
The yellow bus, the green bus, the truck.
qs.x: The truck is on the main road (per the plate) and goes first, then by the right-hand rule the yellow bus, and the green bus last.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The bus, followed by the passenger car and the truck at the same time.
The passenger car and the truck at the same time, followed by the bus.
qs.x: The bus is on the main road and goes first; the car and truck then go together as their paths do not cross.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection if the traffic lights are not working?
o: The trolleybus and the motorcycle, followed by the bus and the passenger car.
The motorcycle, followed by the bus and the passenger car, then the trolleybus.
The bus and the passenger car, followed by the trolleybus and the motorcycle.
qs.x: With the lights off the intersection is unmarked and the right-hand rule applies: motorcycle first, bus and car together, trolleybus last.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The truck, followed by the tram and the bus, then the motorcycle and the passenger car.
The tram and the bus, followed by the motorcycle and the passenger car, then the truck.
qs.x: The truck on the main road goes first, then the tram and bus, and the motorcycle and car at the yield sign go last.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The ambulance, the tram, the motorcycle, the bus, the passenger car.
The motorcycle, the bus, followed by the tram and the ambulance at the same time, then the passenger car.
qs.x: The motorcycle and bus on the main road go first, then the tram and ambulance, and the car at the yield sign goes last.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The truck and the motorcycle, followed by the bus, then the trolleybus.
The truck and the bus, followed by the motorcycle, then the trolleybus.
qs.x: The truck and motorcycle on the main road go together, then the bus, and the trolleybus at the yield sign goes last.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The truck, the passenger car, the bus, the tanker truck.
The truck, the bus, the passenger car, the tanker truck.
qs.x: By the priority plate the truck goes first, then by the right-hand rule the car, the bus and finally the tanker.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The passenger car, the bus, the truck.
The bus, the truck, the passenger car.
The bus, the passenger car, the truck.
qs.x: The car at the yield sign goes last, and the bus goes before the truck by the right-hand rule.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The truck, the passenger car, the bus.
The bus, the truck, the passenger car.
The bus, the passenger car, the truck.
qs.x: By the priority sign with plate and the right-hand rule, the truck goes first, then the car, and the bus last.

qs.x: Our left turn does not conflict with the truck, which is turning right itself, so we pass through first.

qs.q: When turning right in this situation, you:

qs.x: The oncoming red car turns left and must yield to us turning right, so we go first.

qs.q: When turning left, you must yield the right of way to:
o: The drivers of the passenger car and tram A.
Only the driver of tram A.
qs.x: Turning left we must yield only to tram A, which crosses our path on the main road; tram B and the car do not obstruct us.

qs.q: If you continue straight ahead, you will:
o: Pass through after the passenger car.
qs.x: At the unmarked intersection the white car approaches from our right and has priority, so going straight we pass after it.

qs.q: When making a U-turn in this situation, you must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: In a U-turn we yield only to the oncoming car; the tanker on the side road yields to us on the main road.

qs.q: In this situation, are we required to avoid obstructing pedestrians?
qs.x: When turning we must not obstruct pedestrians crossing the road we are turning into.

qs.q: If there is a traffic jam immediately beyond the intersection, entering the intersection is permitted:
o: If you intend to continue straight ahead.
If you intend to turn or make a U-turn.
qs.x: With a jam beyond the junction you may enter only if turning or making a U-turn; going straight would leave you stuck in the intersection.

qs.q: We must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: We are on the main road (sign with plate) and vehicles from the crossing road must yield to us, so we yield to no one.

qs.q: When passing through the intersection, the driver must yield the right of way to:
o: The passenger car driver and the driver of tram B.
qs.x: Turning left we must yield to tram B on the main road, per the plate, and to the car next to it.

qs.q: When turning left in this situation, we must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: We are on the main road, which bends left (plate), so turning left we yield to no one.

qs.q: We must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: At the unmarked intersection the tram has priority as a rail vehicle and the truck approaches from our right, so we yield to both.

qs.q: We must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: We are on the main road (sign with plate), so we yield to no one.

qs.q: When passing through the intersection in this situation, are you required to yield the right of way?
qs.x: Nothing approaches from our right and the vehicle from the left has no priority, so we need not yield.

qs.q: When passing through the intersection in this situation, we:
o: Have the right of way and may proceed first.
Must yield the right of way to the tram driver.
Must yield the right of way to the truck driver.
Must yield the right of way to all other drivers.
qs.x: We are on the main road (priority sign), while the tram and truck are on the crossing road, so we have the right to go first.

qs.q: When entering a roundabout marked with the “Roundabout” sign, the driver of a vehicle:
o: Must yield the right of way to vehicles already circulating on the roundabout.
Has priority over vehicles already circulating on the roundabout.
qs.x: At a roundabout with the Roundabout sign, an entering driver must yield to vehicles already circulating.

qs.q: When turning left in this situation, we must yield the right of way to:
o: The bus driver and the passenger car driver.
qs.x: We face a yield sign and the bus and car are on the main road, so turning left we must yield to both.

qs.q: May the driver turn left in this situation?
o: Yes, provided they do not obstruct the truck driver.
qs.x: We face a yield sign, so we may turn left provided we do not obstruct the truck on the main road.

qs.q: When turning left in this situation, the driver:
o: Must yield the right of way.
Will pass through the intersection first.
qs.x: The black car approaches from our right and has priority, with no sign giving us priority, so turning left we must yield.

qs.q: These signs indicate that:
o: In 200 m, you must yield the right of way to traffic on the intersecting road.
You must yield the right of way to all vehicles along the next 200 m.
qs.x: The yield sign with the 200 m plate means that after 200 m you must give way to traffic on the intersecting road.

qs.q: When turning left at the second junction, the driver:
o: Must yield the right of way to the other drivers.
Must yield the right of way to the bus driver.
qs.x: A left turn must yield to oncoming traffic going straight, which here is the bus coming toward us.

qs.q: When proceeding straight ahead through the intersection, the driver:
o: Must yield the right of way to the tram.
Must yield the right of way to both drivers.
qs.x: A tram on its tracks has priority over road vehicles at an intersection, so going straight we yield to the tram in the picture.

qs.q: When turning left, to whom must the driver yield the right of way?
qs.x: With the priority-road sign and its turning plate, a left turn must yield to the oncoming bus on the main road.

qs.q: When entering this intersection, the driver:
o: Must yield the right of way to the truck driver.
Must yield the right of way to both drivers.
qs.x: At a roundabout, vehicles already on the circle have priority, so we yield to both the van and the motorcycle on the ring.

qs.q: When turning left, to whom must the driver yield the right of way?
qs.x: Under the Yield sign, turning left we must give way to both vehicles on the main road, the car and the bus.

qs.q: In this situation, we must yield the right of way to:
o: Only the truck driver approaching from the opposite direction.
qs.x: At an equal-priority crossroads we yield to the tanker truck coming from the right, and, turning left, also to the oncoming truck, so to both.

qs.q: When turning left, you:
o: Will pass through the intersection first.
Must yield the right of way.
qs.x: Nothing approaches from the right and the oncoming car is far away, while the white car on the left is no obstacle, so we go first when turning left.

qs.q: In this situation, we turn right by:
o: Yielding the right of way to the passenger car driver.
Yielding the right of way to both drivers.
qs.x: Turning right we take the nearest lane, so the white car on the left and the oncoming motorcycle do not interfere and we go first.

qs.q: When turning right, you:
o: Must yield the right of way.
qs.x: Turning right, no vehicle approaches from the right and the black car on the left does not cross our path, so we may go first.

qs.q: When turning left, you must yield the right of way to:
o: The bus driver and the motorcycle rider.
qs.x: Under the Yield sign, turning left we must give way to everyone on the main road: the bus, the motorcycle on the left and the white car on the right.

qs.q: When turning left, you:
o: Will proceed first, at the same time as the passenger car.
qs.x: With no signs the intersection is equal, so turning left we give way to the motorcycle approaching from the right and go after it.

qs.q: When proceeding straight ahead, you must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: Under the Yield sign, going straight we give way to both main-road vehicles, the pink bus and the white car on the right.

qs.q: Are we required to yield the right of way to the tram?
qs.x: The tram on its tracks approaching from the right has priority at the intersection, so we must yield.

qs.q: When is it permitted to turn right in this situation?
o: At the same time as the truck passes, provided you do not obstruct it.
qs.x: A right turn goes into the nearest lane, so we may turn while the truck passes as long as we do not hinder it.

qs.q: When proceeding straight ahead through the intersection, you must yield the right of way to:
o: Only the driver of tram A.
Only the driver of tram B.
qs.x: Both trams, A ahead and B crossing from the left, run on tracks through the intersection, so we must yield to both.

qs.q: When turning left, you must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: The priority-road sign and plate show the bus is on the main road, so turning left we yield only to it.

qs.q: Who will pass through the intersection first?
o: The traffic rules do not regulate this situation. The drivers should proceed with mutual consideration.
qs.x: Each vehicle is the other's right-hand obstacle, so the rules give no priority and the drivers must sort it out with mutual consideration.

qs.q: When must the driver avoid obstructing pedestrians?
qs.x: Whether turning left or right, the driver must not hinder pedestrians crossing the road being entered, like those at both crossings shown.

qs.q: When turning right, you must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: Turning right we must give way to both the pedestrians on the crossing and the cyclist riding straight on the bike lane.

qs.q: When turning left, you must yield the right of way to:
o: The passenger car and bus drivers.
qs.x: The plate shows the white car on the right is on the main road, so turning left we yield only to it.

qs.q: If a driver cannot determine whether a road has a paved surface (due to darkness, mud, snow, etc.) and there are no priority signs,:
o: The driver must assume that they are on a minor road.
The driver must follow the rules for negotiating an intersection of roads of equal priority.
qs.x: If the surface cannot be determined and there are no priority signs, assume you are on the secondary road.

qs.q: In this situation, we must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: At an equal intersection with no signs, turning left we give way to the car on the right and to the oncoming truck.

qs.q: We must yield the right of way to:
o: The bus and passenger car drivers.
qs.x: The plate under the Yield sign shows the bus and the white car are on the main road, while the motorcycle on the left is on the same secondary road as we are.

qs.q: When making a U-turn at this intersection,:
o: I will perform the manoeuvre first.
I must yield the right of way to the other driver.
qs.x: When making a U-turn we must give way to everyone whose path we cross, including the blue car approaching on the left.

qs.q: When proceeding straight ahead through an intersection while the traffic light is flashing yellow, we must:
o: Stop and wait for the green signal.
Yield the right of way to the passenger car driver.
Yield the right of way to the tram driver.
qs.x: A flashing yellow means the signal does not regulate, so the signs apply: the plate shows the car on the right is on the main road.

qs.q: When proceeding straight ahead,:
o: We may pass through the intersection first.
We must yield the right of way.
qs.x: There are no signs and the intersection is equal, so we must give way to the white truck approaching from the right.

qs.q: When making a U-turn, to whom must you yield the right of way?
qs.x: In the picture we yield to the truck because it is on the main road, while the passenger car comes from a minor road and must itself yield.

qs.q: When turning left, must we yield the right of way to the tram?
qs.x: Turning left we cross the tram tracks, and the tram on rails has priority, so we must yield.

qs.q: At this intersection, must we yield the right of way to the truck approaching from an unpaved road?
o: Yes, because it is approaching from our right.
No, because a paved road has priority over an unpaved road.
qs.x: A paved road is the priority road relative to an unpaved one, so the truck coming from the dirt road on the right must yield to us.

qs.q: When the traffic light is flashing yellow,:
o: We must wait for the green signal.
We will pass through the intersection after yielding the right of way to the driver of the horse-drawn cart.
We will pass through the intersection at the same time as the passenger car.
qs.x: With the signal flashing yellow the intersection is unregulated and equal, so we give way to the horse-drawn cart from the right.

qs.q: When turning left, we must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: The priority sign and plate show we are on the main road, which turns left, so we yield to no one.

qs.q: In this situation,:
o: We must yield the right of way to the truck driver.
We may pass through the intersection at the same time as the tram.
qs.x: With no signs the intersection is equal, so we yield to the blue truck on the right; the tram on the left does not hinder us.

qs.q: When passing through the intersection, we must yield the right of way to:
o: The motorcycle rider and the bus driver.
The bus and passenger car drivers.
qs.x: Under the Yield sign, going straight we give way to all main-road traffic: the bus, the motorcycle on the left and the yellow car on the right.

qs.q: In this situation, you must yield the right of way to:
o: The passenger car and tram drivers.
qs.x: The plate shows the main road bends right, so going straight we leave it and yield to the car on the right as well as to the tram on its rails.

qs.q: When turning left in this situation,:
o: You will pass through the intersection first.
You will enter the intersection, yield the right of way to the motorcycle rider, and then complete the manoeuvre.
qs.x: When turning left, the oncoming motorcycle going straight has priority, so we enter, let it pass and then complete the turn.

qs.q: When proceeding straight ahead through the intersection, you must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: Under the Yield sign, going straight we give way to both main-road vehicles, the tanker truck on the right and the car.

qs.q: In this situation,:
o: You will pass through the intersection first.
You will yield the right of way to the passenger car driver.
You will yield the right of way to both drivers.
qs.x: There are no signs and the intersection is equal, so turning left we yield to the white car approaching from the right.

qs.q: We must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: Under the Yield sign, turning left we give way to both main-road vehicles, the bus on the left and the oncoming car.

qs.q: At this intersection, you must:
o: Yield the right of way to the truck driver.
qs.x: There are no signs and the intersection is equal, so we yield to the truck approaching from the right.

qs.q: Must we yield the right of way to the tram driver?
qs.x: A tram on its rails has priority over road vehicles at the intersection, so we must yield.

qs.q: When turning left, we must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: On the main road the car on the right does not hinder us, but a left turn must give way to the oncoming truck going straight.

qs.q: At this intersection, you must:
qs.x: Nothing approaches from the right and the dark car is far away on the left, so we go first.

qs.q: When proceeding straight ahead, must we yield the right of way to the tram?
qs.x: A tram has priority over non-rail vehicles where paths cross, so going straight we must yield to it.

qs.q: Must we yield the right of way to the tram?
qs.x: There are no signs, and the tram approaching on rails from the left has priority, so we must yield.

qs.q: In this situation, turning right is permitted:
o: Only after the truck has passed.
At the same time as the truck, provided this does not obstruct the truck driver.
qs.x: A right turn goes into the right-hand lane, so we may turn at the same time as the truck on the left as long as we do not hinder it.

qs.q: To which tram driver must we yield the right of way?
qs.x: Both trams, A on the left and B on the right, run on rails through the intersection and have priority, so we must yield to both.

qs.q: When proceeding straight ahead, we must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: The plate shows the main road bends to the right, so going straight we yield to the white car on the right.

qs.q: In this situation, we must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: Under the Yield sign, turning left we give way to both main-road vehicles, the bus on the left and the blue truck on the right.

qs.q: Which sign requires drivers to yield the right of way to vehicles approaching from the left at an intersection?
qs.x: Only B (Give Way with a plate showing the main road coming from the left) requires yielding to traffic from the left; A merely warns of a side road.

qs.q: Which illustration shows the priority road?
o: Only the illustration on the left.
The illustrations at the bottom and on the left.
qs.x: The yellow diamond in the left image and the crossroads sign with a thick vertical bar and thin side road in the lower image show the priority road; the right image is a dead-end sign.

qs.q: Which illustration shows the priority road?
o: Only the illustration on the right.
The illustrations on the right and at the bottom.
qs.x: The yellow diamond in the right image and the side-road junction sign with a thick main bar in the lower image show the priority road; the blue sign on the left only gives priority to oncoming traffic.

qs.q: Which illustration shows the priority road?
qs.x: The upper images show the green motorway sign and the side-road junction warning sign with a thick main bar, both indicating priority; the lower blue sign only marks a one-way road.

qs.q: At an intersection, which road is considered the priority road?
o: A road with a hard surface (asphalt concrete, cement concrete, stone materials, etc.) in relation to an unpaved road.
A three-lane road in relation to a road with one lane in each direction.
An asphalt-concrete road in relation to a road paved with blocks.
qs.x: A paved road is the priority road over an unpaved one; number of lanes or paving type does not matter.

qs.q: Who is permitted to use a pedestrian path?
o: Only persons pushing bicycles or motorcycles.
Pedestrians and persons pushing bicycles or motorcycles.
qs.x: A pedestrian path is for pedestrians and for people pushing bicycles or motorcycles, not riding them.

qs.q: Who is permitted to use a path marked with the 'Cycle Track' sign?
o: Cyclists, as well as pedestrians where there are no pavements or pedestrian paths.
qs.x: A cycle track is for cyclists and moped riders, plus pedestrians where no pavement or path exists; motorcycles are not allowed.

qs.q: When turning right or left, must a bus driver yield the right of way to cyclists travelling on a cycle track?
o: No, because a bus is a larger vehicle and has priority.
Only if the cyclist is approaching from the right.
qs.x: Turning, a bus driver must always yield to cyclists on the cycle track; size gives no priority.

qs.q: Does a bus driver have priority over a cyclist at an uncontrolled crossing between a cycle track and a road outside an intersection?
qs.x: At an uncontrolled cycle-track crossing outside an intersection the road user has priority, so the bus has priority over the cyclist.

qs.q: Before turning or making a U-turn, a bus driver must position the bus in advance:
o: In any lane from which the manoeuvre can conveniently be performed.
In the second lane and perform the manoeuvre from that lane to allow a wider turning radius.
In the appropriate outermost lane of the carriageway for the intended direction of travel.
qs.x: Before turning or making a U-turn a bus must move in advance into the appropriate outermost lane.

qs.q: When may a bus driver turn without first moving into the appropriate outermost lane?
o: When the traffic lanes are separated by continuous road markings.
qs.x: When entering a roundabout there is no duty to take the outermost lane; continuous lines do not create an exception.

qs.q: May a bus driver cross a continuous line separating traffic lanes when turning if the bus is too large to complete the turn from the outermost lane?
o: Yes, if the driver uses the turn indicator and ensures safety.
No, crossing a continuous line is prohibited; the driver must change lanes in advance where the road markings permit it.
Yes, if the bus is a public transport vehicle.
qs.x: Crossing a continuous lane-dividing line is prohibited; the driver must change lanes earlier where the markings allow it.

qs.q: When may a bus driver turn without first moving into the appropriate outermost lane?
o: When the dimensions of the bus make it impossible to turn from the outermost lane.
When there are no horizontal road markings on that section of road.
qs.x: The outermost lane may be skipped only when the bus's size makes the turn impossible from it; missing markings are no excuse.

qs.q: From which lane must a bus driver turn if road signs or markings also permit the manoeuvre from lanes other than the outermost lane?
o: Only from the outermost lane, because a bus must always travel as far to the right as possible.
From any lane from which the manoeuvre is permitted by the road signs or markings.
qs.x: If signs or markings permit the manoeuvre from non-outermost lanes too, the bus may turn from any lane where it is allowed.

qs.q: From where must a bus driver turn left or make a U-turn if tram tracks run in the same direction at the same level on the left side of the carriageway, unless signs or markings prescribe otherwise?
o: From the leftmost lane of the carriageway, without entering the tram tracks.
From the tram tracks running in the same direction, provided this does not obstruct tram traffic.
qs.x: With same-direction tram tracks on the left at road level, a left turn or U-turn may be made from them provided it does not obstruct trams.

qs.q: How must a bus driver make a turn to comply with traffic rules?
o: The bus must not enter the side of the road intended for oncoming traffic when leaving the intersection of carriageways.
The bus must not enter the side of the road intended for oncoming traffic when leaving the intersection area.
qs.x: When leaving the intersection of carriageways after a turn, the bus must not end up on the oncoming-traffic side.

qs.q: A bus driver turns left onto a road with two lanes in the same direction. Which lane may the driver occupy on completing the turn?
o: Any lane, provided it is not a lane intended for oncoming traffic.
Only the leftmost lane, to avoid obstructing vehicles turning from the right.
Only the rightmost lane, because a bus must always travel as far to the right as possible.
qs.x: After a left turn any lane may be taken except one meant for oncoming traffic.

qs.q: A bus driver turns right onto a road with three lanes in the same direction. Which lane must the driver occupy on completing the turn?
o: Any lane, provided the bus does not enter the side intended for oncoming traffic.
Only the second or third lane, leaving the rightmost lane clear for other vehicles approaching a stop.
qs.x: After a right turn the bus should take the rightmost lane wherever possible.

qs.q: A bus driver is travelling through a three-lane roundabout. From which lane must the driver exit if road signs or markings do not prescribe otherwise?
qs.x: A bus must leave the roundabout from the rightmost lane unless signs or markings say otherwise.

qs.q: May a bus driver enter a reversible traffic lane immediately after turning if the traffic signal currently permits travel in that lane?
o: Yes, but only after a left turn.
Only if the bus is a public transport vehicle.
qs.x: Entering a reversible lane immediately after a turn is not permitted, even when its signal allows travel.

qs.q: How must a bus driver proceed when turning or making a U-turn, at or outside an intersection, if the dimensions of the bus make it impossible to manoeuvre from the appropriate outermost lane?
o: Switch on the hazard warning lights and perform the manoeuvre first, relying on the size of the bus.
Switch on the hazard warning lights, yield the right of way to vehicles approaching from the opposite direction, and then manoeuvre.
Switch on the hazard warning lights and yield the right of way to vehicles approaching in both the same and opposite directions.
qs.x: If the manoeuvre is impossible from the outermost lane, switch on the hazards and yield to vehicles from both the same and opposite directions.

qs.q: What must a bus driver do if a deceleration lane is provided before a turn?
o: Reduce speed in the main traffic lane before moving into the deceleration lane.
Move into the deceleration lane in advance and reduce speed only within that lane.
qs.x: Move into the deceleration lane early and slow down only within it, so the main flow is not obstructed.

qs.q: What must a bus driver do if an acceleration lane is provided?
o: Stop at the beginning of the acceleration lane, wait until the road is clear, and then enter the adjacent lane.
Travel along the acceleration lane and merge into the adjacent lane, yielding the right of way to vehicles already travelling on that road.
qs.x: Use the acceleration lane to build speed and merge into the adjacent lane, yielding to traffic already there, rather than stopping at its start.

qs.q: Is a bus permitted to reverse on a one-way road?
o: Yes, if it is safe and does not obstruct other road users.
Only if it is a scheduled-service bus.
qs.x: Reversing on one-way roads is prohibited for all buses, scheduled ones included.

qs.q: What is the purpose of a deceleration lane?
o: To allow a driver intending to turn to move into that lane in good time and reduce speed only within it.
To accommodate slow-moving vehicles that obstruct the main traffic flow.
To connect a motorway to an ordinary road.
qs.x: A deceleration lane lets a driver who intends to turn move over in good time and slow down only within it.

qs.q: Where are vehicles, including buses, prohibited from making a U-turn?
qs.x: U-turns are prohibited on one-way roads; they are not automatically banned at uncontrolled intersections.

qs.q: A bus is prohibited from making a U-turn:
o: Where visibility is less than 100 metres in at least one direction.
