qs.x: A U-turn is prohibited where visibility is under 100 m in at least one direction; at intersections it is allowed.

qs.q: A bus is prohibited from making a U-turn:
o: In built-up areas where visibility is 150 metres.
qs.x: A bus may not make a U-turn at railway level crossings; 150 m visibility in a built-up area does not prohibit it.

qs.q: A bus is prohibited from reversing:
o: When entering a road from an adjoining area.
qs.x: Reversing is prohibited at intersections, on pedestrian crossings and when leaving an adjoining area, so in all the cases listed.

qs.q: A bus is prohibited from reversing:
qs.x: Reversing is prohibited in tunnels; a steep uphill gradient alone does not prohibit it.

qs.q: A bus is prohibited from making a U-turn:
o: On and under bridges, viaducts and flyovers.
qs.x: U-turns are prohibited on and under bridges, viaducts and flyovers; a steep descent alone is no ban.

qs.q: Which driver has violated the traffic regulations?
o: The driver who travelled at 50 km/h in a residential zone.
The driver who yielded to a cyclist when turning off the road into adjacent premises.
Neither driver has violated the regulations.
qs.x: Neither violated: yielding to a cyclist when turning off the road is required, and 50 km/h is the normal built-up limit.

qs.q: What must a bus driver do if congestion beyond a pedestrian crossing would force the bus to stop on the crossing?
o: Do not enter the pedestrian crossing; stop before it.
The driver may stop on the crossing while the traffic signal is still permitting movement, provided the driver yields the right of way to all pedestrians crossing it.
qs.x: With a jam beyond a pedestrian crossing you must not enter it; stop before it even if the signal permits.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to enter a pedestrian crossing if congestion beyond it would force the bus to stop on the crossing?
o: Yes, if it is a scheduled-service bus approaching a bus stop.
No, the driver must stop before the pedestrian crossing.
Yes, if no pedestrians are present.
qs.x: With congestion beyond the crossing the bus must stop before it, whether or not it is a scheduled bus or pedestrians are present.

qs.q: What must a bus driver do when the traffic signal changes to permit movement at a signal-controlled pedestrian crossing?
o: Move off immediately, since pedestrians are prohibited from entering the crossing when the signal permits vehicles to proceed.
Allow pedestrians to finish crossing the carriageway in their chosen direction before proceeding.
qs.x: When the signal turns green, the driver must let pedestrians finish crossing before moving on.

qs.q: What must a bus driver do when the traffic signal changes to permit movement at a signal-controlled pedestrian crossing?
o: Move off while sounding the horn to encourage pedestrians to cross faster or turn back.
Allow pedestrians to finish crossing the carriageway in their chosen direction before proceeding.
qs.x: Hurrying pedestrians with the horn is not allowed; let them finish crossing first, then proceed.

qs.q: What must a bus driver do when approaching an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing?
o: Yield the right of way to pedestrians who are in the bus's traffic lane.
Not impede pedestrians crossing the carriageway.
qs.x: Approaching an uncontrolled crossing, the driver must not obstruct any pedestrians crossing, not only those in the bus's lane.

qs.q: If a vehicle has slowed down or stopped before an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing, the driver of a bus travelling in an adjacent lane may proceed:
o: If there are no pedestrians in the bus's lane.
Only after making sure there are no pedestrians in front of that vehicle.
In all of the above cases.
qs.x: You may pass a vehicle slowed or stopped at a crossing only after making sure there are no pedestrians in front of it.

qs.q: According to traffic regulations, what is a bus driver prohibited from doing on a motorway?
qs.x: On a motorway a bus is prohibited from both reversing and learner driving.

qs.q: In which direction may a tram proceed when a traffic officer has both arms extended sideways or lowered and the tram approaches from the officer's right or left?
o: Straight ahead and to the right.
qs.x: With the officer's arms out sideways or lowered, a tram may go straight ahead only.

qs.q: In which direction may a tram proceed when a traffic officer has the right arm extended forward and the tram approaches from the officer's left?
o: Straight ahead and to the left.
qs.x: With the officer's right arm forward and the tram approaching from his left, it may go to the left only.

qs.q: In which directions may a bus with a maximum permissible mass of 12 tonnes travel?
qs.x: The 10 t sign applies to trucks and a bus is not a truck, so the 12 t bus may go in all directions.

qs.q: In built-up areas, must drivers yield the right of way to public transport vehicles pulling away from designated and marked stops?
qs.x: In built-up areas drivers must yield to a public transport vehicle pulling away from a marked stop.

qs.q: Taking the vehicle's large dimensions into account, the driver is permitted to proceed:
o: Along either of the two paths.
qs.x: A right turn should end in the right-hand lane where possible, so path B is the permitted one.

qs.q: In which direction may the driver of the route-service bus travelling in a dedicated lane proceed in this situation?
qs.x: The vertical white bar of the T-shaped signal (top centre and bottom lights) permits straight ahead only.

qs.q: The bus driver must not obstruct:
o: Only the pedestrian crossing at the pedestrian crossing.
qs.x: The bus driver must not obstruct any pedestrians, not only those on a crossing or met when turning.

qs.q: When leaving an intersection after turning right or left, the bus driver must:
o: Not obstruct pedestrians crossing the carriageway.
Yield the right of way to cyclists travelling along a cycle track.
qs.x: Leaving the intersection after a turn, the driver must both not obstruct pedestrians and yield to cyclists on the cycle track.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to pass the truck by entering the lane for oncoming traffic?
qs.x: Passing a vehicle queued at a railway crossing by driving into the oncoming lane is prohibited.

qs.q: In this situation, must the driver of the intercity bus yield the right of way to the driver of the route- service bus pulling away?
qs.x: A route bus pulling away from a marked stop has priority, so the intercity bus must yield.

qs.q: Reversing in this situation is:
qs.x: Reversing is not barred here (no intersection, crossing or other prohibited place), so it is allowed if it is safe.

qs.q: In this situation, the driver of the public transport vehicle:
o: Has priority over the cyclist only.
Has priority over both the cyclist and the pedestrians.
Must yield the right of way to the cyclist and must not obstruct the pedestrians.
qs.x: A public transport vehicle turning here must yield to the cyclist and not obstruct the pedestrians.

qs.q: Outside built-up areas, must drivers yield the right of way to public transport vehicles pulling away from designated and marked stops?
qs.x: The priority for public transport leaving a stop applies only in built-up areas, not outside them.

qs.q: At an intersection of roads of equal priority, a tram driver must yield the right of way to:
o: The drivers of all vehicles approaching from the right.
Only the drivers of trams approaching from the right.
qs.x: At an equal intersection a tram yields only to trams from the right, since rail vehicles have priority over others.

qs.q: Travelling along the indicated path is, for the bus driver:
o: Permitted only when making a U-turn or turning left.
qs.x: The indicated path (left lane) is allowed for the bus only when turning left or making a U-turn.

qs.q: Must the tram driver yield the right of way to a bus operating on a scheduled route?
o: No, the driver is not required to yield.
qs.x: A tram is rail transport with priority and need not yield even to a bus on a scheduled route.

qs.q: On roads with four lanes for traffic travelling in the same direction, are public transport vehicles permitted to use the leftmost lane?
o: Permitted when turning left or making a U-turn.
qs.x: On a four-lane one-direction road public transport may use the leftmost lane only to turn left or make a U-turn.

qs.q: Must the driver of the route-service bus yield the right of way to the passenger car before moving off in this situation?
o: No, the driver is not required to yield.
qs.x: A route bus pulling away from a stop has priority over the passenger car, so it need not yield.

qs.q: If a traffic controller extends both arms sideways, which public transport vehicles are permitted to proceed straight ahead only?
qs.x: With the officer's arms extended sideways, of the public transport vehicles only trams are limited to going straight.

qs.q: Must the bus driver yield the right of way to the cyclist?
o: No, if the bus operates on a scheduled route.
No, if the bus is large and is travelling straight ahead.
qs.x: The cyclist crosses the bus's path and the bus must yield, whether it is on a route, large or going straight.

qs.q: Must the bus driver yield the right of way to the cyclist?
o: No, if the bus is large.
No, if the bus operates on a scheduled route.
qs.x: The bus must yield to the cyclist, since large size or route service gives no priority.

qs.q: Must the bus driver yield the right of way to the tram?
o: No, because the bus is approaching the tram from the right.
qs.x: The bus must yield to the tram because rail vehicles have priority; approaching from the right changes nothing.

qs.q: If a bus driver enters an intersection while the traffic light displays a permissive signal, the driver:
o: Must stop regardless of the traffic light signals.
Must comply with any traffic light signal where a stop line is marked.
qs.x: A driver who entered on green must obey the next signal where a stop line is marked, rather than stopping regardless of signals.

qs.q: Before turning or making a U-turn, a bus driver must move into the appropriate outermost lane in advance, except:
o: When making a U-turn at an intersection.
When turning right, provided that no obstruction is caused to other vehicles.
When the bus's dimensions or other circumstances make this impossible.
qs.x: The exception to taking the outermost lane first is when it is impossible because of the bus's dimensions or other reasons.

qs.q: At intersections of roads of equal priority, which public transport vehicles have priority?
qs.x: At equal intersections only trams, as rail vehicles, have priority among public transport.

qs.q: Under this traffic light signal, tram traffic is:
o: Permitted to the right or left.
qs.x: The three top white lights (a horizontal bar) prohibit tram movement in all directions.

qs.q: For a public bus travelling in a dedicated lane, movement is prohibited:
o: When turning right, turning left or making a U-turn.
qs.x: The horizontal bar of three top white lights prohibits a bus in the dedicated lane from moving in any direction.

qs.q: In which direction is a public bus travelling in a dedicated lane permitted to proceed?
o: To the right or left only.
qs.x: The vertical white bar (top centre and bottom lights) permits straight ahead only.

qs.q: A bus driver travelling in the leftmost lane intends to change to the right lane. Which illustration shows a situation in which the driver must yield the right of way to the passenger car?
qs.x: When changing lanes you must yield to the vehicle in the target lane whether or not it signals, so in both pictures.

qs.q: You intend to turn left. To whom must you yield the right of way?
qs.x: Turning left, you must yield to the oncoming bus going straight and to pedestrians on the road you enter.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to proceed?
o: The bus and the passenger car.
qs.x: The officer's signals override the traffic light, and with his arm out the bus and the car on his side may proceed.

qs.q: Who must yield the right of way in this situation?
o: The driver of the bus moving off.
The driver of the passenger car.
qs.x: The driver moving off (the bus) must yield to vehicles already travelling on the road.

qs.q: You are driving a route-service bus and intend to turn left in this situation. In what order will you pass through the intersection?
qs.x: Turning left, the bus yields to the oncoming car and, because of the give-way sign, to the truck on the crossing road, so it goes third.

qs.q: You are driving a route-service bus and intend to turn left, while the tram is proceeding straight ahead. Who has priority?
o: The bus driver, because route-service vehicles always have priority over trams when manoeuvring at intersections.
qs.x: A bus turning left must yield to the tram going straight; being a route vehicle gives no priority over a tram.

qs.q: You are driving a route-service bus. Which is the correct order of passage through the intersection in this situation?
o: The truck first, followed by the tram and the bus simultaneously.
The truck, then the tram, then the bus.
The tram, then the truck, then the bus.
qs.x: The tram has rail priority and the truck is on the bus's right, so the order is tram, truck, bus.

qs.q: You are driving a bus. Which is the correct order of passage through the intersection in this situation?
o: The passenger car, then the tram, then the motorcycle, then the bus.
The tram, then the passenger car, then the bus, then the motorcycle.
qs.x: By priority the tram goes first, then the car on the main road, then the bus, and the motorcycle last.

qs.q: In what order will the bus pass through the intersection?
qs.x: The bus is on the minor road (give-way sign) while the trolleybus and car are on the main road, so the bus goes last.

qs.q: In what order will the tram pass through the intersection?
o: First, simultaneously with the blue passenger car.
qs.x: The tram goes second: the blue car passes first and the tram must yield to it.

qs.q: In what order will the tram pass through the intersection?
o: Second, together with the blue passenger car.
qs.x: The tram goes third, after the blue car and the motorcycle that have priority over it here.

qs.q: Which vehicles are prohibited from proceeding?
o: The red and white passenger cars.
The blue, green and white passenger cars.
The white, blue and yellow passenger cars.
qs.x: The controller stands with arms outstretched, so traffic facing his chest or back is prohibited: the blue, green and white cars must stop while the red and yellow may proceed.

qs.q: Which drivers are permitted to proceed straight ahead?
o: The passenger car and truck drivers.
qs.x: The controller's right arm is stretched forward: the car on his left side may go in all directions, the truck and bus on his right side and back only turn right, and the motorcycle facing his chest must stop.

qs.q: Which driver must yield the right of way?
qs.x: The car has a green light while the tram has red with a green right arrow, so the tram turning right must give way to the car going on green.

qs.q: If the traffic controller extends their right arm forward, non-rail vehicles are permitted to proceed:
o: From the left side, to the left and in the opposite direction (making a U-turn).
From the right side, only to the right.
From the left side, in all directions.
From behind, only to the right.
qs.x: With the controller's right arm extended forward, traffic from his left side may go in all directions.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The tram and the bus, followed by the passenger car.
The tram, the passenger car, the bus.
The passenger car, followed by the tram and the bus.
qs.x: The car has the main green light and goes first, while the tram and bus, on red with only a green arrow, must give way to it.

qs.q: Which answer correctly identifies the vehicles permitted to proceed?
o: The passenger car and the truck.
qs.x: From the controller's stance only the red passenger car's side may move, while the motorcycle, truck and bus are on prohibited sides.

qs.q: This signal given by the traffic controller means that movement is permitted for:
o: The blue and green cars, but prohibited for the red, yellow and white cars.
The blue, red and green cars, but prohibited for the yellow and white cars.
qs.x: With arms spread the controller allows traffic from his sides, so the blue, red and green vehicles may go while the yellow and white face his chest or back and stop.

qs.q: Which vehicles may turn right?
qs.x: The controller has his arms spread, so the red and green cars on his sides may go straight or turn right, while those facing his chest or back must stop.

qs.q: Movement is permitted:
o: To the right at the first junction.
To the right at the second junction.
To the right at both the first and second junctions.
qs.x: The controller's right arm is stretched forward, so from his right side or back only a right turn is allowed; the red car may only turn right at the first opening.

qs.q: Movement is permitted:
o: To the right at the first junction.
Straight ahead and to the right at the first junction.
qs.x: With the controller's right arm stretched forward, the red car on that side may only turn right at the first opening, not go straight.

qs.q: This traffic light prohibits movement:
o: Straight ahead and to the left.
Straight ahead and to the right.
qs.x: The top-left light is off, so only movement to the left is prohibited; straight and right are allowed.

qs.q: If the traffic controller has both arms extended sideways or lowered, non-rail vehicles are permitted to proceed:
o: From the front and rear, only to the right.
From the left and right sides, straight ahead and to the right.
From the left and right sides, straight ahead only.
qs.x: With the controller's arms lowered or out to the sides, traffic from his left and right may go straight or right.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to proceed?
o: The green, red and white cars.
qs.x: The controller has his arms spread: the yellow and red cars at his sides may go, while the blue, green and white at his chest or back may not.

qs.q: At which traffic light signal may the driver complete the U-turn?
qs.x: The car is waiting at the second stop line (marked STOP), so it may complete the U-turn only on the green signal.

qs.q: What does the combination of red and amber traffic light signals mean?
o: Movement is prohibited and the green signal is about to appear.
A vehicle with special audible warning signals and flashing beacons activated is approaching the intersection.
qs.x: Red and yellow lit together prohibit movement and warn that the green signal is about to come on.

qs.q: In which picture is the driver making the turn correctly?
o: In the picture on the left.
In the picture on the right.
qs.x: In the left image the driver follows the controller's signal, while in the right image the controller's arm position does not allow that turn.

qs.q: When the traffic light shows green, must the tram driver yield the right of way to vehicles approaching from other directions?
o: No, the driver is not required to yield.
qs.x: With the main light red, the green arrow only allows the turn, and the tram operator must give way to vehicles from other directions.

qs.q: This traffic light is used to control traffic:
o: Across the entire width of the carriageway.
In lanes where the direction of traffic may be reversed.
Only in lanes designated for public transport vehicles.
qs.x: The red cross and green arrow form a reversible-lane signal, which regulates lanes where the direction of traffic can be switched.

qs.q: If the traffic controller extends their right arm forward, non-rail vehicles approaching from the controller’s left side are permitted to proceed:
qs.x: With his right arm forward, traffic from the controller's left may go in all directions.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to proceed under the traffic light signal shown?
o: The tram and the yellow and red cars.
qs.x: The green arrows allow straight and right only, so the yellow car in the middle lane and the red car in the right lane may go, but the blue car and the tram on the left may not.

qs.q: Movement is permitted for:
qs.x: The motorcycle is at the side of the controller whose arms are spread and may go, while the car and tram facing his chest must stop.

qs.q: If the traffic controller has both arms extended sideways or lowered, non-rail vehicles approaching from the controller’s left and right sides are permitted to proceed:
o: Straight ahead and to the right.
qs.x: With his arms out or lowered, traffic from his left and right may go straight or right.

qs.q: Which vehicle has the right of way?
qs.x: The tram has a green signal, and a tram on rails has priority over the car, so the tram goes first.

qs.q: Movement is prohibited for:
o: The white, blue and green cars.
qs.x: The controller has his arms spread: the blue, green and white cars at his chest or back are prohibited, while the red and yellow may proceed.

qs.q: When this traffic light shows a red signal, movement is prohibited:
o: Across the entire width of the carriageway.
In the lane above which the traffic light is installed.
qs.x: The red cross prohibits traffic only in the lane over which the signal is mounted, not across the whole roadway.

qs.q: What does a flashing circular green traffic light signal mean?
o: It indicates that entering the intersection is prohibited.
It permits movement and indicates that the green signal is about to end and a prohibitory signal will appear shortly.
qs.x: A flashing green permits movement and warns that a prohibiting signal will come on shortly.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The tram, the red car, then the green car.
The red car, followed by the tram and the green car simultaneously.
The tram and the green car simultaneously, followed by the red car.
qs.x: The red car with its green signal goes first, while the tram and green car, on red with only a green straight arrow, must wait and then go together.

qs.q: Which answer correctly identifies the vehicles permitted to proceed?
qs.x: The controller's right arm is stretched forward: from his left side cars and the motorcycle may go in all directions, while the tram may only turn left, not go straight.

qs.q: If the traffic controller extends their right arm forward, non-rail vehicles approaching from the controller’s left side are permitted to proceed:
o: Straight ahead and to the left.
qs.x: With his right arm forward, traffic from his left may proceed in all directions.

qs.q: Movement is prohibited for:
o: The blue-and-yellow car proceeding straight ahead, and the red car proceeding straight ahead or turning right.
qs.x: The controller's arms are lowered, so traffic from the sides may go straight or right; only the blue-and-yellow car's left turn is prohibited.

qs.q: In which direction is movement permitted?
o: Straight ahead and to the right at the first junction.
To the right at the first junction.
To the right at the second junction.
To the right at both the first and second junctions.
qs.x: With the main light red and only the green right arrow lit, only a right turn at the first opening is allowed.

qs.q: Which car will pass through the intersection first?
qs.x: The green truck has a green light while the red and blue cars are on red with only a right arrow, so the green truck goes first.

qs.q: In which picture is the driver turning correctly?
o: In the picture on the left.
In the picture on the right.
qs.x: In the left image the driver follows the controller's signal, while in the right image the controller's arm position does not allow that turn.

qs.q: The red car will pass through the intersection:
qs.x: The red car turning left on green must give way to the oncoming green and yellow cars and the tram, so it goes last.

qs.q: This traffic light is used to control:
o: Tram traffic and other public transport vehicles travelling in designated lanes.
qs.x: The T-shaped white signal controls trams and other public transport in dedicated lanes.

qs.q: The car will pass through the intersection:
qs.x: The blue car has a green light while the tram is on red with only a right arrow and must yield, so the car goes first.

qs.q: Movement is permitted for:
o: The blue-and-yellow car to proceed straight ahead and the red car to turn right.
The red car to proceed straight ahead or turn right, and the blue-and-yellow car to proceed straight ahead.
Both cars to proceed straight ahead only.
qs.x: The controller's arms are lowered, so the red car may go straight and right and the blue-and-yellow car straight, as the arrows show.

qs.q: Movement is permitted for:
o: The tram and the red car.
qs.x: From the controller's arm position only the red car's side may move, while the motorcycle, tram and truck are on prohibited sides.

qs.q: Is it permitted to follow the indicated path when the reversible-lane traffic lights are switched off?
o: Yes, for the purpose of overtaking.
Yes, if there are no oncoming vehicles.
qs.x: When the reversible-lane signals are off, entering the left lane along the arrow shown is prohibited because oncoming traffic may use it.

qs.q: In this situation, which vehicles are permitted to proceed?
o: The passenger car straight ahead, the patrol car in all directions, and the bus to the right only.
Only the patrol car, in all directions.
The patrol car in all directions and the bus to the right only.
qs.x: The controller's signals override the traffic light: with his right arm stretched forward the bus may only turn right, while the patrol car with its beacon and siren may go in all directions.

qs.q: What does the traffic light signal indicate?
o: Drivers must comply with the road signs when passing through the intersection.
Drivers must wait for a permissive traffic light signal.
qs.x: The red-plus-yellow combination means green is about to come on, so the driver must wait for the permissive signal.

qs.q: Which vehicle must yield the right of way?
o: The motorcycle and the passenger car.
qs.x: The bus under the Yield sign must give way to the motorcycle and the car going straight on the main road.

qs.q: Which drivers are permitted to proceed along the indicated paths?
o: The passenger car and bus drivers.
qs.x: The controller's arms are lowered: only the bus at his side turning right may go, while the truck and the U-turning taxi face his chest or back and must stop.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The tram, the passenger car, the bus.
The passenger car, the tram, the bus.
The passenger car, the bus, the tram.
qs.x: The car goes straight first on green, while the tram and bus, on red with a green right arrow, yield, and the tram has priority over the bus.

qs.q: In this situation, is the bus driver permitted to proceed straight ahead?
o: Yes, if the bus is operating on an established route.
qs.x: In this situation the bus may not proceed straight ahead, and being on a route does not change that.

qs.q: In which direction may the driver proceed?
o: To the right at the first junction.
To the right at both the first and second junctions.
To the left at the first junction.
qs.x: With the main light red and only the green right arrow lit, only a right turn at the first opening is allowed.

qs.q: When turning right, the driver must yield the right of way to:
o: Both the pedestrians and the cyclist.
The driver may proceed without stopping.
qs.x: Turning right, even on green, we must yield to both the pedestrians on the crossing and the cyclist riding straight past the bicycle-path sign.

qs.q: In which order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
o: The tram, the bus, the truck, the motorcycle.
The bus, the truck, the tram, the motorcycle.
The bus, followed by the tram and the motorcycle, then the truck.
qs.x: The bus goes first, then the tram and the motorcycle, which do not interfere, go together, and the truck, crossing the tram tracks, goes last.

qs.q: In this situation, to which tram driver must you yield the right of way?
qs.x: Although our signal is green, our path crosses the tram tracks and a tram on rails has priority, so we must yield to both trams A and B.

qs.q: Which driver has the right of way?
qs.x: The bus is stopped by the signal for its direction while the car proceeds on a permissive light, so the car has the right-of-way.

qs.q: When turning left in this situation,:
o: I will yield the right of way to the tram.
I will proceed through the intersection first.
qs.x: The green left arrow lets us turn while the tram's white horizontal lights stop it, so we go first.

qs.q: What should you do in this situation?
o: Enter the intersection and proceed through it after yielding the right of way to the passenger car driver.
Wait before the stop line until the passenger car driver has passed through the intersection.
qs.x: On green, turning left we enter the intersection, give way to the oncoming car going straight, then complete the turn.

qs.q: When turning right in this situation, must you yield the right of way?
qs.x: With a red light the green right arrow only permits the turn, and we must still yield to traffic from other directions, here the car on the right.

qs.q: Is turning right permitted in this situation?
o: Yes, provided you do not obstruct pedestrians.
qs.x: The controller's signal permits the right turn, but we must not hinder the pedestrians on the crossing.

qs.q: Must you yield the right of way to the tram driver in this situation?
o: No, you are not required to.
qs.x: Even on a green signal you must yield to the tram, which has priority where your paths cross.

qs.q: When the green traffic light comes on, the driver:
o: Must yield the right of way to the truck driver.
qs.x: When green comes on we must let vehicles still clearing the intersection finish, so we yield to the truck that is still crossing.

qs.q: At this intersection, the driver:
o: Will proceed through the intersection first.
Must yield the right of way to the tram.
qs.x: The tram signal stops the tram with white lights while our signal permits movement, so we go first.

qs.q: When proceeding straight ahead through the intersection, the driver:
o: Must yield the right of way to the tram.
Must yield the right of way to both drivers.
qs.x: Even with our light green, the tram crossing the intersection on its rails has priority, so going straight we must yield to it.

qs.q: When turning, the driver must yield the right of way to:
qs.x: Turning right, even on green, we must yield to both the pedestrians on the crossing and the cyclist on the bicycle path.

qs.q: When turning right, must you yield the right of way to the driver approaching from the opposite direction?
qs.x: Turning right we enter the right-hand lane while the oncoming car stays in its own, so there is no need to yield to it.

qs.q: When proceeding straight ahead through the intersection,:
o: We must yield the right of way to the passenger car driver.
qs.x: Our light is red with only a straight green arrow, so we must yield to the blue car on the left, which is crossing on green.

qs.q: When turning left, you must yield the right of way to:
o: Both the passenger car driver and pedestrians.
qs.x: Turning left on green, we must yield to the oncoming car going straight and to the pedestrians crossing the road we enter.

qs.q: Is turning right permitted in this situation?
o: Yes, provided you do not obstruct the pedestrian.
qs.x: The controller's signal allows the right turn, but we must not hinder the pedestrians on the crossing.

qs.q: When turning left,:
o: You must yield the right of way to the tram driver.
You may proceed through the intersection first.
qs.x: When turning left you must yield to a tram on the tram tracks because it has priority.

qs.q: Which road signs do not apply when their requirements conflict with traffic light signals?
qs.x: Priority signs do not apply when they conflict with traffic signals; the signals govern.

qs.q: In this situation, who must yield the right of way?
qs.x: The tram has a red light with only a green arrow, so it must give way to the car proceeding on green.

qs.q: When turning right,:
o: We must yield the right of way to the tram driver.
We will proceed through the intersection first.
qs.x: The controller's signal lets us turn right while the tram on the other side is held back, so we go first.

qs.q: You intend to turn left. To whom must you yield the right of way?
o: Both the passenger car driver and the tram driver.
qs.x: Turning left on green, we must give way to both the oncoming car going straight and the tram.

qs.q: When turning left,:
o: I will complete the manoeuvre without stopping.
After entering the intersection, I will stop before the second stop line and wait for the green traffic light.
qs.x: After entering the junction, stop at the second stop line and wait for green, as the road you turn onto has its own signal.

qs.q: Must we yield the right of way to the truck driver in this situation?
qs.x: Turning left on green, we must still give way to the oncoming truck going straight.

qs.q: When turning left in this situation, you must:
o: Enter the intersection and wait for the traffic officer’s signal permitting a left turn.
Stop before the stop line marking and wait for the traffic officer’s signal permitting a left turn.
Enter the intersection and proceed through it after yielding the right of way to the driver approaching from the opposite direction.
qs.x: The traffic light is dark and the controller directs traffic, so to turn left we stop before the stop line and wait for his permissive signal.

qs.q: When may you proceed through the intersection without yielding the right of way to another road user?
qs.x: Going straight on green we yield to no one, whereas turning requires giving way to pedestrians or oncoming vehicles.

qs.q: When turning right, you must:
o: Stop before the stop line to avoid obstructing pedestrians.
Enter the intersection and stop to avoid obstructing pedestrians.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.
qs.x: Turning right on green, pedestrians and a cyclist cross the road we enter, so we move into the intersection and stop so as not to hinder them.

qs.q: When turning right,:
o: You must yield the right of way to the passenger car driver.
You may proceed through the intersection first.
qs.x: The controller's signal permits our right turn and the car on the right by the U-turn marking does not hinder us, so we go first.

qs.q: After the traffic light displays a signal permitting movement, we may enter the intersection:
o: Only when making a turn or a U-turn.
qs.x: There is a queue ahead, so going straight we would get stuck and block the intersection, while entering to turn or make a U-turn is acceptable on green.

qs.q: When the traffic light turns green, we must:
o: Make sure that there are no pedestrians who have not finished crossing in the part of the pedestrian crossing that is not visible.
Start moving immediately in accordance with the traffic light signal.
qs.x: The truck blocks part of the crossing, so when green comes on we must check that no pedestrians are still crossing in the hidden part.

qs.q: When making a U-turn in this situation, must we yield the right of way to the other driver?
o: No, we are not required to.
qs.x: In a U-turn we must give way to traffic the controller lets move, here the blue car coming from the left.

qs.q: In which direction may the driver continue in this situation?
qs.x: The controller's arm lets us continue only straight, and the blue arrow sign on the right shows that street is one-way against us, so no right turn.

qs.q: Which driver may continue driving?
qs.x: The controller's signal overrides the red light, and his outstretched arm allows movement from the side where both the minibus and the car stand.

qs.q: Crossing the railway level crossing is:
qs.x: The flashing white-lunar light at the crossing permits movement, so crossing the railroad is allowed.

qs.q: Proceeding through the intersection is:
o: Permitted if the driver cannot stop before the stop line without braking sharply.
qs.x: Proceeding is permitted if the driver cannot stop at the stop line without harsh braking, as when the officer has just raised his arm.

qs.q: Where must you stop in accordance with the traffic light signal?
qs.x: There is no stop line or crossing, and the STOP plate is on the signal itself, so on red we stop before the traffic signal.

qs.q: Turning left is permitted:
o: From the lane indicated in the illustration.
qs.x: A left turn is allowed from the lane shown in the picture; the reversible lane is closed by the X above it and cannot be used.

qs.q: Driving is permitted:
qs.x: The traffic controller faces us side-on with arms lowered, so driving straight and to the right is allowed.

qs.q: Driving is permitted:
qs.x: Our lane carries only a right-turn arrow, so only a right turn is allowed from it.

qs.q: The arrows shown on the green traffic light signal indicate that:
o: Traffic moving to the right is controlled by an additional traffic light section.
qs.x: An arrow shown on the green signal means traffic in that direction is controlled by an additional signal section.

qs.q: Is overtaking the truck permitted?
qs.x: A red X is lit above our lane, so entering the reversible lane and passing are prohibited.

qs.q: In which direction may the driver proceed in this situation?
o: The driver must wait for a signal permitting movement.
Left or by making a U-turn.
qs.x: From the left lane, a green left arrow permits both a left turn and a U-turn.

qs.q: Entering the reversible traffic lane in this situation is:
qs.x: A green arrow is lit above our lane, so driving in this reversible lane is permitted.

qs.q: Proceeding straight ahead from the indicated lane is:
o: Permitted only after the main green traffic light signal comes on.
qs.x: Only a right arrow is lit in the extra section while the main signal is red, so going straight is prohibited.

qs.q: Driving is permitted:
qs.x: The controller faces us chest-on with the right arm extended forward, so all directions are allowed.

qs.q: Driving in this situation is:
qs.x: The controller has his back to us with the arm extended, so traffic from our side is prohibited.

qs.q: Before moving off or performing a manoeuvre, a bus driver must make sure that:
o: There are no other vehicles in the same lane at that moment.
The manoeuvre is safe and will not obstruct other road users.
The manoeuvre can be completed as quickly as possible to clear the road.
qs.x: Before moving off or manoeuvring, the driver must make sure it is safe and will not obstruct other road users.

qs.q: Is it permitted to travel on tram tracks on the left-hand side of the carriageway, at the same level and in the same direction as traffic, when all lanes in that direction are occupied?
o: Yes, provided that the relevant road signs do not prescribe a different traffic arrangement and that this does not obstruct tram traffic.
Only if the vehicle is overtaking.
No, it is prohibited in all cases because tram tracks are intended exclusively for rail vehicles.
qs.x: Driving on same-direction tram tracks on the left is allowed if all lanes are occupied, signs say nothing else and trams are not obstructed.

qs.q: If the carriageway is divided into lanes by road markings, when may a driver cross the broken lines separating the lanes?
o: At any time, a driver may cross or drive along a broken line if there are no other vehicles on the road.
qs.x: Broken lane lines may be crossed only when changing lanes; driving along them is not allowed even on an empty road.

qs.q: What distance must a bus driver maintain from the vehicle travelling ahead?
o: A sufficient distance to avoid a collision with that vehicle.
A distance that allows other vehicles overtaking the bus to complete the manoeuvre and move back into the lane ahead of it without obstruction.
qs.x: The distance to the vehicle ahead must be enough to avoid a collision.

qs.q: What lateral clearance must a bus driver maintain from a vehicle travelling alongside the bus?
o: Sufficient clearance to avoid a collision with that vehicle.
qs.x: Lateral clearance must be sufficient to avoid a collision; no fixed figure is set.

qs.q: Outside built-up areas, on two-way roads with one lane in each direction, what distance must drivers of buses longer than 7 metres maintain from the vehicle ahead?
o: At least 50 metres, regardless of speed and road conditions.
A distance sufficient to allow drivers overtaking them to move back into their original lane without obstruction if necessary.
A distance at their discretion, taking road safety into account.
qs.x: A driver of a bus over 7 m long must keep a gap that lets overtaking vehicles pull back into the lane ahead if needed.

qs.q: Before overtaking, a bus driver must, among other requirements, make sure that:
o: After completing the overtaking manoeuvre, the bus can return to its original lane without obstructing the vehicle being overtaken.
The driver of the vehicle ahead has noticed the manoeuvre and is yielding the right of way by reducing speed.
qs.x: Before overtaking, make sure you can return to your lane without obstructing the vehicle overtaken; you cannot count on it giving way.

qs.q: Before overtaking, a bus driver must, among other requirements, make sure that:
o: Vehicles behind are maintaining a sufficient distance and the vehicle ahead has already begun to slow down to give way.
The vehicle travelling behind in the same lane has not begun overtaking, and the vehicle ahead has not signalled an intention to overtake, turn left or make a U-turn.
qs.x: Before overtaking, ensure the vehicle behind has not begun to overtake and the one ahead has not signalled to overtake, turn left or U-turn.

qs.q: Is it permitted to overtake non-rail vehicles on the right?
o: Yes, if the driver of the vehicle ahead has signalled a left turn and begun the manoeuvre.
No, overtaking on the right is prohibited in all cases because overtaking must be carried out exclusively on the left for safety reasons.
qs.x: A non-rail vehicle may be overtaken on the right when the driver ahead has signalled left and begun the turn.

qs.q: Outside built-up areas, if a large bus is difficult for other vehicles to overtake, what must its driver do?
o: Keep as far to the right as possible and, if necessary, stop to allow vehicles behind to pass.
Switch on the hazard warning lights and continue at the same speed until reaching a section where overtaking is permitted.
qs.x: If a large bus is hard to overtake outside built-up areas it must keep right and, if necessary, stop to let traffic behind pass.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to overtake several vehicles in a single manoeuvre?
o: Yes, if the manoeuvre is safe for other road users.
No, the driver must return to the original lane after overtaking each vehicle before beginning the next overtaking manoeuvre.
qs.x: Overtaking several vehicles at once is allowed if the manoeuvre is safe for other road users.

qs.q: Is it permitted to begin overtaking a vehicle whose driver has signalled a left turn and begun the manoeuvre?
o: Only if overtaking is carried out on the right.
qs.x: A vehicle that has signalled left and begun turning may be overtaken only on the right.

qs.q: Are U-turns prohibited where visibility is less than 100 metres in at least one direction?
qs.x: U-turns where visibility is under 100 m are prohibited on all roads, in and outside built-up areas.

qs.q: What must a bus driver do to ensure safety when reversing?
o: Switch on the position lights and reverse at the lowest possible speed.
Seek assistance from other persons if necessary.
qs.x: When reversing, the driver should seek help from other people if needed; continuous honking is not required.

qs.q: How must a driver determine the number of traffic lanes if road markings and mandatory direction signs are absent?
o: In the absence of markings, the road is considered to have one lane regardless of its width.
The number of lanes is determined by the width of the carriageway, the dimensions of vehicles and the necessary lateral clearance between them.
qs.x: Without markings the number of lanes is judged from the carriageway width, vehicle sizes and the clearances needed between them.

qs.q: On roads with three or more lanes in the same direction, when may buses operating regular services use the leftmost lane?
o: In heavy traffic, if all other lanes are occupied.
Only to overtake other vehicles or pass an obstruction.
Only to turn left or make a U-turn.
qs.x: On roads with three or more lanes a scheduled-service bus may use the leftmost lane only to turn left or make a U-turn.

qs.q: If a bus cannot exceed 40 km/h for technical reasons, may its driver leave the rightmost lane to stop on the left?
o: No, vehicles travelling at no more than 40 km/h must remain exclusively in the rightmost lane and may not leave it.
Yes, if the bus stops at a location where stopping is permitted under the traffic rules.
qs.x: A bus limited to 40 km/h may leave the right lane to stop on the left if stopping is permitted at that place.

qs.q: In heavy traffic within a built-up area, when is changing lanes permitted?
o: Only when turning left or right.
Only before passing an obstruction or stopping.
qs.x: In heavy traffic in a built-up area, changing lanes is allowed in all the cases listed: turning, U-turn, passing an obstruction and stopping.

qs.q: Is it prohibited for buses to travel on road shoulders, pavements and pedestrian paths even when no other route is available?
o: Buses operated by road maintenance and municipal services may do so, provided they do not obstruct pedestrians and ensure road safety.
qs.x: Buses may not use shoulders, pavements or pedestrian paths, except road-maintenance and municipal-service buses that do not obstruct pedestrians.

qs.q: Which part of the carriageway must buses use outside built-up areas?
o: As close as possible to the right-hand edge of the carriageway.
Any lane except the leftmost lane.
At the driver’s discretion, provided road safety is ensured.
qs.x: Outside built-up areas buses must keep as close as possible to the right-hand edge of the carriageway.

qs.q: Which lane must buses use on a road marked with the 'Road for Motor Vehicles' sign within a built- up area?
o: As close as possible to the right-hand edge of the carriageway.
Any lane except the leftmost lane.
qs.x: On a road for motor vehicles, buses must keep as close as possible to the right-hand edge of the carriageway.

qs.q: Which lanes may buses providing regular passenger services use on a road with three lanes in the same direction?
o: Only the first and second lanes, unless turning left or making a U-turn.
Any lane when traffic is heavy and the other lanes are occupied.
qs.x: Scheduled buses on a three-lane road use only the first and second lanes, the third only for a left turn or U-turn.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to overtake a vehicle that has slowed down immediately before an intersection?
o: Yes, if no pedestrians are crossing the carriageway at that moment.
Yes, if visibility at the intersection is sufficient to complete the manoeuvre safely.
qs.x: Overtaking a vehicle that has slowed immediately before an intersection is prohibited, whatever the pedestrians or visibility.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to overtake near the crest of a hill without entering the lane of oncoming traffic?
qs.x: Overtaking at the crest of a hill is banned only when it means entering the oncoming lane; without that it is allowed.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to overtake near the crest of a hill by entering the lane of oncoming traffic?
o: Yes, if there are no other vehicles in the oncoming lane.
qs.x: Overtaking into the oncoming lane at the crest of a hill is prohibited because oncoming traffic cannot be seen.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to overtake on a road section with limited visibility by entering the lane of oncoming traffic?
o: Yes, if the driver is confident the manoeuvre can be completed safely.
qs.x: Overtaking into the oncoming lane where visibility is limited is prohibited, regardless of the driver's confidence.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to overtake on a road section with limited visibility without entering the lane of oncoming traffic?
qs.x: Overtaking where visibility is limited is banned only if it involves entering the oncoming lane; otherwise it is permitted.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to overtake on a road section with limited visibility?
o: Yes, if the overtaking manoeuvre does not involve entering the lane of oncoming traffic.
No, regardless of visibility and whether the oncoming lane is entered.
qs.x: Overtaking on a limited-visibility section is allowed if it does not involve entering the oncoming lane.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to overtake where the road narrows?
o: Yes, if the overtaking manoeuvre does not involve entering the lane of oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the driver is confident the manoeuvre can be completed safely.
qs.x: Overtaking where the road narrows is prohibited, whether or not the oncoming lane is entered.

qs.q: A bus driver is prohibited from overtaking when the driver of the vehicle to be overtaken is:
qs.x: Overtaking is prohibited when the vehicle ahead is itself overtaking or passing an obstruction.

qs.q: Travel is permitted:
o: Straight ahead and in the opposite direction only.
qs.x: The no-left-turn sign bans only the left turn, so going straight and a U-turn remain permitted.

qs.q: If you are driving a bus, may you begin overtaking?
qs.x: Overtaking may not be started because the truck ahead is itself overtaking, and overtaking is then prohibited.

qs.q: Is the driver of a bus weighing more than 5 tonnes permitted to begin overtaking in this situation?
o: Yes, provided the driver is certain the manoeuvre will be completed before reaching a point 100 metres from the railway level crossing.
qs.x: Overtaking near a railway crossing is banned, but it may be started if it will be finished before the 100 m point from the crossing.

qs.q: Must the driver of the route-service bus yield the right of way in this situation?
qs.x: With no priority signs, the bus must yield both to the tram and to the truck approaching from the right.

qs.q: In which direction may the driver of the tourist bus proceed in this situation?
qs.x: The green round signal allows all directions; the white signal applies only to trams.

qs.q: Overtaking along the indicated path is:
o: Permitted only for drivers of public transport buses.
qs.x: The shown path crosses the continuous line and uses the oncoming lane near an intersection, so overtaking is prohibited.

qs.q: In built-up areas, where there are two lanes for traffic travelling in the same direction, are public transport vehicles permitted to use the leftmost lane?
o: Permitted when turning left or making a U-turn.
qs.x: In a built-up area with two lanes in one direction, public transport vehicles may use the leftmost lane in all cases.

qs.q: Is the bus driver permitted to overtake the trucks along the indicated path outside a built-up area?
o: Yes, if the trucks are travelling at less than 30 km/h.
qs.x: The path crosses a continuous line and passes through an intersection, so it is not permitted whatever the trucks' speed.

qs.q: Is overtaking permitted in a tunnel?
o: Yes, but only if artificial lighting is provided.
qs.x: Overtaking in a tunnel is prohibited regardless of lighting.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to proceed straight ahead?
o: The passenger car and the truck.
qs.x: The green straight arrow is over the middle lane where the truck stands; the other lanes have different signals.

qs.q: You are driving a route-service vehicle and intend to turn left in this situation. In what order will you pass through the intersection?
qs.x: A left-turning driver yields to the police car with special signals, then to the oncoming motorcycle, so passes third.

qs.q: You are driving a bus. When the traffic signal is flashing yellow, must you yield the right of way to the tram?
o: Yes, because trams always have priority over non-rail vehicles at intersections.
No, because the tram is on a minor road.
qs.x: With a flashing yellow signal the intersection is unregulated; the bus is on the main road and the tram on the minor one, so no yielding is needed.

qs.q: Must the bus driver yield the right of way to the motorcycle?
o: No, because the bus is larger, which gives it priority over the motorcycle.
qs.x: A vehicle's size gives no priority, so the bus driver must yield according to the intersection rules.

qs.q: Is the tram permitted to pass through the intersection first, simultaneously with the green passenger car?
o: No. The tram must yield the right of way to the yellow passenger car.
qs.x: The tram's and the green car's paths do not cross, so they may pass through the intersection at the same time.

qs.q: Parking is prohibited:
o: In all of the above situations.
qs.x: Parking is prohibited both on and under bridges, elevated roadways and overpasses.

qs.q: Is it permitted to let a passenger alight at a location where a continuous yellow line is marked along the top of the kerb and a 'No stopping' sign is installed?
o: Permitted if no public transport vehicles are present.
Permitted only for public transport vehicles.
qs.x: The continuous yellow kerb line and the no-stopping sign also ban letting a passenger out, since that is stopping.

qs.q: Does the prohibitory sign apply to the section of road where the driver has stopped?
qs.x: A prohibitory sign applies up to the nearest intersection; the U-turn pocket and sign do not cancel it.

qs.q: Within what distance of a railway level crossing is parking prohibited?
qs.x: Parking is prohibited within 25 m of a railroad crossing.

qs.q: In this situation, is it permitted to stop to let a passenger alight?
o: Permitted, provided this does not obstruct the movement of public transport vehicles.
qs.x: In the public-transit lane, stopping to drop off a passenger is allowed if it does not hinder transit vehicles.

qs.q: Which driver is required to stop?
qs.x: The bus has stopped at the crossing for a pedestrian, so the passenger-car driver must stop.

qs.q: This road marking permits travel:
o: To the left and to make a U-turn.
Straight ahead, to the left and to make a U-turn.
qs.x: The lane arrow shows a left turn, and from the leftmost lane a U-turn is also permitted.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to park within the area of effect of this road sign?
o: Vehicles driven by persons with disabilities and taxis with their taximeters switched on.
qs.x: The No Parking sign does not apply to vehicles driven by disabled persons or to taxis with the meter running.

qs.q: What does this road marking indicate?
o: A place for picking up and setting down passengers.
A stop for public transport vehicles.
A stop for public transport vehicles and a taxi rank.
qs.x: The yellow zigzag marking beside the stop sign marks a public transit vehicle stop.

qs.q: What does a solid yellow line used as a horizontal road marking indicate?
o: A place where stopping and parking vehicles are prohibited.
A place where stopping is permitted to let passengers alight or to unload the vehicle.
A place where parking vehicles is prohibited.
qs.x: A solid yellow line at the roadway edge or on the curb prohibits both stopping and parking.

qs.q: Is a driver permitted to cross the solid line marking the boundaries of parking spaces?
qs.x: A solid line marking parking-space boundaries does not regulate traffic, so it may be crossed.

qs.q: In which of the directions indicated by the arrows is movement permitted?
o: To the left and in the opposite direction (making a U-turn).
Straight ahead, to the left and in the opposite direction (making a U-turn).
qs.x: The line to the left of our lane may not be crossed, so a left turn or U-turn is impossible; only straight is allowed.

qs.q: What does this road marking indicate?
o: A pedestrian crossing where traffic is controlled by traffic lights.
A place where a cycle path crosses the carriageway.
A place where a pedestrian path crosses the carriageway.
qs.x: The row of squares across the road marks where a bicycle path crosses the roadway.

qs.q: How many traffic lanes does a road have if opposing traffic flows are separated by double solid lines?
qs.x: A double solid line separates opposing traffic on roads with four or more lanes.

qs.q: What do the arrows marked on the carriageway warn drivers about?
o: Approaching a hazardous section of road.
Approaching the end of a traffic lane.
The direction of a dangerous bend in the road.
qs.x: The slanted arrows on the roadway warn that the traffic lane is about to end.

qs.q: Which of these road marking lines is used to mark lanes with reversible traffic?
qs.x: Reversible lanes are marked by line 2, the double broken line.

qs.q: Where is the solid yellow line indicating places where stopping and parking are prohibited marked?
o: Near the edge of the carriageway.
Near the edge of the carriageway or on the upper surface of the kerb.
Only on the upper surface of the kerb.
qs.x: The solid yellow no-stopping line is drawn near the roadway edge or on top of the curb.

qs.q: Which road sign may be used together with a broken yellow road marking?
o: No parking on odd-numbered days of the month.
qs.x: A broken yellow line goes with the No Parking sign: it bans parking only, not stopping.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to use the right-hand lane of the carriageway?
qs.x: The right lane is set off by a solid line and marked A, so it is for public transit vehicles only.

qs.q: What does this road marking indicate?
o: Parking spaces alongside the pavement, showing how motor vehicles must be positioned.
Places where motor vehicles are prohibited from stopping.
Stops for public transport vehicles and taxi stands.
qs.x: The yellow zigzag marking shows public transit stops and taxi parking places.

qs.q: What does this horizontal road marking indicate?
o: A narrowing of the carriageway where the number of lanes in the direction of travel is reduced.
A place where the driver must stop, if necessary, to yield the right of way to vehicles travelling on the intersecting road.
Approaching a place where stopping is prohibited.
qs.x: The row of triangles (give-way line) marks where you must stop if necessary to yield to traffic on the crossing road.

qs.q: Is it permitted to enter the painted traffic island marked with wide white lines?
qs.x: Entering a channelizing island marked with wide white lines (chevrons) is prohibited.

qs.q: What should a driver do when approaching an intersection with a stop line road marking and a green traffic light signal?
o: Stop at the stop line and then proceed.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.
qs.x: The stop line applies only at a red signal or STOP sign; on green you drive through without stopping.

qs.q: What does this road marking indicate?
o: A place where a cycle path crosses the carriageway.
qs.x: The row of squares across the road shows where a bicycle path crosses the roadway.

qs.q: Where must the driver stop the vehicle when this road marking is present?
o: At least 5 m before the road marking.
qs.x: At the give-way line the driver stops right at the marking without crossing it.

qs.q: What does this road marking indicate?
o: A lane reserved for public transport vehicles.
A lane reserved for special-purpose vehicles.
The boundaries of lanes subject to reversible traffic control.
qs.x: The double broken line marks the boundaries of lanes under reversible traffic control.

qs.q: Is making a U-turn permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: The line on our side of the double marking is broken, so a U-turn is permitted here.

qs.q: Is the driver of a bus operating on a tourist route permitted to enter the lane marked 'A' when this road marking is present?
qs.x: A bus on a tourist route counts as a route vehicle, so it may enter the lane marked A.

qs.q: What does a wide broken road marking line indicate?
o: The boundary between the carriageway and the shoulder.
The boundary between the main traffic lane and an acceleration lane.
The boundary between the main traffic lane and a deceleration lane.
qs.x: The wide broken line separates the main lane from the acceleration lane.

qs.q: Which vehicle is permitted to stop within the area of effect of these road signs?
o: The yellow passenger car displaying a 'Disabled person' identification sign.
qs.x: The No Stopping sign does not apply to the yellow car bearing the Disabled badge; the red car may not stop.

qs.q: In which picture has the driver stopped correctly to allow passengers to alight?
o: In the picture on the left.
In the picture on the right.
qs.x: In the left image the car stops at least 5 m from the intersection; in the right it stands on the pedestrian crossing.

qs.q: Which of the following serves as a signal to stop a train?
o: A circular movement of the arm (by day, holding a brightly coloured cloth or another clearly visible object; by night, holding a torch or lantern).
An arm raised above the head holding a disc or a red flag.
An arm extended forward and moved up and down.
qs.x: The signal to stop a train is a circular motion of the arm (a bright cloth by day, a lantern at night).

qs.q: In built-up areas, on roads with one traffic lane in each direction and no tram tracks in the middle, stopping and parking on the left-hand side of the road are:
qs.x: In a populated area, on a road with one lane each way and no tram tracks, stopping and parking on the left are permitted.

qs.q: Where must a vehicle be stopped in relation to a stop line or a 'Stop' road sign in order to yield the right of way to an approaching train?
o: Directly at the stop line and/or the road sign.
qs.x: To yield to a train, stop immediately at the stop line and/or sign.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: The car is at the solid yellow curb line, which prohibits stopping.

qs.q: Is stopping a passenger car permitted at this location?
o: Prohibited, because the distance between the broken road marking line and the stopped vehicle is less than 3 m.
Prohibited on even-numbered days of the month.
qs.x: The sign bans only parking, not stopping, and there is no solid line, so stopping is permitted.

qs.q: Which vehicle driver has violated the parking rules?
o: The driver of the blue passenger car.
The driver of the red passenger car.
qs.x: The blue car parks in the No Parking zone and the red one in a forbidden spot, so both violate the rules.

qs.q: Outside built-up areas, where is parking permitted for long rests, overnight stays or other purposes?
o: In designated parking areas or outside the boundaries of the road.
On the right-hand side of the carriageway, provided that other vehicles are not obstructed.
On the left-hand side of the road, provided that road traffic safety is ensured.
qs.x: Outside populated areas, long-term parking is allowed only in designated parking areas or off the road.

qs.q: Stopping is prohibited if the distance between a solid road marking line and the stopped vehicle is:
qs.x: Stopping is prohibited if less than 3 m remains between the solid line and the stopped vehicle, i.e. 2.5 m here.

qs.q: If traffic across a railway level crossing is prohibited and there are no traffic lights, road signs, road markings or barriers, the driver must stop:
o: At least 5 m from the nearest rail.
At least 7 m from the nearest rail.
At least 10 m from the nearest rail.
qs.x: With the crossing closed and no gate, signal or signs, stop at least 10 m from the nearest rail.

qs.q: Within what distance of a railway level crossing is parking prohibited?
qs.x: Parking is prohibited within 15 m of a railroad crossing.

qs.q: Which answer correctly identifies the drivers who have violated the stopping rules?
o: The drivers of the red passenger car and the motorcycle.
The driver of the blue passenger car.
qs.x: The No Stopping sign with a double-arrow plate covers both sides of the road, so all drivers violated it.

qs.q: Which vehicle drivers have stopped incorrectly to allow passengers to alight?
o: The driver of the passenger car.
The motorcycle rider and the bus driver.
qs.x: The motorcycle stands on the pedestrian crossing and the minibus within 5 m of it, while the red car stopped correctly.

qs.q: If traffic across a railway level crossing is prohibited and there are no traffic lights, road signs or road markings, the driver must stop:
o: At least 5 m before the barrier.
At least 3 m before the barrier.
qs.x: With the crossing closed, stop at least 5 m before the barrier gate.

qs.q: Is a tourist bus permitted to use the lane marked with the letter “A”?
qs.x: The lane marked A is reserved for public route vehicles, which a tourist bus is not.

qs.q: What does the letter “A” marked on a traffic lane of the carriageway indicate?
o: A designated lane for public transport vehicles.
A designated lane for category A vehicles.
qs.x: The letter A on a lane marks a special lane for public transit vehicles.

qs.q: Is the vehicle permitted to stop at the indicated location to allow passengers to alight?
o: Yes, but only by mounting the pavement.
qs.x: The solid yellow curb line prohibits stopping, even to drop off a passenger, and driving onto the sidewalk is not allowed.

qs.q: Is it permitted to continue in the direction indicated by the arrow?
o: Yes, for the purpose of stopping to allow passengers to alight.
Yes, for the purpose of overtaking a truck.
qs.x: Moving in the direction of the arrow is allowed only to stop and drop off a passenger.

qs.q: What is indicated by this type of vertical road marking?
o: The lower edges of a bridge or tunnel.
The entrance to an unlit tunnel.
Any element of a road structure that poses a hazard to traffic.
qs.x: This black-and-white vertical marking indicates the lower edges and supports of bridges and tunnels.

qs.q: A bus driver has stopped to pick up passengers. A passenger car is travelling at 70 km/h. Which driver is violating the road traffic regulations?
qs.x: The bus stopped properly at the right edge and 70 km/h does not exceed the permitted speed.

qs.q: In which of the following situations may a bus driver enter the middle lane of a three-lane two-way road, where the middle lane is used by traffic in both directions?
o: To overtake or pass an obstruction.
To turn left or make a U-turn.
In both of the above situations.
None of the answers is correct.
qs.x: The middle lane of a three-lane road may be entered both for overtaking or passing an obstruction and for a left turn or U-turn.

qs.q: Where must the driver stop in this situation?
o: Before the intersection of the carriageways.
qs.x: At the red light you stop before the stop line, not at the signal or beyond it.

qs.q: Is the driver of a bus operating a scheduled passenger service permitted to stop at the indicated location to pick up passengers?
qs.x: Stopping at the indicated place is prohibited; even a scheduled bus may pick up passengers only at a designated stop.

qs.q: Is the driver of a tourist bus permitted to park at the indicated location for an extended rest?
o: No, the driver is not permitted.
qs.x: The no-parking sign bans a long stop for a rest, since that counts as parking.

qs.q: Where must the bus driver stop to yield the right of way to the passenger car before proceeding to the left?
o: At a safe location chosen by the driver.
qs.x: The bus driver must stop at the give-way marking (triangles) to yield to the car.

qs.q: Where must the driver stop in this situation?
qs.x: At a STOP sign the driver must stop before the stop line.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to stop within the area of effect of this road sign?
o: Vehicles driven by persons with disabilities only.
Taxis with their meters switched on only.
Stopping is prohibited for all vehicles.
qs.x: The No Stopping sign prohibits stopping for all vehicles without exception.

qs.q: Is stopping to pick up passengers permitted within the area of effect of these road signs?
qs.x: The No Parking sign bans only parking, so stopping to pick up a passenger is permitted.

qs.q: For which vehicles is the lane marked with the letter “A” reserved?
o: Only buses operating on a designated route.
qs.x: The lane marked A is reserved for public transit vehicles.

qs.q: Are buses permitted to stop and park on the left-hand side of the carriageway on one-way roads in built-up areas?
o: Yes, both stopping and parking are permitted.
qs.x: On one-way roads in built-up areas buses may stop and park also on the left side of the carriageway.

qs.q: Are public transport vehicles permitted to stop outside designated stopping places?
qs.x: Public transport vehicles may stop only at designated stopping places.

qs.q: Is parking of buses permitted in residential zones and courtyard areas?
qs.x: In residential zones and courtyards parking is allowed only in places designated for it.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: Stopping at the right edge is permitted because no sign or marking prohibits it.

qs.q: Is parking permitted in this situation?
qs.x: Parking on the carriageway beside the barrier, with no shoulder and limited visibility, is prohibited.

qs.q: At which of the indicated locations is stopping permitted?
qs.x: A is at the left edge of a one-way street and B is before the sign, while C is inside the No Stopping zone, so A and B are allowed.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: Stopping on the yellow zigzag marking is prohibited because that space is for public transit vehicles.

qs.q: Is stopping to pick up passengers permitted in the situation shown?
qs.x: Stopping in a tunnel is prohibited, including to pick up a passenger.

qs.q: In which of the situations shown is stopping permitted?
qs.x: Stopping is permitted only at B; A and C are in the no-stopping zone next to the pedestrian crossing.

qs.q: Stopping is prohibited:
o: At railway level crossings and within 50 m of them.
At railway level crossings and within 50 m before them.
qs.x: Stopping is prohibited at the crossing itself; near it only parking is banned.

qs.q: Parking is prohibited:
o: At railway level crossings and within 50 m of them.
At railway level crossings and within 50 m before them.
qs.x: Parking is prohibited at the crossing and within 50 m of it.

qs.q: Which of the indicated vehicles are stopped correctly?
qs.x: Only C has stopped correctly, at the right edge; A and B are in forbidden or wrong positions.

qs.q: Are you required to yield the right of way to the truck?
qs.x: The obstruction (the broken-down car) is on the truck's side, so the truck must yield to us.

qs.q: When is crossing the road marking permitted?
qs.x: The line is solid up to the pedestrian crossing and may be crossed only after it, where it becomes broken.

qs.q: Is stopping to pick up passengers permitted in this situation?
o: Only for the driver of a public transport vehicle.
qs.x: At the stop sign and zigzag marking only the driver of a public transit vehicle may pick up passengers.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: Stopping is prohibited on the crossing and within 15 m of the bus stop, even to drop off a passenger.

qs.q: At which of the indicated locations is parking permitted?
qs.x: A and C are outside the No Parking sign zone, while B is under it, so parking is allowed at A or C.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: Stopping is prohibited within 5 m of the intersecting road, and the indicated spot is closer than that.

qs.q: Is parking permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: The No Parking sign with a Zone plate prohibits parking throughout the whole zone.

qs.q: Is stopping on a bridge to pick up passengers permitted?
qs.x: Stopping on a bridge is prohibited, including to pick up a passenger.

qs.q: Which driver has stopped correctly?
qs.x: Outside built-up areas stopping at the left edge is prohibited; only C stands correctly at the right edge.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: Less than 3 m would remain between the solid line and the car (the road is 4 m wide), so stopping is prohibited.

qs.q: At which of the indicated locations is stopping permitted?
qs.x: The No Parking sign does not ban stopping, so only A is allowed; B stands in the middle of the carriageway.

qs.q: Stopping at the indicated location is:
qs.x: Stopping is prohibited within 5 m of a pedestrian crossing, and the car stands too close.

qs.q: In which of the indicated cases is stopping permitted?
qs.x: In a built-up area on a road with one lane each way and no tram tracks, stopping on either side is allowed, so all cases are permitted.

qs.q: After passing the truck, is it permitted to continue driving in this lane?
qs.x: After passing you must return to the right lane; the left lane is for passing and you may not stay in it.

qs.q: Is it permitted to continue driving in the lane currently occupied in this situation?
qs.x: Continuing in the occupied lane is permitted; no marking or sign forbids it, so you may stay in your lane.

qs.q: Stopping at the indicated location is:
o: Permitted if the distance between the vehicle and the road marking exceeds 3 metres.
qs.x: On this narrow street less than 3 m would remain to the solid line, so stopping is prohibited.

qs.q: This road marking indicates:
o: Approach to a bend in the road.
Approach to the end of a lane.
qs.x: The curved slanted arrows show the approach to the end of the lane.

qs.q: What does this road marking indicate?
o: Approach to a Stop line sign at a signal-controlled intersection.
Approach to a stop line road marking used together with a STOP sign.
qs.x: The word STOP on the road warns of an approaching stop line used together with the STOP sign.

qs.q: The vertical markings on barriers indicate:
o: Approach to a railway level crossing.
qs.x: The black-and-white vertical marking on barriers warns of travel along a dangerous section of road.

qs.q: This triangular road marking indicates:
o: Approach to a point where drivers must yield the right of way.
Approach to a place where vehicles must stop.
qs.x: A triangle painted on the road announces the approach to a place where you must give way.

qs.q: These broken road markings within an intersection indicate:
qs.x: Broken lines inside an intersection show the traffic lanes.

qs.q: Overtaking across this road marking is:
qs.x: The line on our side is broken, so passing the slow tractor is permitted.

qs.q: These vertical road markings indicate:
o: All vertical elements adjacent to the carriageway.
Only those elements of road structures that pose a hazard to drivers.
qs.x: Vertical marking is applied only to road-structure elements that pose a hazard to traffic.

qs.q: With this road marking, is it permitted to enter the intersection if doing so will not obstruct the driver of the passenger car?
qs.x: The give-way marking before the intersection requires yielding to traffic on the main road, so entering is not allowed.

qs.q: In which case is it permitted to cross the solid road marking?
qs.x: A solid line may be crossed only to stop where stopping is allowed, which applies only to B.

qs.q: What does the broken road marking indicate?
o: Permission to stop on the shoulder.
The edges of the carriageway on a two-lane road.
Permission to drive on the shoulder.
qs.x: The broken line on a two-lane road marks the edges of the roadway.

qs.q: Driving along this path in the situation shown is:
qs.x: The path crosses the double solid line toward lanes under crossed-out signals, so it is prohibited.

qs.q: Is parking permitted at the indicated location?
o: Permitted, provided the vehicle does not mount the pavement.
qs.x: The solid yellow curb line bans stopping and parking, so parking here is prohibited.

qs.q: With this road marking, overtaking is:
o: Permitted if the vehicle ahead is a slow-moving vehicle.
qs.x: A double continuous line prohibits overtaking, however slow the vehicle ahead is.

qs.q: May you continue driving beyond the sign?
o: Yes, up to the stop line.
qs.x: The STOP sign stands before the stop line, so you may proceed past the sign up to the stop line.

qs.q: When orange and white road markings conflict, drivers:
o: May follow whichever markings they prefer.
Must comply with the white road markings.
Must comply with the orange road markings.
qs.x: Orange marking is temporary, so when it conflicts with white marking the orange one is followed.

qs.q: Which driver is permitted to cross the solid road marking in order to stop?
o: The driver travelling in the opposite direction.
qs.x: Only the oncoming driver, on whose side there is a permitted stopping place, may cross the solid line to stop.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: The broken yellow line bans only parking, so stopping is permitted.

qs.q: This road marking:
o: Indicates the boundaries of a residential zone.
qs.x: The row of black-and-white squares across the road marks a speed hump.

qs.q: This road marking prohibits:
o: Driving to the left of it or crossing over it.
qs.x: A continuous line prohibits driving to the left of it or crossing it.

qs.q: This road marking indicates:
o: The maximum permitted speed on the indicated section of road.
qs.x: The number in a circle painted on the carriageway shows the maximum permitted speed on that section.

qs.q: The marking on the carriageway indicates:
o: The distance from the nearest intersection.
The distance from the nearest built-up area.
qs.x: The inscription A 100 on the roadway is the road or route number.

qs.q: On which side may the obstruction be passed?
qs.x: The arrow on the blue sign dictates the direction; the obstruction may be passed only on side A, the left.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to use the rightmost lane of this road?
qs.x: The right lane carries the letter A and a bus sign, so it is for trolleybuses and public transit buses.

qs.q: Is parking permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: The broken yellow line at the curb prohibits parking, although stopping is allowed.

qs.q: The increasing length of the broken road marking lines indicates:
o: That the end of the lane is approaching.
That a hazardous section is approaching.
That the broken line will soon become a continuous line.
qs.x: Lengthening dashes warn that the broken line will soon become a continuous line.

qs.q: In the situation shown, proceeding straight ahead is:
o: Permitted after changing to the right-hand lane.
qs.x: The left lane has only a left arrow, so to go straight you must change into the right lane.

qs.q: How many traffic lanes does this road have?
qs.x: A double solid line splits the road into two directions with two lanes each, four in total.

qs.q: Where are passengers permitted to wait for public transport vehicles?
o: Only on raised passenger waiting areas, or, where none are provided, on pavements or verges.
At the edge of the carriageway if the approaching vehicle is already visible.
qs.x: Passengers must wait only on raised boarding platforms, or on pavements or verges where there are none, never at the carriageway edge.

qs.q: When are passengers permitted to step onto the carriageway to board a public transport vehicle?
o: When the vehicle approaches the stop and slows down.
Only after the vehicle has come to a complete stop.
qs.x: A passenger may step onto the carriageway only after the vehicle has come to a complete stop.
