qs.q: When must a passenger leave the carriageway after alighting from a public transport vehicle?
o: When the vehicle driver closes the doors.
qs.x: After alighting, a passenger must clear the carriageway immediately.

qs.q: Is a trolleybus driver permitted to stop at a stop marked with the “Tram Stop” sign?
o: Yes, if no tram is present at the time and the trolleybus does not obstruct other vehicles.
Only if the tram tracks are located along the right-hand edge of the road in the trolleybus’s direction of travel.
qs.x: The tram stop is meant only for trams, so a trolleybus may not stop there.

qs.q: Is a trolleybus driver permitted to stop at a stop marked with this sign?
o: No, because it is intended for buses only.
qs.x: The bus and/or trolleybus stop sign allows both buses and trolleybuses to stop.

qs.q: Are drivers of other vehicles permitted to park in an area marked with the “Taxi Rank” sign?
o: Only at night, when taxi traffic is light.
Only on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.
qs.x: Other vehicles may not park in a taxi rank at any time of day or week.

qs.q: What is the main difference between a “Zone with Parking Restrictions” sign and ordinary prohibitory signs?
o: It prohibits both parking and stopping for any purpose.
It applies across the entire width of the road, on both sides, and its effect is not interrupted by an intersection.
qs.x: A parking-restriction zone applies on both sides of the road and is not interrupted by an intersection.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to park within the area of effect of this sign immediately after passing through an intersection?
o: Yes, because all restrictive signs cease to apply after an intersection.
Yes, if the bus is a public transport vehicle.
No, because the restriction imposed by the sign is not interrupted by an intersection.
qs.x: The zone sign's effect is not interrupted by an intersection, so parking just beyond it is still prohibited.

qs.q: Is the driver of a public transport bus permitted to stop within the area of effect of this sign to pick up or set down passengers?
o: No, because parking is prohibited within the zone.
qs.x: The zone bans parking, not stopping, so stopping to pick up or set down passengers is allowed.

qs.q: A bus driver sees this sign on the right-hand side of a road in a built-up area. The road has one lane in each direction and no tram tracks in the middle. Is the driver permitted to park on the left-hand side of the road?
o: Yes, because the sign is on the right and applies only to that side.
qs.x: The zone sign applies to both sides of a road with one lane each way and no tram tracks, so parking on the left is not allowed.

qs.q: Is the driver of a bus powered by an internal combustion engine permitted to park in the parking area marked with this sign?
o: Yes, if parking does not exceed 5 minutes.
Yes, if the charging station is unoccupied and no electric vehicles are present.
qs.x: The plug plate reserves the space for electric vehicles being charged, so a combustion-engine bus may not park there.

qs.q: Is the driver of a hybrid-powered bus permitted to park in the parking area marked with this sign?
qs.x: The plate is for vehicles charged from an external source; a hybrid bus that is not so charged may not park there.

qs.q: Is the driver of an electric bus permitted to park in the parking area marked with this sign if the bus is not connected to a charging device?
qs.x: The space is for electric vehicles connected to a charger, so one that is not connected may not park there.

qs.q: For drivers of which vehicles is the inspection point marked with this sign intended?
o: All types of vehicles crossing the state border.
Vehicles engaged in international road transport.
qs.x: The inspection point is intended for vehicles engaged in international road transport.

qs.q: Is the driver of a hybrid vehicle that cannot be charged from an external power source permitted to park within the area of effect of this sign?
o: Yes, because a hybrid vehicle also has an electric motor.
No, because this parking area is intended only for vehicles that can be charged from an external power source.
qs.x: The area is only for vehicles that charge from an external source, so a hybrid without that ability may not park there.

qs.q: Is the driver of a tourist bus permitted to let a passenger alight in the zone where these signs are installed?
o: Yes, if the driver remains at the wheel and can immediately leave the area of effect of the sign.
Yes, because towing away applies only to passenger cars.
qs.x: Stopping is prohibited for all vehicles in the towing-away zone, including to let a passenger alight.

qs.q: Are buses permitted to stop and park on the right-hand side of a road, at the edge of the carriageway?
o: Yes, if there is no road shoulder.
qs.x: Stopping and parking at the right edge of the carriageway is allowed when there is no shoulder.

qs.q: Are buses permitted to stop and park on the right-hand side of the carriageway if a road shoulder is available?
qs.x: If a shoulder exists the bus must stop on it, so stopping on the carriageway itself is prohibited.

qs.q: Are buses permitted to stop and park on the pavement on the right-hand side of the road?
o: Yes, if the bus is a small-class bus.
qs.x: Stopping and parking a bus on the pavement is prohibited, even partially.

qs.q: Are buses permitted to stop and park on the left-hand side of the carriageway on roads outside built- up areas with one lane in each direction?
o: Yes, if there is no safe place to stop or park on the right-hand side.
qs.x: Outside built-up areas on a one-lane-each-way road, stopping and parking on the left is prohibited whatever the situation on the right.

qs.q: Within built-up areas, are buses permitted to stop and park on the left-hand side of the carriageway on roads with one lane in each direction and no tram tracks in the middle?
qs.x: In a built-up area on a road with one lane each way and no tram tracks, buses may stop and park on the left.

qs.q: Are buses permitted to stop and park on the left-hand side of a one-way road outside built-up areas?
qs.x: On a one-way road, stopping and parking on the left is allowed outside built-up areas too.

qs.q: Within built-up areas, which vehicles may stop, but not park, on the left-hand side of the carriageway on a one-way road for loading or unloading goods or for passengers to board or alight?
o: Trucks with a maximum permissible mass exceeding 3.5 tonnes.
qs.x: On the left of a one-way road in a built-up area only trucks over 3.5 t may stop (not park) for loading or unloading.

qs.q: Where are buses permitted to park for an extended period (overnight) outside built-up areas?
o: Only in designated parking areas or off the road.
On the shoulders of illuminated road sections, outside the carriageway.
Wherever the driver considers it safe.
qs.x: Outside built-up areas buses may park long-term only in designated areas or off the road.

qs.q: What must a bus driver do after making a forced stop at a place where stopping is prohibited?
o: Switch on the hazard warning lights and wait for assistance without moving the vehicle.
Switch on the hazard warning lights, place a warning triangle and take all possible measures to remove the vehicle from that location.
Inform the police and follow their instructions.
qs.x: After a forced stop, switch on the hazards, place the warning triangle and do everything possible to remove the vehicle from that spot.

qs.q: Where are buses prohibited from stopping and parking?
o: On pedestrian crossings and within 15 metres of the edge where a pedestrian crossing meets the carriageway.
On pedestrian crossings and within 10 metres of the edge where a pedestrian crossing meets the carriageway.
On pedestrian crossings and within 5 metres of the edge where a pedestrian crossing meets the carriageway.
In all of the above cases.
qs.x: Stopping and parking are banned on pedestrian crossings and close to them, so all listed options cover the prohibited zone.

qs.q: Where are buses prohibited from stopping and parking?
o: On all downhill sections of roads.
At all of the above locations.
qs.x: Stopping and parking are banned on and under bridges, but not generally on all downhill sections or along reservoir shores.

qs.q: On which sections of the road are buses prohibited from stopping and parking?
o: Where a stationary bus would obstruct other drivers' view of traffic signals or road signs.
On any uphill or downhill gradient.
Where vehicle traffic and pedestrian movement are heavy.
qs.x: Stopping is banned where the bus would hide traffic signals or road signs from other drivers.

qs.q: Where are buses prohibited from stopping and parking?
o: Within 15 metres of an intersection of carriageways.
On all roads with tram tracks.
In all of the above cases.
qs.x: Stopping and parking are banned at railway level crossings; there is no blanket ban within 15 m of every intersection or on all tram roads.

qs.q: Are buses permitted to stop or park where the distance between the stationary bus and a continuous road marking, the opposite edge of the carriageway or a central reservation is less than 3 metres?
o: Yes, if traffic is not heavy and the bus does not cause congestion.
Yes, if the driver remains at the wheel and can move the bus immediately if necessary.
No, stopping and parking are prohibited.
Yes, but only for up to 5 minutes to allow passengers to board or alight.
qs.x: Stopping and parking are prohibited where less than 3 m remains between the bus and a continuous line or the opposite edge.

qs.q: At what distance from a railway level crossing is stopping a bus prohibited?
o: Within 50 metres of the railway level crossing.
Directly on the railway level crossing.
Within 15 metres of the railway level crossing.
In all of the above cases.
qs.x: Stopping is prohibited directly on a railway level crossing, not at 15 or 50 m from it.

qs.q: Where is parking a bus prohibited near railway level crossings?
o: Within 100 metres of a railway level crossing.
Less than 50 metres from a railway level crossing.
Directly on a railway level crossing.
In all of the above cases.
qs.x: Parking is banned on the crossing itself and closer than 50 m to it, so options 2 and 3 are correct.

qs.q: Are buses permitted to stop or park on the shoulders of a road marked with the 'Road for Motor Vehicles' sign?
o: Yes, anywhere, provided the bus is entirely off the carriageway and on the shoulder.
No, except in the event of a forced stop.
qs.x: On a road for motor vehicles, stopping and parking are prohibited except for a forced stop.

qs.q: Are buses permitted to park in residential zones outside designated parking spaces indicated by signs and road markings?
o: No, because only passenger cars belonging to residents of the area may park in a residential zone.
qs.x: In a residential zone outside marked spaces only smaller vehicles such as minibuses may park.

qs.q: Is bus parking permitted in courtyard areas?
qs.x: In courtyard areas parking is allowed only in designated places.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to stop as shown within the area of effect of these signs?
qs.x: The parking sign with its plate allows parking only in the manner shown on the plate, so stopping as shown is not allowed.

qs.q: A bus driver is permitted to stop at the indicated location:
o: Only if the bus is a public transport vehicle.
Only if the bus is not a public transport vehicle.
Stopping is prohibited in all cases.
qs.x: Stopping close to an intersection is prohibited for all buses, including public transport, except at a designated stop.

qs.q: In this situation, the bus driver is permitted to stop:
qs.x: In a built-up area on a road with one lane each way and no tram tracks, stopping is allowed on either side.

qs.q: Is the driver of the tourist bus permitted to stop at the indicated location if it is 3 metres from the pedestrian crossing?
qs.x: Stopping is prohibited within 5 m of a pedestrian crossing, and 3 m is within that distance.

qs.q: Which driver has violated the stopping rules?
qs.x: Both drivers broke the rules by stopping on the pavement, where stopping is prohibited.

qs.q: Parking of buses is prohibited:
o: At the edge of the carriageway where there is no road shoulder.
Outside built-up areas, on the carriageway of roads marked with the 'Priority Road' sign.
At a distance of 10 metres from the edge of intersecting carriageways.
qs.x: Outside built-up areas, parking buses on the carriageway of a road with the Priority Road sign is prohibited.

qs.q: Are public transport vehicles permitted to stop outside designated stopping places?
o: Yes, in the event of a forced stop.
qs.x: Public transport vehicles may stop outside stopping places only in the case of a forced stop.

qs.q: When this sign is displayed, stopping is permitted for:
qs.x: The sign marks a bus and/or trolleybus stop, so buses and/or trolleybuses may stop there.

qs.q: When this sign is displayed, stopping is permitted for:
qs.x: The sign shows a tram, so only trams may stop there.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to stop on a bridge to pick up passengers?
o: Yes, but only for buses in subcategory D1.
qs.x: Stopping on a bridge is prohibited for all buses, even to pick up a passenger.

qs.q: Which bus driver has violated the parking rules?
o: Only the driver of the green bus.
Only the driver of the yellow bus.
qs.x: The yellow bus stands under a no-stopping sign, so only its driver has broken the rules.

qs.q: After turning left at this intersection, the driver of a route-service bus must stop at the designated bus stop to pick up and set down passengers. Which path must the driver follow when turning left?
o: Path B only, because the bus stop is on the right-hand side of the road.
qs.x: The route bus may make its left turn along either path, as both are permitted.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for a truck carrying passengers in a specially equipped cargo body?
qs.x: A truck carrying people in an equipped cargo bed must not exceed 60 km/h.

qs.q: At what distance before the beginning of a hazardous road section is this warning sign placed outside built-up areas?
qs.x: The winding-road warning triangle is placed 150–300 m before the hazard outside built-up areas.

qs.q: At what maximum speed may vehicles carrying organized groups of children travel?
qs.x: Vehicles carrying organized groups of children are limited to 60 km/h.

qs.q: At what maximum speed may vehicles travel in built-up areas?
qs.x: The general maximum speed in populated areas is 60 km/h.

qs.q: In which directions is traffic permitted?
o: Straight ahead and to the right.
Straight ahead, to the right and to the left.
qs.x: The blue straight-arrow sign marks a one-way road, so straight, right and left are allowed, but not a U-turn.

qs.q: At what maximum speed may intercity buses travel outside built-up areas?
qs.x: Intercity buses may travel up to 90 km/h outside built-up areas.

qs.q: Are drivers of suburban, interregional and intercity buses permitted to exceed 60 km/h in built-up areas?
o: Yes, but only on roads with two or more lanes in the same direction.
qs.x: Suburban, interregional and intercity buses may not exceed 60 km/h in built-up areas.

qs.q: Is an intercity bus driver permitted to exceed 70 km/h outside built-up areas?
o: Yes, but only when travelling on roads with two or more lanes in the direction of travel.
Yes, provided the speed does not exceed 90 km/h.
qs.x: An intercity bus may exceed 70 km/h outside built-up areas, up to 90 km/h.

qs.q: When towing a vehicle, where must the warning triangle be placed if the hazard warning lights are absent or defective?

At the front of the towing vehicle.
On either vehicle in a visible position, at the driver’s discretion.

qs.q: When towing with a rigid coupling, the distance between the vehicles must not exceed:

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed when towing with a motor vehicle?

qs.q: When towing with a flexible or rigid coupling, is it permitted to carry passengers in the towed motor vehicle?
o: Yes, in a bus or trolleybus.
Yes, but only in a passenger car.
Yes, in the cargo body of a truck or in a passenger car.
Yes, in the cab of a truck or in a passenger car.
qs.x: In a towed motor vehicle, people may ride only in a truck cab or a passenger car.

qs.q: When roads are icy, towing:
o: Is permitted with a rigid coupling or by the partial-loading method.
qs.x: On ice, towing is allowed only with a rigid coupling or by partial loading, not with a flexible one.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed when towing a vehicle with a flexible coupling?
qs.x: Towing with a flexible coupling is allowed at up to 50 km/h.

qs.q: In which case is towing prohibited?
o: When roads are icy and a rigid coupling is used.
When roads are icy and a flexible coupling is used.
qs.x: In icy conditions towing is prohibited with a flexible coupling, while a rigid one is allowed.

qs.q: When towing motor vehicles outside built-up areas, the speed must not exceed:
qs.x: Even outside populated areas, towing a motor vehicle is limited to 50 km/h.

qs.q: What distance between the vehicles must be maintained when towing with a flexible coupling?
qs.x: A flexible coupling must keep the vehicles 4 to 6 m apart.

qs.q: When towing with a rigid coupling, the distance between the vehicles must not exceed:
qs.x: With a rigid coupling the distance between the vehicles must not exceed 4 m.

qs.q: Is towing a motorcycle with a sidecar permitted?
o: Permitted only with a rigid coupling.
qs.x: Motorcycles with sidecars are stable, so towing them is permitted.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed when towing with a flexible coupling?
qs.x: The maximum speed when towing with a flexible coupling is 50 km/h.

qs.q: Is carrying passengers in a truck trailer permitted?
o: Permitted only for persons accompanying the cargo.
qs.x: Carrying people in a cargo trailer is prohibited, even those accompanying the cargo.

qs.q: When towing with a rigid or flexible coupling, is it permitted to carry passengers in the towed bus?
o: Permitted for up to eight passengers.
qs.x: Carrying people in a bus being towed by rigid or flexible coupling is prohibited.

qs.q: When roads are icy, towing a bus is prohibited:
qs.x: On icy roads towing with a flexible coupling is prohibited because the towed vehicle may slide uncontrolled.

qs.q: When towing with a flexible or rigid coupling, is it permitted to carry passengers in the towed motor vehicle?
o: Permitted in a bus or trolleybus.
Permitted in the cab of a truck or in a passenger car.
Permitted in the cargo body of a truck or in a passenger car.
qs.x: In a towed motor vehicle people may ride only in a truck cab or passenger car, not in a bed or bus.

qs.q: Carrying passengers is prohibited if:
o: The number of passengers on a bus operating on a tourist route exceeds the number of equipped seats.
The number of passengers on a bus operating on an intercity route exceeds the number of equipped seats.
qs.x: Carrying more passengers than equipped seats is prohibited on both tourist and intercity buses.

qs.q: When transporting an organized group of children by bus, there must be at least:
o: One adult accompanying person on board.
Two adult accompanying persons on board.
Three adult accompanying persons on board.
qs.x: When transporting organized groups of children, at least one adult escort must be on board.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for buses providing interregional and intercity passenger services on all roads outside built-up areas?
qs.x: Interregional and intercity buses may do up to 90 km/h on all roads outside built-up areas.

qs.q: Are buses permitted to travel at 70 km/h outside built-up areas?
qs.x: Buses are allowed to travel at 70 km/h outside built-up areas.

qs.q: In built-up areas, buses providing intercity passenger services may travel at a speed not exceeding:
qs.x: Intercity buses may not exceed 60 km/h in built-up areas.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for buses providing intercity passenger services outside built- up areas?
qs.x: Buses on intercity services may travel up to 90 km/h outside built-up areas.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for buses in areas marked by the “Residential Zone” and “End of Residential Zone” road signs?
qs.x: The maximum speed in a residential zone is 20 km/h.

qs.q: When towing with a rigid or flexible coupling, is it permitted to carry passengers in the towed bus?
qs.x: Carrying people in a towed bus is prohibited.

qs.q: Is it permitted to carry passengers in the towing bus?
qs.x: The ban applies to the towed bus; passengers may be carried in the towing bus.

qs.q: In the presence of this road sign, what is the maximum permitted speed for drivers of intercity buses?
qs.x: Under the Motorway sign intercity buses may travel up to 90 km/h.

qs.q: What is the maximum speed at which the driver of the towing bus may travel in this situation?
qs.x: While towing, speed must not exceed 50 km/h.

qs.q: What is the maximum speed at which the driver of an intercity bus may travel in this situation?
qs.x: Outside a built-up area with no other limit, an intercity bus may travel up to 90 km/h.

qs.q: At what speed may the bus driver continue driving within the area indicated by this road sign?
o: At least 60 km/h but not more than 70 km/h.
At least 60 km/h but not more than 90 km/h.
qs.x: The minimum speed sign requires at least 60 km/h, and a bus's maximum outside built-up areas is 90 km/h.

qs.x: Carrying passengers in the towed vehicle is prohibited.

qs.q: When towing with a rigid or flexible coupling, is carrying passengers in the towed bus permitted?
o: Permitted when towing with a rigid coupling.
qs.x: Carrying passengers in a towed bus is prohibited with both rigid and flexible couplings.

qs.q: When a vehicle is being towed, which lights or signals must be switched on on the towed vehicle?

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for intercity buses on motorways?

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for a bus on road sections where this road sign applies?
qs.x: On a section with the Motorway sign a bus's maximum speed is 90 km/h.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for intercity buses on motorways?
qs.x: Intercity buses may travel up to 90 km/h on motorways.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for vehicles in areas marked by the “Residential Zone” and “End of Residential Zone” road signs?
qs.x: Within the Residential Zone signs the limit is 20 km/h.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for passenger cars on road sections where this road sign applies?
qs.x: On a section with the Motorway sign passenger cars may travel up to 110 km/h.

qs.q: When towing a motor vehicle, which lane of this road may you use to continue driving?
qs.x: The sign reserves the right lane for vehicles going 60 km/h or less, and a towing vehicle is limited to 50 km/h, so it must stay in the right lane.

qs.q: Which conditions must a driver take into account when choosing a speed within the permitted limits?
o: The condition of the road surface.
Visibility in the direction of travel.
qs.x: When choosing speed a driver must consider both the road surface condition and visibility ahead.

qs.q: What speed should a driver choose within the permitted limits?
o: A speed that allows the driver to maintain full control of the vehicle.
Any speed that does not exceed the maximum permitted speed.
qs.x: The driver should choose a speed that keeps full control of the vehicle; the legal maximum is not a target.

qs.q: A driver is prohibited from:
o: Exceeding the maximum speed specified in the technical characteristics of the vehicle.
Exceeding the speed indicated by the speed limit identification sign displayed on the vehicle.
Driving unnecessarily slowly and obstructing the movement of other vehicles.
Braking sharply unless necessary to prevent a road traffic accident.
qs.x: All the listed actions are prohibited: exceeding the speed limits, driving needlessly slowly and braking sharply without need.

qs.q: Which sign imposes a speed limit?
qs.x: The residential zone sign (2) limits speed to 20 km/h; the blue square 50 is only a recommended speed, and signs 1 and 4 set no limit.

qs.q: A driver is prohibited from:
o: Crossing a railway level crossing at a speed exceeding 30 km/h.
Crossing a railway level crossing at a speed below 30 km/h.
Crossing a railway level crossing without the permission of the head of the railway track section in a slow-moving vehicle travelling at less than 8 km/h, or in a tractor towing a harrow.
qs.x: Without the track-section head's permission it is prohibited to cross a railroad crossing in machines slower than 8 km/h or tractors towing harrows.

qs.q: When approaching an intersection, a driver must drive at a speed that:
o: Does not exceed the maximum permitted speed on that section of road.
Allows the driver to stop and yield the right of way to vehicles that have priority.
qs.x: Approaching an intersection, speed must allow stopping to yield to vehicles with priority.

qs.q: A driver is prohibited from increasing speed:
o: If doing so would prevent the driver of a vehicle overtaking them from completing the overtaking manoeuvre.
If doing so is necessary to clear the way for a driver who has stopped to yield the right of way to them.
If doing so is intended to clear an intersection.
qs.x: A driver may not speed up if this prevents the overtaking driver from completing the manoeuvre.

qs.q: A driver must reduce speed:
o: When approaching a vehicle displaying the “Transport of Children” identification sign while children are boarding or alighting.
When an obstruction or hazard to traffic arises.
When approaching a vehicle with flashing blue and red beacons and a special audible warning signal in operation, or a stationary vehicle with flashing blue or blue and red beacons in operation.
In all of the above cases.
qs.x: A driver must reduce speed in all of the listed cases.

qs.q: When must a bus driver switch on the hazard warning lights when towing another motor vehicle?
o: Only on the towing bus, to warn vehicles travelling behind it.
On both the towing bus and the towed vehicle, to ensure maximum visibility.
qs.x: When towing, the hazard lights are switched on on the towed vehicle.

qs.q: Is it mandatory to place a warning triangle at the rear of a towed vehicle if its hazard warning lights are switched on?
o: Yes, both must be used simultaneously.
No, a warning triangle is required only if the hazard warning lights are absent or defective.
qs.x: A warning triangle is required only if the hazard lights are absent or defective.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to drive at an unnecessarily low speed?
o: Yes, if the driver is tired.
No, if doing so obstructs the movement of other vehicles.
Yes, but only when driving through intersections or following signals from a traffic controller.
qs.x: Driving needlessly slowly is prohibited if it obstructs other vehicles.

qs.q: When selecting a speed, a bus driver is prohibited from:
o: Exceeding the speed indicated on the 'Speed Limit' identification sign displayed on the vehicle.
Driving below 60 km/h on any road without a sign specifying a minimum speed.
qs.x: Exceeding the speed on the vehicle's speed-limit sign is prohibited; there is no general ban on driving below 60 km/h.

qs.q: When selecting a speed, a bus driver is prohibited from:
o: Transporting luggage at the maximum permitted speed for that road section if no specific speed limit is stated in the cargo documents.
Exceeding the speed indicated on the 'Speed Limit' identification sign displayed on the vehicle.
qs.x: It is prohibited to exceed the speed shown on the bus's speed-limit sign.

qs.q: While driving, a bus driver is prohibited from:
o: Braking sharply unless necessary to prevent a road traffic accident.
Braking when the vehicle following behind is not keeping a safe distance.
qs.x: Sharp braking is prohibited unless needed to prevent an accident; a tailgater behind is no excuse.

qs.q: Within a built-up area, what is the highest permitted speed that the competent authorities may set by using a 'Maximum Speed Limit' sign?
o: Any speed that is safe for the road section concerned.
qs.x: Within built-up areas authorities may set a limit of at most 80 km/h.

qs.q: Outside built-up areas, what is the highest permitted speed that the competent authorities may set by using a 'Maximum Speed Limit' sign?
o: Any speed that is safe for the road section concerned.
qs.x: Outside built-up areas authorities may set a limit of at most 110 km/h.

qs.q: Within a built-up area, a 'Maximum Speed Limit' sign sets a limit of 80 km/h. What is the maximum permitted speed for a vehicle carrying passengers in an equipped truck body and a vehicle transporting an organized group of children?
qs.x: Vehicles carrying people in an equipped body and organized groups of children may not exceed 60 km/h.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for a bus towing a passenger car?
qs.x: While towing, speed must not exceed 50 km/h.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for a bus transporting an organized group of children within a built-up area?
qs.x: A bus carrying an organized group of children may travel up to 60 km/h in built-up areas.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for a bus transporting an organized group of children outside built-up areas?
qs.x: A bus carrying an organized group of children may not exceed 60 km/h outside built-up areas either.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed outside built-up areas for buses that do not provide suburban, interregional or intercity passenger services?
qs.x: Buses not on suburban, interregional or intercity services may do up to 70 km/h outside built-up areas.

qs.q: A bus driver must select a speed:
o: That enables the driver to maintain full control of the vehicle.
That enables the driver to stop only if another vehicle or an obstruction is visible ahead.
That satisfies both of the above conditions.
qs.x: Speed must keep the vehicle fully under control, not merely allow stopping for an obstacle that is already visible.

qs.q: What must a bus driver do if an obstruction or hazard arises that the driver is able to detect?
o: Take measures to reduce speed, stopping the vehicle if necessary.
Immediately change lanes without reducing speed so as not to disrupt the route schedule.
qs.x: On detecting an obstruction or hazard the driver must reduce speed, stopping if necessary.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to brake sharply?
o: Yes, if the bus is equipped with a modern anti-lock braking system (ABS) and other brake-assist systems.
Yes, in any situation, provided the driver has switched on the hazard warning lights beforehand.
Only when necessary to prevent a road traffic accident.
qs.x: Sharp braking is allowed only to prevent a traffic accident; having ABS changes nothing.

qs.q: If a bus displays a 'Speed Limit' identification sign, is its driver permitted to exceed the speed shown?
o: Yes, but only on a road section where a road sign indicates a higher speed limit.
No, exceeding the speed shown on the identification sign is prohibited.
Yes, when driving on a motorway.
Yes, by up to 20 km/h if necessary to complete an overtaking manoeuvre.
qs.x: With a speed-limit identification sign on the bus, exceeding the stated speed is prohibited.

qs.q: Is the driver of a scheduled-service bus permitted to travel at a very low speed?
o: Yes, provided this does not obstruct other vehicles.
No, because doing so would disrupt the route schedule.
qs.x: Driving very slowly is allowed provided it does not obstruct other vehicles.

qs.q: In residential zones, bus drivers are prohibited from:
o: Driving through the zone without stopping at a destination there.
qs.x: Through traffic is banned in a residential zone, while stopping with the engine running is not specifically prohibited.

qs.q: In residential zones, minibus drivers are prohibited from:

qs.x: Driving lessons are prohibited in a residential zone, which is the prohibition the official answer identifies.

qs.q: Is a bus driver permitted to tow another vehicle using a rigid coupling if there is no driver at the wheel of the towed vehicle?
o: No, because a driver must be at the wheel of the towed vehicle during any type of towing.
Yes, if the design of the rigid coupling ensures that the towed vehicle follows the path of the towing vehicle when travelling in a straight line.
qs.x: With a rigid coupling no driver is needed in the towed vehicle if the coupling keeps it following the towing vehicle's path.

qs.q: When a bus tows another vehicle using a flexible coupling, what is the minimum number of warning devices (flags or panels) that must be attached to make the coupling visible?
o: One for every metre of the coupling.
qs.x: A flexible coupling must carry at least two warning devices (flags or panels) so it is clearly visible.

qs.q: Is it permitted to use a rigid towing coupling of any design or length?
o: No, because the design of the rigid coupling must meet the applicable standards.

qs.x: A rigid coupling must meet the applicable standards; adding flags does not make any design acceptable.

qs.q: Is a bus permitted to tow a vehicle whose windscreen wipers and factory-fitted washers are not working?
o: Yes, except where the towed vehicle is being steered by a driver.
No, in any weather conditions, because a vehicle with defective windscreen wipers may not be moved on the carriageway.
qs.x: A vehicle with faulty wipers may be towed as long as a driver is steering it.

qs.q: Is it permitted to tow a bus whose steering system is not functioning?
o: No, towing is prohibited by any method; a vehicle with a defective steering system may be transported only by recovery vehicle.
qs.x: A bus with defective steering may be towed only by the partial-loading method, with the steered axle lifted.

qs.q: Is a bus with an actual mass of 3 tonnes permitted to tow a passenger car with an actual mass of 1.7 tonnes if the passenger car's braking system is not functioning?
qs.x: A towed vehicle without working brakes may weigh at most half of the towing vehicle (1.5 t here), so 1.7 t is too much.

qs.q: Is a bus with an actual mass of 3 tonnes permitted to tow a passenger car with an actual mass of 1.3 tonnes if the passenger car's braking system is not functioning?
o: Yes, but only with a rigid coupling.
qs.x: 1.3 t is within half the bus's mass (1.5 t), but a car with no brakes may be towed only on a rigid coupling.

qs.q: Which documents must a person providing individual driving instruction carry?
o: A document issued in the prescribed manner authorizing the person to provide driving instruction.
A driving licence valid for the relevant category of vehicle.
qs.x: A person giving individual driving instruction must carry a driving licence for the relevant vehicle category.

qs.q: Is it correct that the number of people carried in buses operating on intercity routes must not exceed the number of fitted seats?
qs.x: On intercity routes the number of people on board must not exceed the number of fitted seats.

qs.q: Is it correct that the number of people carried in buses transporting organized groups of children must not exceed the number of fitted seats?
qs.x: When carrying organised groups of children, the number of people must not exceed the number of seats.

qs.q: When may a bus driver open the passenger doors for boarding or alighting, and when may the bus start moving?
o: The driver may open the doors while approaching a bus stop, once the bus has slowed to a minimum speed, and may start moving when no passengers remain at the stop.
The driver must keep the doors closed until the bus comes to a complete stop, open them only after stopping, and start moving only after the doors are fully closed.
qs.x: Doors may be opened only after the bus has fully stopped, and the bus may move off only once the doors are fully closed.

qs.q: The carriage of passengers is prohibited if:
o: The number of people on a bus operating on a tourist route exceeds the number of fitted seats.
The bus doors are partially open.
qs.x: Carrying passengers is prohibited both when a tourist-route bus exceeds its fitted seats and when the doors are partly open.

qs.q: Organized groups of children must be transported:
o: In a bus displaying the 'Transportation of Children' identification sign.
In a bus displaying the 'Speed Limit' identification sign.
qs.x: Organised groups of children travel in a bus with the 'Transportation of Children' sign; the speed-limit sign is not the required one.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for buses operating interregional and intercity passenger services on all roads outside built-up areas?
qs.x: Interregional and intercity buses may travel at most 90 km/h outside built-up areas.

Yes, provided the speed does not exceed 90 km/h.
qs.x: An intercity bus may exceed 70 km/h outside built-up areas, up to a cap of 90 km/h even on motorways.

qs.q: Are tourist buses permitted to travel at 70 km/h outside built-up areas?
qs.x: A tourist bus may go up to 90 km/h outside built-up areas, so 70 km/h is allowed.

qs.q: Is the driver of the tourist bus permitted to pick up a passenger in the situation shown?
o: Yes, provided this does not obstruct public transport vehicles.
qs.x: The marked stop with the bus sign is for scheduled public transport, so a tourist bus may not pick up a passenger there.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for tourist buses on motorways?
qs.x: Tourist buses are limited to 90 km/h on motorways.

qs.q: On roads marked with this sign, drivers of intercity buses must not exceed:

qs.q: What is the maximum speed permitted for the driver of a suburban bus in this situation?
qs.x: The picture shows a road outside a built-up area, where a suburban bus may go up to 90 km/h.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for buses in areas marked by the 'Residential Zone' and 'End of Residential Zone' signs?
qs.x: Inside a residential zone all vehicles, buses included, are limited to 20 km/h.

qs.q: At what speed may the bus driver continue within the area indicated by this road sign?
o: Not less than 60 km/h and not more than 90 km/h.
Not less than 60 km/h and not more than 70 km/h.
qs.x: The picture shows the end of the built-up area and a 60 km/h minimum-speed sign, with the bus's overall cap at 90 km/h.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for drivers of interregional buses where this sign is displayed?
qs.x: Even on a motorway, as shown by the sign, interregional buses are capped at 90 km/h.

qs.q: When towing a passenger car with a bus, the maximum permitted speed is:
qs.x: While towing a vehicle with a bus the speed limit is 50 km/h.

qs.q: What must a bus driver do if the reversible traffic signal is switched off while driving in a reversible lane?
o: Continue to the nearest intersection and then move to the right of the road marking.
Immediately move to the right of the road marking.
qs.x: If the reversible-lane signal goes off, the driver must immediately move to the right of the marking.

qs.q: Is through traffic by buses permitted in residential zones?
o: Permitted only for residents living there.
qs.x: Through traffic by buses is prohibited in residential zones.

qs.q: 'Organised transport of groups of children' means:
o: The organised transport of three or more children of preschool or school age.
The organised transport of two or more children of preschool or school age by a motor vehicle (excluding public transport vehicles).
qs.x: It means organised carriage of two or more preschool or school-age children in a motor vehicle, other than public transport vehicles.

qs.q: If the carriageway is divided into lanes by road markings, a bus driver is permitted to cross broken lane lines:
o: In heavy traffic when all lanes are occupied.
qs.x: On a marked multi-lane road, broken lines may be crossed only when changing lanes.

qs.q: Is towing with a bus permitted in foggy conditions?
o: Yes, at a speed not exceeding 50 km/h.
qs.x: Towing in fog is allowed, but only at no more than 50 km/h.

qs.q: In this situation, the driver of the bus changing to the right lane:
o: Must not obstruct the passenger car.
Has priority because the driver is completing an overtaking manoeuvre.
Has priority because the bus's right turn indicator is switched on.
qs.x: A driver changing lanes must give way to the car already in that lane, and an indicator gives no priority.

qs.q: Are the actions of the bus driver travelling in the centre of the road consistent with the Road Traffic Rules?
o: Yes, if there are no oncoming vehicles.
qs.x: Driving in the centre of the road breaks the rules, since the vehicle must keep to the right side regardless of oncoming traffic.

qs.q: Must the bus driver yield the right of way to the passenger car?
o: No, the driver is not required to yield.
qs.x: The car is changing into the bus's lane, so the car must yield and the bus going straight need not.

qs.q: Must the bus driver yield the right of way to the truck?
o: Yes, if the truck has begun changing to the right lane.
No, the driver is not required to yield.
qs.x: The truck is signalling right into the bus's lane, so the truck must yield and the bus need not.

qs.q: Is the bus driver permitted to turn right in this situation?
o: Yes, but only if driving a route-service bus.
Yes, any bus driver is permitted.
qs.x: No sign in the picture prohibits a right turn, so any bus driver may make it.

qs.q: In a built-up area, is the driver of a bus with a maximum authorised mass exceeding 3.5 tonnes permitted to change into the third lane along the indicated path and stop?
